  `tests/test_host_acting.py`, `examples/host-explainer/video.yaml`.
- `src/vidgen/actions.py`, `api.py`, `cartoon/directing.py` (`directing_used`), `cartoon/host.py`,

- Docs: `DESIGN.md` (layout, §6.4 api note, §71 intro and gaps, new §71.1, §71.2),

## Step 135 — Voices with feeling, part 1: Kokoro

What was built
- **`emotion:`** on a beat, on `voice:` and on `voices.<name>` (a speaker's default; not inherited
  by named voices, `voices.SPEAKER_FIELDS`): a built-in name or `{like, speed, pitch, gain,
  pauses}`. 13 emotions in `emotions.EMOTIONS` (neutral, happy, excited, sad, angry, worried,
  scared, surprised, calm, doubtful, sleepy, whisper, shout), each a `Prosody` (speed factor,
  pitch in semitones within ±3, gain in dB, pause factor); the table is in CONFIG.md and DESIGN §72.
  `Project.beat_emotion(beat_id)`: the beat's, else its voice's; `None` when unset or neutral.
- **Kokoro applies it** (`KokoroProvider(voice, emotion=...)`): speed = voice speed × factor
  (Kokoro's own control; its timings follow); then `tts/prosody.py`: pauses at `, ; : — . ! ? …`
  followed by a word edited in their middle using Kokoro's punctuation token times (above 1:
  `(f − 1) × max(pause, 0.2 s comma / 0.4 s sentence)` of silence inserted, because Kokoro's comma
  pause is ~0.05 s; below 1: the middle cut), every word and phoneme time moved (`shift_time`), so
  `.align.json`, captions and the viseme track follow the edited audio; gain with a tanh soft
  limiter for boosts; pitch via ffmpeg `asetrate,aresample,atempo` in the MP3 encode (length kept).
  Pauses need word timings: English only.
- **Weighted voice blends**: `voice: af_heart+af_bella:0.6` (0.4 / 0.6; unweighted parts share the
  rest; all weighted: in proportion). Kokoro 0.9.4 supports it: `KPipeline.__call__` accepts a
  `FloatTensor` voice, so `KokoroProvider.voice_for` mixes `load_single_voice` packs by weight once
  per provider. Malformed blends are config errors (`VoiceConfig`, `voice_provider_problems`).
  The `,` blend (Kokoro's equal average) is unchanged.
- **Hash**: `spec()["emotion"] = {name, speed, pitch, gain, pauses}` only with a non-neutral
  emotion; pinned Kokoro, ElevenLabs and OpenRouter keys unchanged (tested). `beat_providers`
  makes one provider per (voice, emotion) for `tts.EMOTION_PROVIDERS` (kokoro) only; other
  providers keep one provider per voice, ignore the emotion and `vidgen validate` warns
  (`tts.emotion_warnings`). A variant whose beat emotions differ gets its own audio folder.
- **Screenplays**: manner words also set the beat's `emotion` (`emotions.EMOTION_WORDS`:
  `cross` → angry, `whispering` → whisper...; also for the narrator); emotion words are no longer
  `# TODO:` manners. `vidgen tts --dry-run` names a beat's emotion.

Real check (Kokoro venv, Python 3.12, kokoro 0.9.4, CPU, 2500 MB cgroup, run alone; script
`scratchpad/s135/real_check.py`, audio left in `scratchpad/s135/`, not committed). Line: "Not a
cloud in the sky, Pip. I checked, and the forecast said sunshine all day." (`af_heart`; median
pitch by autocorrelation, BS.1770 loudness; pauses from the stored word timings):

| emotion | duration | pitch | loudness | comma pause | sentence pause |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neutral | 5.20 s | 202 Hz | -25.7 LUFS | 0.05 s | 0.12 s |
| excited | 4.85 s | 228 Hz (+2.0 st) | -22.7 | 0.03 s | 0.09 s |
| sad | 6.16 s | 185 Hz (-1.5 st) | -28.9 | 0.15 s | 0.35 s |
| whisper | 5.69 s | 189 Hz | -34.7 | 0.09 s | 0.23 s |
| shout | 5.00 s | 232 Hz (+2.4 st) | -20.7 | 0.04 s | 0.10 s |
| sleepy | 7.01 s | 178 Hz | -30.2 | 0.19 s | 0.40 s |
| neutral, `af_heart+af_bella:0.5` | 5.50 s | 196 Hz | -25.3 | 0.05 s | 0.12 s |

Model load 142 s on the first (cold) run, 11 s on the second; then 3-4 s per line. Kokoro's peaks
were 0.3-0.6, so the soft limiter did not act. A first version scaled only Kokoro's own pause
(sad: comma 0.05 → 0.07 s, inaudible), hence the natural-pause floor.

## Step 136 — Voices with feeling, part 2: other providers

What was built
- **One table by name**: `emotions.NamedCues(tag, stability, style, instruction)`,
  `NAMED_CUES` (12 rows, every emotion but neutral) and `named_cues(prosody)`. ElevenLabs and
  OpenRouter models with instructions use the emotion's name only (a mapping's `like`).
- **ElevenLabs `eleven_v3`**: `Project.spoken` puts the tag before the line (`[excited] Hello
  there.`) with `Spoken.inserted` (after the voice sounds, so it comes first); the text sent and
  so the hash change; voice settings unchanged. `readback.compare_beat` now drops bracketed
  audio tags that no written word claims (also fixes v3 voice-sound tags counting as missing
  words).
- **Other ElevenLabs models**: `ElevenLabsProvider(voice, emotion=)` adds the row's stability and
  style changes to `voice_settings` (clamped 0-1); the text is never changed.

  after the voice's own `instructions` (`spec` gains `emotion: {name, instruction}`). Other
  models: `with_prosody` re-encodes the returned MP3 with the emotion's gain (soft-limited),

## Step 137 — Fast drafts (`vidgen render --draft`)

What was built
- `vidgen render --draft` (exclusive with `--preview`) and MCP `render` `draft: true` (which
  drops the default `preview`): a render to check timing and staging, about 8 fps at 240 px on
  the shorter side, without decoration. Config `draft: {width, height, fps}` (each optional;
  width and height together, even); default from the format's shape: 426x240 (16:9), 240x426
  (9:16), 240x240 (1:1), 320x240 (4:3), never larger nor faster than `format`.
- Never mixed: `Project.draft` (set by `Project.load(draft=True)`, kept by `without_overlays`)
  makes `render_dir` `build/draft[_<variant>][_bare]`, `render_format` the draft's and every
  output name `<output>[_<variant>]_draft` (MP4, SRT, chapter list, thumbnail, export stem),
  whatever `preview` the path methods get; a preview made at the draft's exact size and rate is
  still not reused (tested). The worker takes `--quality draft`; scene timings gain
  `render.draft: true`, combined timings `draft: true`, `render --json` `draft`. The `draft` key is
  left out of the scene fingerprint.
- `NarratedScene.is_draft` (from the project, set in `__init__` before the host is built). In a
  draft: no idle motion (stage characters and the host: `stop_idle`); the wind sways and trails
  nothing (`StageWind` without props or characters, no updater; its `Wind` is kept so balloons
  and blown props drift as in the video); no shadows, motion effects, puddles, settling snow,
  fog, lightning bolt or flash; particle fields are empty and never move
  (`ParticleField(drawn=False)`; their start / fade / end stay, so the rain bed, storms and
  thunder are unchanged); the light is flat (`StageLight(flat=True)`: the camera is not wrapped,
  no flashes, the changes keep their times, stars and window skies still follow the grade).
  Splashing steps now read `Stage._puddles_from` (the puddle rains' starts) instead of the drawn
  puddles, so a draft keeps them (same times as before otherwise).
- Kept: every beat, action, position, lip sync (at 8 fps), effect symbols, overlays, cards,
  living props, birds, water, rainbows and every sound.

Measured (copies of the examples in the scratchpad, worker alone per scene, `--no-audio`
word-count timing, under the 1500 MB cap, two alternating runs; `measure_draft.py` in the
scratchpad)
| scene | preview (640x360 @ 15) | draft (426x240 @ 8) | speed-up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cartoon-rain-check` `storm` (23.4 s: wind, rain with puddles, a light change, blown umbrella) | 21.20 / 21.78 s wall (CPU 22.6 / 23.2 s) | 8.01 / 8.21 s (CPU 8.4 / 8.6 s) | ×2.65 |
| `cartoon-muffin-mystery` `morning` (31.2 s indoors, 3 characters, walks, effects) | 25.34 / 25.39 s (CPU 26.3 / 26.4 s) | 12.68 / 12.80 s (CPU 13.1 s) | ×2.0 |
Peak memory of the worker processes: 0.28 GB (rain-check), 0.25 GB (muffin), the same at both
qualities. Beat starts: the draft's fall on whole 1/8 s frames, the preview's on 1/15 s ones
(`narrate` waits relative to each beat's start), so they drift apart by up to 0.15 s (storm, 7
beats) and 0.18 s (morning, 8 beats); sound effects (20 / 25) and ambience beds are the same
apart from that. Stills at 10 s (storm) and 20 s (morning) checked by eye: same places and
poses, no rain / puddles / shadows, ungraded colours, captions and the sweat symbol kept.

## Step 138 — Animatic (`vidgen animatic`)

What was built
- `vidgen animatic [PROJECT] [--variant NAME] [--no-audio] [--captions | --no-captions]
  [--jobs N|auto] [--output-dir DIR] [--json]` and the MCP tool `animatic` (`captions`: null /
  true / false): `<output>[_<variant>]_animatic.mp4` in the `output/` folder, the storyboard's
  preview stills held in time with the narration, with the video's audio and captions, made by
  ffmpeg alone (no Manim) once the stills are current.
- Stills: `make_animatic` reuses every scene whose stills are current
  (`storyboard.stills_current(..., None)`: any count per beat, so `storyboard --per-beat N` stills
  are used too) and renders the others with `render_scenes(..., frames=1)`, the storyboard's own
  call; nothing else renders. With every scene current, `render_scenes` is not called at all (it
  would load the extensions once more to check scenes that were checked when rendered).
- Timing (pure `hold_plan`): each still from its time in the video until the next still's
  (beat-end stills from their beat's end, mid-action stills from half-way through their action),
  rounded to frames; a scene's first still from the scene's start, the video's first from 0, the
  last to the end; a still at or after the next scene's start (overlapping scenes) is dropped.
  Scene starts and length come from the combined timings, so beat overlaps and word-count timing
  need nothing extra.
- Audio: decided "mixed like the final": `render/pipeline.prepare_join` (split out of
  `join_scenes`, which now calls it then `ff.join`) writes the padded scene WAVs, the effects track
  and the mix (music, ambience, normalisation) into `build/preview[_<variant>]/animatic/audio/`.
- Captions (pure `with_captions`, `draw_captions`): the SRT's cues (`pipeline.video_cues`, which
  `render_project` now also uses for the SRT) cut the holds; each piece gets the texts spoken
  then (overlapping cues stacked), drawn with Pillow (bold, 0.055 of the shorter side, white on a
  dark plate near the bottom). Default on unless the video has a `captions` overlay.
- Encoding: `ff.join_stills` (concat demuxer with `duration` lines via
  `write_concat_list(..., durations)`, `fps` + `tpad` + `-frames:v` for exactly
  `round(duration × fps)` frames, x264 `-tune stillimage`); `ff.join`'s audio inputs and its
  partial-file replace are now shared helpers (`_audio_inputs`, `_write_video`).

Measured (copy of `examples/cartoon-music-box` in the scratchpad: 51.1 s, 2 stage scenes, no
MP3s, 21 stills, 640x360 @ 15, under the 1500 MB cap)
| run | time |
| --- | --- |
| no stills yet (`--jobs auto` chose 1): both scenes rendered (15.5 + 19.3 s worker) | 42.3 s |
| stills current, captions off (default: the example has a `captions` overlay) | 7.0 / 7.2 s (9.1 s wall with Python start) |
| stills current, `--captions` | 7.4 / 7.5 s |
| stills current, `--no-audio` | 3.7 s |
Profile of a cached run: x264 2.9 s (767 frames), mix 2.7 s (1.1 s the `bright` bed, 1.6 s
limiter / loudness), extensions 1.0 s. A tiled strip of the result was checked by eye (stills
change at beat ends and mid-actions, drawn captions under the overlay's).

Decisions / deviations
- Still timing as asked (held from its time until the next still's): the picture is the latest
  captured moment, so a beat-end still shows through the following beat, and a bullet revealed
  during a beat appears at that beat's end. Showing each still from the previous still's time
  instead (a beat's picture during the beat) is a one-line change in `hold_plan` if wanted.
- No crossfade between stills or scenes: the concat demuxer cannot blend; a blend would need the
  `xfade` graph `ff.join` uses, re-encoding per still pair.
- Captions with Pillow, not ffmpeg's `subtitles` filter (needs libass, absent from some Windows
  builds); drawn per still and caption text, so a cue change costs one PNG.
- Preview format only (what `vidgen storyboard` makes by default); no `--final`.

## Step 138 follow-up — animatic still timing per beat, test_extending_example

What changed
- Animatic timing (`animatic.hold_plan`): each still is now shown up to its own capture time,
  from the time of the scene's still before it. Within a beat the stills split the beat's time
  in order (a mid-action still from the beat's start or the still before it, up to half-way
  through its action) and the beat-end still covers the rest until the beat's end, so what a beat
  reveals is on screen during that beat (before, a beat-end still showed through the FOLLOWING
  beat). A scene's first still from the scene's start, the video's first from 0; a scene's last
  still stays through the scene's tail until the next scene; in overlapping scenes a still is cut
  at the next scene's start and one that would start at or after it is dropped; zero-frame holds
  dropped. No beat start times are needed: a beat starts where the previous still was captured.
  Replaces the "Decisions" note of Step 138 on still timing.
- `test_sfx.py::test_extending_example` (failing since d33ebb3, Step 134; checked in a scratchpad
  worktree: passes at 874f796, fails at d33ebb3): Step 134 inserted the automatic-directing /
  `reveal_steps` paragraph and its snippet between the "Sound effects" text of docs/EXTENDING.md
  and its `countdown` example, so the test's regex (first ```python block after "**Sound
  effects**") took the `reveal_steps` snippet. Fixed in the docs (the out-of-date part): the
  `countdown` example moved back right after the Sound effects text, before the
  automatic-directing paragraph. Code unchanged.

## Step 139 — Ready-made sets, part 1: outdoors

What was built
- Built-in sets: `src/vidgen/data/sets/outdoors.yaml` (package data, `data/sets/*` in
  pyproject) holds `sets:` `city_street`, `park`, `beach`, `forest`, `snowy_hills` in the format
  of a project's sets. `includes.builtin_sets()` returns a copy (read once). `expand_sets` uses the
  project's `sets:` first, else the built-in set, with the Step 101 merge rules unchanged (scene
  params win, image / generate / background one choice, marks merge, lists add, name-matched
  entries change, `[]` clears). A built-in set's values keep the scene's locations for problems
  (no `sets.NAME` origin, the project has none). `set_reference_problems` checks both and lists

## Step 141 — Flag badly spoken words

What was built
- **Word flags** (`src/vidgen/speech_flags.py`, DESIGN §78): from each beat's transcript (word
  times, and faster-whisper's per-word probability, now kept) and its comparison with the text,
  `flag_words` lists the words to listen to. Unclear: probability below 0.5, a pause over 0.5 s
  before a word inside a sentence (not after punctuation in the text or the transcript, not where
  a voice sound sits), or a difference with the text about a term or covering 2+ words. Doubtful:
  probability below 0.75, or one ordinary word heard differently with confidence. A difference
  and the probability / pause of its words are one flag. Each flag: scene, beat, word heard,
  written word, level, reasons (`low_probability`, `gap`, `mismatch`), time and end in the MP3,
  time in the video (from the last render: preview, else final; `null` before one), probability,
  gap, detail and a fix (respell the pronunciation entry; add an entry with a respelling for a
  name / acronym / number; another voice, speed or emotion, or a respelling, for other words; a
  comma, speed, emotion or rephrasing for a pause). Thresholds: `lint.rules.unclear_speech`
  (`min_probability`, `doubtful_probability`, `max_gap`).
- **`vidgen readback`** always flags: report section "words to check: N unclear, M doubtful
  (...)" with `fix:` lines; JSON `flag_thresholds`, `summary.unclear` / `doubtful`, each beat's
  `flags`.
- **`vidgen lint --readback`**: lint rule `unclear_speech` (default warning, doubtful words info),
  run only when asked (`--readback`, or `--rule unclear_speech`); it transcribes the selected
  scenes' beats first as `vidgen readback` does (cache reused, progress on stderr). One finding
  per flag at the beat's start + the word's time. MCP `lint` got `readback` and `confirm_cost`
  (asked for a paid `stt.provider`, like MCP `readback`).
- **Decoding with ffmpeg**: `stt.faster_whisper.load_audio` now decodes with the ffmpeg
  executable (`render.ffmpeg.decode_mono`, f32le mono 16 kHz) instead of PyAV
  (`sfx.decode_audio`, unchanged, still used elsewhere).
- Transcript cache: words `[text, start, end, probability]` (3-element words of older files still
  load); a cached faster-whisper transcript without probabilities is transcribed again (local,
  free); ElevenLabs transcripts (no probabilities) are kept. `CACHE_VERSION` stays 1.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/speech_flags.py`, `tests/test_speech_flags.py`.
- `src/vidgen/stt/__init__.py` (`TranscriptWord.probability`, `word_probabilities`,
  `has_probabilities`, JSON), `stt/faster_whisper.py` (probability, ffmpeg decoding),
  `render/ffmpeg.py` (`decode_mono`), `readback.py` (alignment kept on `BeatReadback` /
  `Edit`, flags in `run_readback`, `flag_lines`, cache refresh; helpers made public:
  `term_core`, `written_owner`, `entries_by_word`, `entry_says`, `EDGE_CHARS`), `config.py`
  (`UnclearSpeechRule`, `LintRules.unclear_speech`, `LINT_RULES` / `RuleName`),
  `lint/readback_rule.py` (rule), `lint/rules.py` (`SceneContext.speech_flags`), `lint/run.py`
  (`lint_project(readback=, log=)`, `_speech_flags`), `cli.py` (`lint --readback`, help texts),

## Step 142 — Drawing style switch (`drawing:`)

What was built
- Config `drawing: {outline: thin | normal | bold, shading: flat | soft, texture: none | paper |
  storybook, seed}` (`DrawingConfig`, every key optional) at the top level (variants change it as
  any key) and as the `stage` param `drawing` (wins key by key). The name `drawing` was chosen
  over the task's placeholder `cartoon_style_draw`; `cartoon_style` (Step 77, prompt words) is
  untouched.
- `src/vidgen/cartoon/drawing_style.py`: `DrawingStyle` / `resolve_drawing` (merge, defaults
  normal / flat / none / 0, `for_draft`), `OUTLINE_FACTORS` (0.6 / 1 / 1.7), `soft_stops`,
  `TEXTURES` + `texture_shade` (cached seeded H×W×4 uint16 multiplier: per-pixel grain, bicubic
  blotches, storybook's darker corners) + `apply_texture`, `attach_texture`, `mark_shaded`,
  `mark_outlined`, `style_camera`.
- Applied as Manim draws, like the light (Step 97), never to the mobjects: `style_camera` wraps
  the camera's `apply_stroke` (scales `cairo_line_width_multiple` per stroke: one place for every
  stroke of a stage: characters, props, set, effect symbols, motion effects, bubbles; a thinned
  stroke stays ≥ 1 px unless thinner) and `apply_fill` (a `soft` vertical Cairo gradient on
  members marked shaded: the stage marks every character and prop, a host its character).
  `attach_texture` wraps the renderer's `add_frame` between the overlay layer and the colour
  fade: the grain covers everything the stage draws (bubbles too) and the fade colour, never
  overlays or burned-in captions. Not a mobject, so no change to Manim's static image (Step 87).
- `NarratedScene`: `uses_drawing_style` (class attribute; `stage` True), `drawing_settings()`
  (`stage` adds its param), `_apply_drawing_style()` in `__init__` after `_build_host`, before
  `_attach_color_fade`; `self.drawing`. A host on other scene types: outline and shading on its
  figure (marked), no texture. Drafts: outline kept, shading and texture dropped.
- Gallery still `docs/gallery/media/drawing_styles.png` (52 KB, 48 colours): `park` in six styles
  (default, thin, bold, soft, paper, bold + soft + storybook), each a quarter of the preview still
  around the left character; made by `tools/make_sets_gallery.py --styles --colors 48 park` (new
  options `--styles`, `--colors`). Checked by eye, and a host-explainer copy with a styled host.

Default unchanged
- A plain style installs nothing (tests check the camera and renderer are not wrapped). Frames
  compared with HEAD 5a11a8c (worktree in the scratchpad, `PYTHONPATH` to its `src`; scratchpad
  `s142/frame_digest.py`, 320x180 @ 5 fps, no audio): `cartoon-rain-check` `storm` 117 frames
  and `host-explainer` `grow` 75 frames, SHA-256 of every frame identical (3bbe96e677d07055,
  ae9a388ed28c08e9). The generator's pinned digests (Steps 113–125) are untouched (the drawings do
  not change); `test_cartoon_outfits` passes.

Render cost (worker alone, `--no-audio`, a copy of `cartoon-rain-check` with a variant per style,
scene `storm` 23.4 s; scratchpad `s142/measure_styles.py`)
| style | 640x360 @ 15 (2 runs) | 1280x720 @ 30 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain | 20.65 / 21.39 / 22.28 s | 56.33 / 56.63 s |
| thin | 21.12 / 22.61 s | |
| bold | 21.38 / 22.15 s | 56.78 s |
| soft | 22.29 / 22.19 s | 58.58 s |
| paper | 21.85 s (22.49 / 23.77 before the faster multiply) | 62.18 s (68.81 before) |
| storybook | 21.84 s (22.99 / 23.03 before) | |
| bold + soft + storybook | 23.78 s (24.57 / 25.50 before) | 64.95 s (72.31 before) |
The texture multiply on all four channels at once takes 1.9 ms a 1280x720 frame (8.0 ms at
1080p; 14.5 ms with the first version on a colour slice); the rest of a textured frame's cost is
H.264 encoding the grain. Preview runs vary by ±1 s between runs.

Decisions / deviations
- Texture placement: under overlays (so captions, lower thirds and watermarks stay crisp), over
  speech bubbles (they are scene mobjects; leaving them out would need a mobject in the draw
  order, which redraws the full-frame grain every frame and which the stage's depth ordering can
  pass). Grain is in screen space: it does not pan with the camera.
- "Outline weight scales every cartoon stroke" is done by stroke width at draw time on the stage's
  camera, so later additions (effects, rain rings, motion effects) need no marking; overlays draw
  with their own camera and are unaffected.
- `soft` shading is a gradient over each member's own height (light from above), not a shape
  drawn inside it: the silhouette and outline stay Manim's path.
- Drafts keep the outline (it changes how a frame reads, not what moves) and drop the rest.
- Searched first: no stroke-width or texture code existed beyond `scale_strokes` (build-time, per
  object; kept for sizes) and `StageLight`'s camera wrapper (the pattern reused).

## Step 143 — Dubbing

What was built
- **`dub:`** on `voice:` and on every `voices:` entry (`dict[LanguageTag, str | DubVoice] | None`):
  the voice in another language, as the provider's voice (Kokoro / OpenRouter `voice`, ElevenLabs
  `voice_id`) or a mapping of the keys a named voice may set (`{voice: pm_alex, speed: 0.9}`). The
  most specific tag matching the video's `language` wins (`pt-BR` before `pt`).
- **Automatic dubbing** (`src/vidgen/dubbing.py`, no manim, `voice_dubs(config)`): a named voice
  that keeps the base voice follows the base voice's dub; a Kokoro voice of another language
  (no `lang` written) gets a Kokoro voice of the video's language of the same kind (`f` / `m`,
  the name's second letter), the least used so far (given dubs counted first), best grade on a
  tie, never `*_santa`; one source voice gets one target everywhere; a language without the kind
  (French: only `ff_siwis`) takes another and says so. ElevenLabs and OpenRouter voices are kept.
- **Applied in `voices.resolve_voice`** (`_merge_voice`, `DUB_FIELDS`): the dubbed voice is the
  effective voice, so the variant's `audio/<variant>/`, hashes, `vidgen tts`, viseme tracks (lip
  sync from that language's audio and phonemes) and every timing (VideoPlan, overlaps,
  interrupts) follow without other changes. A base voice without a dub resolves to the same
  object as before.
- **Checks**: config problems for dub keys of another provider and malformed blends
  (`_dub_problems`); `vidgen validate` warnings (`dubbing.dub_warnings`) for voices that differ in
  their language but share one voice in the dubbed one (a blend suggested for Kokoro) and for a
  kind not kept; a `dub [pt]: default bf_emma -> pf_dora+bf_emma:0.4 (given), ...` line under
  the language line. `kokoro_voices.voice_warnings` no longer warns about a blend's later voices
  being of another language (the first gives the language).
- **`--all-languages`** on `vidgen tts`, `render` and `lint` (`cli.each_language`,
  `dubbing.language_variants`): the base config, then every variant whose `language` differs
  from it, in turn; a `== pt (pt-BR) ==` heading before each; worst exit code; `--json` an
  envelope with `languages: [documents]`; refused with `--variant`. MCP `render` / `lint` take
  `all_languages`.
- **Example**: `examples/cartoon-music-box` variant `pt` (pt-BR, `translations/pt.yaml`, 12 texts
  written by hand, `[gasp]` / `[laugh]` and `*nada*` kept); narrator `dub: {pt:
  pf_dora+bf_emma:0.4}` and Gus `dub: {pt: pm_santa}` given, Fen (`pf_dora`) and Bram (`pm_alex`)
  automatic, so the four speakers stay distinct. `video.yaml` 4.5 KB.

## Step 145 — Optional extra and SoundFont

What was built
- **Extra `music`** (`pyproject.toml`): `symusic==0.5.9` (exact; 0.6.0's SoundFont render fails).
  `src/vidgen/synth.py` (new, Step 146 extends it): `INSTALL_COMMAND`, `SYMUSIC_VERSION`,
  `symusic_version()`, `symusic_status()` and `require_symusic()`, which imports symusic or raises
  `VidgenError` naming `pip install "schu-video-generator[music]"` (also when another version is
  installed).
- **SoundFont** (`src/vidgen/soundfont.py`, new): GeneralUser GS 2.0.3 constants (URL, 32,319,396
  bytes, sha256, licence line, `CREDIT`); `cache_dir()` (`VIDGEN_CACHE_DIR`, else
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\vidgen`, `~/Library/Caches/vidgen`, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/vidgen` / `~/.cache/vidgen`),
  `default_path()` (`soundfonts/GeneralUser-GS.sf2`); `fetch(force, url, progress)` streams to a
  `mkstemp` file next to the target, hashes while writing, compares size and SHA-256, then
  `fileio.replace_file`; the temp file is removed on any failure. `resolve(setting, root,
  download)` gives the override or the checked cached file (hashed once per process, then
  remembered by size + mtime), downloading when missing. `info()` for the CLI;
  `soundfont_problems()` for `vidgen validate`.
- **`httpapi.stream_get(url, write, service, timeout, max_bytes)`**: a streaming GET (the existing
  `get` reads the whole body into memory); HTTP statuses and network errors become `VidgenError`.
- **Config** `soundfont: PATH` (top level, `VideoConfig.soundfont`): an SF2/SF3 file relative to
  the project; `vidgen validate` reports a missing file or one without a RIFF `sfbk` header or
  `.sf2` / `.sf3` suffix. In `PATH_KEYS` (confined under `vidgen mcp`); excluded from scene
  fingerprints (audio only).
- **CLI** `vidgen soundfont fetch [--force]` / `vidgen soundfont info [PROJECT]` (path, origin,
  size, sha256, check, licence line, suggested credit, symusic state).
- **Errors**: offline → "cannot download the GeneralUser GS 2.0.3 SoundFont (cannot reach GitHub
  ...); connect to the internet and run `vidgen soundfont fetch`, or download an SF2 / SF3 SoundFont
  yourself (GeneralUser GS: <home page>) and set `soundfont: PATH` in video.yaml"; mismatch → both
  sizes / hashes, "may have changed upstream", the same `soundfont: PATH` hint; a changed cached
  file → the same plus `vidgen soundfont fetch --force`.

## Step 146 — Score and renderer

What was built
- **`src/vidgen/score.py`** (new, pure; DESIGN.md §82): frozen dataclasses `Score(tempo, parts,
  time_signature=(4, 4), key="C major", sections=(), length=None)`, `Part(name, notes, program=0,
  drums=False, volume=0.0, pan=0.0, reverb=0.2)`, `Note(start, length, pitch, velocity=90)`,
  `Section(name, start, tempo=None)`; checked on creation (`VidgenError` "score: ..."). A beat is a
  quarter note; `bar_beats`, `length_beats` (default: last note's end rounded up to a bar),
  `length_seconds`, `tempo_changes()`, `seconds_at(beat)`, `key_signature()` (sharps, minor),
  `tonic`, `fingerprint()`. `to_symusic(score, parts, controls)` and `write_midi(score, path)`
  (ticks 480 per beat, tempo changes, time / key signature, section markers, CC 7 / 10 / 91;
  `midi_volume`, `midi_pan`).
- **`src/vidgen/synth.py`** (extended): `render_score(score, soundfont, cache_dir)` renders each part
  alone with symusic (48 kHz, stereo), `mix_parts` mixes in float64: volume, `pan_gains`
  (constant power), a per-part send to one reverb (`reverb_impulse()`: seeded noise per channel,
  5 kHz low-pass, 12 ms pre-delay, RT60 1.6 s, 2 s, unit energy; `convolve`: overlap-add FFT),
  `TAIL_SECONDS` 3 s, 20 ms end fade, `MUSIC_LEVEL` (−28 LUFS) and `mix.limit` only above
  `TRUE_PEAK_CEILING` (−1 dBTP). Cache `cache_dir/score-<render_key>.wav` (16-bit; the result is
  always the 16-bit value, so cached = fresh); `render_key` = score fingerprint + symusic version
  + SoundFont SHA-256 + `RENDERER_VERSION` + rate.
- **`soundfont.content_sha256(path)`**: the default file's known hash once checked, others hashed
  once per process (size + mtime).
- **Music pipeline**: `music.SCORES` (name → Score) is the internal hook; `music.source_kind`
  (bed / score / file); `Source(cue, root, soundfont, cache_dir)` plays a score like a music file
  (start, loop with the crossfade seam, fades, ducking, scene volumes unchanged);
  `mix.plan_music` passes `config.soundfont` and `build/music/`; summaries say `kind: score`;
  `config_problems` accepts score names.
- `score.py`, `synth.py`, `soundfont.py` added to `fingerprint.NOT_RENDER_INPUTS` (audio only).
- **Credit fix (Step 145)**: the GeneralUser GS credit names its author as its licence / README
  suggest: `soundfont.AUTHOR`, `CREDIT` = "Music rendered with the GeneralUser GS SoundFont by
  S. Christian Collins (https://www.schristiancollins.com/generaluser)." in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES,
  CONFIG.md, README, `vidgen soundfont info` (the "no personal names" rule protects the owner,
  not third-party authors; coordinator's instruction).
- **Test isolation fix**: `tests/test_render.py::test_ffmpeg_missing` loads the built-in scenes
  (manim, click) before patching `sys.platform` to `win32`; it now passes when the file runs alone.

- Score sources are reached only through `music.SCORES` for now (the brief: a minimal internal

## Step 147 — Composer and moods

What was built
- **`src/vidgen/composer.py`** (new, pure, seeded; DESIGN.md §83): `compose_piece(mood, key, tempo,
  instruments, seed=1, bars) -> Piece` and `compose(...) -> Score`. Eight `MOODS` (calm, focused,
  curious, upbeat for explainers; playful, sleepy, tense, triumphant for cartoons), each with key,
  tempo, meter (sleepy 3/4), default bars (16; playful 24), A and B / C progressions as 4-bar
  question (ends on V) / answer (ends on I) pairs in Roman numerals, melody range, rhythm cells,
  cadence cells, a last bar, articulation, chord / bass / drum patterns, default parts with volume,
  pan and reverb, and a fallback bed. Form A A B A (C in every second block); the last bar becomes
  I–V7 so the piece loops. Melody: per-letter motifs (rhythm cells + a shape) varied on return,
  chord tones on the first note of a bar and on strong beats, scale steps between them, never the
  same bar twice in a row. Accompaniment with voice-led voicings; patterns pad / block / arpeggio
  / broken / oompah / ostinato / strum; bass sustain / half / root_fifth / walking / pulse / pop;
  7 drum patterns with phrase-end fills and section cymbals. `parse_chord`, `parse_key`,
  `resolve_voices`, `settings_problems`, `describe`, `mood_entries`, `instrument_entries`.
- **Instruments**: 42 friendly names → GM programs (range + words) and 5 kits (`drums`,
  `room_drums`, `jazz_drums`, `soft_drums`, `orchestral_drums`).
- **Config**: `MusicCue.compose` (`ComposeConfig {mood, key, tempo, instruments, seed, bars}`,
  `compose: playful` short form; `ComposeInstrument {instrument, volume, pan, reverb}`); a cue
  needs exactly one of `source` / `compose`; `MusicCue.label`. Beds and files unchanged.
- **Music source**: `music.source_kind(cue)` (`composed` / `bed` / `file`), `composed_score`,
  `fallback_bed`; `Source` plays composed music as a seamless loop (the 3 s render tail added onto
  the piece's start; `start` wraps; `loop: false` plays once with the tail); without symusic
  0.5.9 it plays the mood's bed and logs a warning naming the install command. The mix summary
  reads `kind`/`source` from the `Source` (`composed`, `compose: <mood>`; a fallback says
  `kind: bed`, `compose: sleepy (bed lullaby: no music extra)`).
- **`Score.balance`** (new, default false) and `synth.BALANCE_LEVEL`: `mix_parts` first sets each
  part to −28 LUFS, then applies its volume. The composer sets it.
- **CLI**: `vidgen list-music` adds the moods (described in words from their parameters) and the
  instruments (JSON: `moods`, `instruments`, `symusic`); new `vidgen music preview [PROJECT]
  [--mood M] [--seed S] [--bars N] [--key K] [--tempo T] [--out DIR]` writes
  `<mood>-seed<S>.wav` and `.mid` and prints parts, chords per phrase, loudness and peak.
- `score.key_signature(key)` and `score.tonic_pitch_class(name)` moved out of `Score` (its methods
  call them).

## Step 148 — Music that follows the video

What was built
- **`src/vidgen/musicfit.py`** (new; DESIGN.md §84): a `compose:` cue without `bars` is composed
  in `mix.plan_music` for the combined timings. `cue_inputs` (config + timings → `Slot`s per
  scene at its start or mid-transition, reveal times, `Pause`s), `plan_sections` (pure: whole
  bars per scene at the tempo nearest the mood's within `TEMPO_LIMIT` ±8 %; beyond it a *hold*,
  the last bar slowing into a held chord; a scene shorter than one bar joins the next; the last
  section closes with a ritardando and the tonic held 1.3 beats per beat), `TempoMap`,
  `fit_music` (pure: one `compose_piece` per run of equal settings, swells, pauses, score sections
  carrying every tempo change), `FittedMusic.summary` / `closing_seconds`, `sting_score`,
  `composed_stings`, `Settings`, `cue_settings`, `scene_settings`, `is_fitted`.
- **Composer**: `compose_piece(..., ending="loop" | "cadence" | "open")`; non-looping pieces take
  any bar count (whole phrases, then a tag repeating an answer's last bars); `_Bar.closing` (held
  tonic in melody / chords / bass, one kick + cymbal); a cadence puts V7 before the last I when
  needed. Looping pieces are unchanged (Step 147's tests pass unchanged).
- **Config**: `SceneMusic` gains `mood`, `key`, `tempo`, `instruments`, `seed` (`compose_keys`,
  `instrument_settings`), checked by `VideoConfig._scene_compose_problems` (only under a fitted
  cue; must compose); `BeatConfig.music_pause: bool | None`; `ComposeConfig.bars` now means "a
  looping piece of this length" (default none: fitted).
- **Mix**: `Source(..., fitted=score)` plays once from the cue's start; `Placement.fit` → the
  cue's summary gains `fit {sections, swells, pauses, closing}`; the fade-out never starts before
  the closing chord; `music.cue_scene_range`.
- **Stings**: `join_scenes` calls `musicfit.composed_stings` and passes the result to
  `sfx.write_track(..., replaced)` (`sfx.placed(..., audio)`): a built-in sting under composed
  music (with the extra) is a 1-2 bar phrase in the scene's key, tempo and instruments, at the
  built-in sting's loudness; `gain`, `at` and ducking unchanged.
- Fingerprints: `musicfit.py` in `NOT_RENDER_INPUTS`; a beat's `music_pause` left out.

Files
- New: `src/vidgen/musicfit.py`, `tests/test_musicfit.py`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/composer.py`, `config.py`, `music.py`, `mix.py`, `sfx.py`,
  `render/pipeline.py`, `render/fingerprint.py`, `docs/CONFIG.md` (scene `music`, beat

Public interfaces added/changed (`vidgen.api` unchanged)
- Config: scene `music: {mood, key, tempo, instruments, seed}`, beat `music_pause`; a `compose:`
  cue without `bars` is now fitted to the video instead of looping the mood's 16/24 bars.

- Mix summary (`timings.json` `mix.music[]`) gains `fit` for fitted cues.

Decisions / deviations
- `bars` decides: given, the Step 147 loop; absent, the fitted piece (no new key). `start` and
  `loop` do not apply to a fitted piece.
- A scene's compose settings apply to that scene only (like its `volume`); another mood starts
  from its defaults with the cue's seed.
- Beyond ±8 %: a hold (ritardando into a held chord at the scene change), not a bridge.
- Scene changes are taken at the scene's start plus half its transition's overlap.
- Automatic pauses, conservative: before a `card` scene (not the cue's first) until its first
  line ends; before the cue's last line when it has ≤ 8 words and its scene has a line before
  it, the closing chord then struck as the line ends (a *button*, ≥ 0.3 s left; under 0.8 s in
  4/4 it runs past the cue end and is cut). `music_pause: false` turns either off.
- Reveal moments come from the config (type `reveal_steps` via `layout.distribute`, as host
  directing; written `reveal`; `sting_reveal` events), not from the scenes' renders, so cached
  renders keep working. `_type_reveal_beats` calls `extensions.load_builtins()`.
- Stings use the nominal tempo of the scene's settings, not the fitted section's.
- Multi-mood scores export one key / time signature to MIDI (the first); the audio is right.
- The swell's held note avoids pitches the part strikes on that beat (a harp re-striking the
  same string).
- Searched first: nothing planned bars from timings; reused `layout.distribute`, `reveal_steps`,
  `composer` internals (`_pitches`, `_voicing`, `fit_range`), `sfx.stereo`, `loudness`.

## Fix — code scenes: colour code before wrapping, wrap at token boundaries

Found in a Free Pascal short (9:16): `code` / `code_walkthrough` wrapped long lines first and then
let Manim's `Code` lex the wrapped text, so every piece was lexed as its own line. A `//` comment's
continuation (`model's sampling defaults`) became a string literal at the apostrophe, and
`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` was hard-cut (`...-Instr` / `uct`) because the breaker saw no space.
- `scenes/code.py`: `lex_code` lexes the whole text with Pygments into runs per source line;
  `wrap_runs` (replaces `wrap_code`) breaks the run stream (spaces and `,`/`;` outside strings,
  opening brackets outside strings and comments, spaces inside strings, then `/ - . _` inside a
  word, then hard), continuation pieces keep their token types; `paint_code` colours the glyphs of
  a `Code` built with `language="text"` from those runs (`token_colors` reads the Pygments style
  as Manim does). `lexer_name` is the language choice both scenes had inline.
  `code_walkthrough` lexes the whole file before taking the `excerpt`. Groups (source line ->
  rows) are unchanged, so highlights, `focus`, actions, `line<N>` / `lines:<a-b>` targets and the
  line numbers (first piece only) still address source lines.
- Second symptom (a faint "weights" behind "One reply" at 26–30 s of the preview): a vidgen bug.
  `CodeWalkthrough._go` faded the old note out and the new one in at the same time; in the bottom
  bar they share one place, so both were half visible for the whole change. Now the old note
  fades out in the first half (`pie.window(0, 0.5)`) and the new one in the second half.
- `mono_metrics` builds its sample under `text_canvas` (it failed at a 90x160 test canvas when it
  ran first in a process).
- A word longer than a continuation line (here 26 characters after a 6-space hanging indent in
  ~30 columns) is still cut, now after `-` or `/`.
- Docs: `docs/CONFIG.md` (`code` wrapping, walkthrough notes), `DESIGN.md` (both code sections).

How to test: `-m "not render" tests/test_regions.py` (31), `tests/test_code_walkthrough.py`
(45 incl. render), `tests/test_regions.py` (48 incl. render), `-k code tests/test_builtin_scenes.py
tests/test_review4.py` (18), `tests/test_review2.py -k walkthrough` (1), `tests/test_presets.py -k
"contrast_lint_with_every_preset and (light or warm)"` (2), `test_docs.py` (60), `test_guide.py` (51).

  `TILE_SYMBOLS`, `STANDABLE`, `MAX_COLUMNS` 400, `MAX_ROWS` 40) and `world.py` (`Body`,
  `Placing`, `World`, `place_bodies`, `CHARACTER_TILES` 2). Tile units, row 0 at the bottom.
- **Map syntax**: `.`/space air, `#` ground, `=` platform, `~` cloud, `|` ladder, a letter a spot
  (stands on the first tile below it). Errors name `map row R, column C` from the top left.
- **Stage** (`scenes/stage.py`): `level: {map, spots, colors}` (`StageLevel`, parsed once per
  text by `_parsed_level`); default `size` 0.25 on a level; spots are marks; refused with a level:
  `width`, `room`, `water`, any `depth` / `against`, a spot name equal to an own mark, anything
  standing over a gap; `validate_project` and `construct` refuse a map narrower than the frame or
  above its top. `Params.level_frame`, `Params.layout` (the level's or `stage_layout`) are used by
  the scene, `directing.stage_frame` and `stage_reframes`. No ground band on a level; a background
  picture moves by parallax factor 0.2 (`_picture(factor)`, `_move_by_parallax` shared with the
  layers); the tiles (`_level_tiles`, `LevelTiles`) come last in the backdrop.
- **Drawing** (`cartoon/level_drawing.py`, Pillow): `level_shapes`, `draw_columns`,
  `LevelColors`, `drawn_rows`; 8-column chunks, supersampled ×2 with a box filter (chunks join
  byte-exactly); each chunk drawn one column wider under the next (a seam showed at the
  resampled edge otherwise); only chunks in view are members of `LevelTiles`.
- **Geometry** (`cartoon/level_stage.py`, no Manim): `LevelFrame`, `level_frame`,
  `level_fit_problems`, `level_world`, `level_layout`, `LEVEL_SIZE`.
- Docs: CONFIG `stage` table (`level` row, `size` default) and new "Platform levels (`level`)";
  the `stage` docstring.

```yaml
- id: meadow
  type: stage
  set: park                 # optional: sky + hills behind the level
  params:
    props: []               # a set's props stand at depths; clear them on a level
    level:
      map: |
        ...............~~~~...........
        ..........b...................
        ..a......=====.........c......
        ##########....################
      spots: {a: start, b: high, c: home}     # optional; unnamed letters are named by themselves
      colors: {grass: accent}                 # ground, grass, platform, cloud, ladder
    camera_at: start
    characters: [{name: pip, at: start}, {name: kit, at: high}]
```

## Step 151 — Walking and jumping on a level, timed to the narration

What was built
- **Rules** (`src/vidgen/world/moves.py`, no manim; exported by `vidgen.world`): `walk_route`
  (cheapest path over (column, height) states: one-tile steps up / down eased across the column
  edge, ladders up and down incl. a hatch through the tile over a ladder, room for the body's
  height, never across a gap), `plan_jump` (take-off on the body's own floor, the lowest clear
  parabola from 0.75 tiles over the higher end, limits 5 across / 3 up / 8 down, landing on the
  goal's height or the highest reachable floor in that column), `Route`, `Leg`, `JumpPlan`,
  `arc_point`, `flight_seconds` (gravity 8 tiles/s², at most 4 tiles/s across, at least 0.7 s),
  `surface_under`, `is_floor`, `map_cell`, `reversed_route`, `walk_body` / `jump_body` (on a
  `World`; `World.moved` added). Refusals are `VidgenError`s saying where the way stops (a gap, a
  drop, a wall, no room under the tiles, another height) or why a jump fails (too far / high /
  deep, the tile the arc hits, a cloud it would land on first), from the nearest take-off.
- **Clouds are one-way** (DESIGN §86.7 says why): stand on top, walk through, jump up through;
  a fall onto a cloud lands there.
- **Goals and validation** (`cartoon/level_stage.py`): `level_goal` (a spot, a mark / x, or a map
  tile `{column, row}`), `LevelFrame.world_point`, `LevelStep`, `level_move_problems` (the replay
  of a scene's `walk_to`, `run_to`, `jump` with `to`, `enter`, `exit` in beat / `at` order) —
  `Stage._level_move_problems` feeds it from `action_sequence_problems`, so `vidgen validate`
  (and a render) refuses `beat 'x': 'pip' cannot walk to spot 'home': ...; jump there instead
  (- jump: pip, to: home)`.
- **Renderer** (`cartoon/level_motion.py`): `RouteWalk(Walk)` (a `_place` hook added to
  `Walk.interpolate_mobject`; facing per leg, front on a ladder, last side when stopped) and
  `ArcJump(Jump)` (faces the landing, longer crouch, arc, squash, landing wobble;
  `LEVEL_JUMP_CROUCH_SECONDS`, `LEVEL_JUMP_LAND_SECONDS`, `LANDING_WOBBLE_DEGREES` in
  `cartoon/motion.py`, whose `jump_phases` / `jump_motion_seconds` take the crouch / landing
  seconds as keyword arguments). Both keep `ground_y` on the floor under the character.
- **Stage** (`scenes/stage.py`): `on_level`, `level_pace`, `level_walk`, `level_enter`,
  `level_exit`, `level_jump` (a `Succession(RouteWalk, ArcJump)` when it needs a run-up),
  `level_moved` (`grounds` = the end floor: `keyframes` y 0), `level_homes`; `STAGE_SIZE` 0.45;
  `feet_y_at` raises on a level; `_timed_parts` splits a Succession for foley and motion effects.
- **Actions** (`scenes/moving.py`): `walk_to`, `run_to`, `enter`, `exit` go through the stage's
  level methods when `on_level` (default speeds × `level_pace`); `jump` gained `to` (`JumpTile`
  `{column, row}`, a spot, a mark or an x; refused without a level or together with `height`);
  `walk_to` `depth` refused on a level; run times the rules refuse while a batch is planned fall
  back to the default (apply raises with scene and beat).
- **Timing / tools**: `rushed_animation.max_speedup` (1.5) reports a `RouteWalk` / `ArcJump`
  play sped up beyond it; automatic directing (`_follow_written`, `_jumps_somewhere`: a jump to a
  place moves the character, changes its look, blocks close-ups) and the prop-handling replay
  (`holding.py`) follow jumps; storyboards show jumps half-way as before.
- Docs: CONFIG "Walking and jumping on a level" (and the Moving table, `run_time`, lint rows),
  DESIGN §86.7, the guide's `jump` row (+ `AGENTS.md`), `tasklist.md`.

YAML
```yaml
actions:
  - {walk_to: pip, to: high}                         # a spot / mark / x: along tiles and ladders
  - {jump: pip, to: cloud, at: 0.2}                   # a spot on the cloud (up through it)
  - {jump: pip, to: {column: 15, row: 3}}             # a tile of the map (from the top left, from 1)
  - {enter: kit, side: left}                          # walks in along the tiles to its own place
```

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/world/moves.py`, `src/vidgen/cartoon/level_motion.py`, `tests/test_platform_moves.py`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/world/__init__.py`, `world/world.py`, `cartoon/level_stage.py`,
  `cartoon/transition.py` (`Walk._place`), `cartoon/motion.py`, `cartoon/directing.py`,
  `cartoon/holding.py`, `scenes/moving.py`, `scenes/stage.py`, `config.py`
  (`RushedAnimationRule.max_speedup`), `lint/timing_rules.py`, `docs/CONFIG.md`, `DESIGN.md`,
  `src/vidgen/data/guide/AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `tasklist.md`, `HANDOFF.md`.

Public interfaces (`vidgen.api` unchanged)
- `jump` option `to`; lint setting `rushed_animation.max_speedup`; `vidgen.world` exports
  `walk_route`, `plan_jump`, `walk_body`, `jump_body`, `surface_under`, `Route`, `Leg`,
  `JumpPlan`; the stage methods above (duck-typed by the moving actions).

Decisions
- One-way clouds (above). Steps of one tile are walked; higher ones need a jump. A jump's run-up
  is on foot without ladders (a climb and a jump are two actions). Default walking speeds on a
  level scale with `size` (otherwise every default walk was "fast": speed lines). The speed-up
  lint only counts level moves so plain-stage lint results do not change. `enter` / `exit` ways
  depend on the camera's view and are checked at render time only.
- Searched first: walks (`Walk`, `walk_seconds`, `enter_path`), jump motion (`jump_phases`,
  `jump_stretch`, `settle_wobble`), timing (`ActionRunner`, `rushed_animation`), replays
  (`holding_problems`, `_follow_written`) are reused; no path-finding or arc code existed.

Known gaps for Step 152 and later
- Props (key / door, coins / stars, friendly blockers) are not world items yet: the rules know
  only tiles and bodies; a body never blocks another (two characters can stand in one place).
- A jump's arc can rise above the frame's top (the camera moves sideways only; a cloud on the
  top used row with a character on it touches the edge); a mid-air pick-up or reaction is not
  possible; no jump sound distinct from the stage's boing and no landing sound (Step 153).
- `enter` of a character that waits off stage, then `exit` before its `enter`, is refused ("not
  standing on a tile"); `walk_to` to a tile `{column, row}` is not offered (only `jump`);
  `vidgen direct` does not know the x of a jump to a tile; `vidgen screenplay` has no "jumps onto"
  verb; climbing uses the front walk cycle (no arms on rungs); walking through a low cloud shows
  the character inside it.
- Level moves of characters that keyframes / rides moved are not replayed by `vidgen validate`
  (checked at render). The camera follow and `character_size` are Step 154.

## Step 152 — Story props and reactions on a level

What was built
- **World items** (`src/vidgen/world/items.py`, no manim): `Item` (key, door, coin, star, blocker;
  `blocks`, `label`, `hint`), `World.items` / `item` / `with_items` (`moved` moves a blocker's
  item too); the map's `$` coins and `*` stars (`Level.items`, named `coin_1`, `star_1`... in map
  order, floating in the middle of an air cell).
- **Rules**: `moves.py` `Obstacle` / `obstacle_of` / `obstacles_in` (a closed door or a blocker
  shuts its column from its feet up to the solid tile above it), `walk_route` / `plan_jump` take
  `obstacles` and name the one in the way with what clears it; `route_pickups` / `jump_pickups`
  (shares of the walk or the flight: mid-jump pickups); `walk_body` / `jump_body` apply both.
  `story_props.py`: `open_door` (locked: only by the key's holder within 1.6 tiles on its floor),
  `close_door`, `step_aside`, `hold_key`. Exported by `vidgen.world`.
- **Stage params**: `level.locks: {door: key}`, `level.blockers: [character]`, `level.colors`
  `coin` / `star`; checks (a door prop, a key prop, characters, no prop or character named like
  a coin or star); every closed `door` prop on a level is in the way. New built-in prop `key`
  (`STORY_PROPS`, 0.3 tall, held by its bow).
- **Actions**: `open` gained `by` (the opener turns to the door and reaches for its edge with the
  key's hand; on a level the rules check it); `close` puts a door back in the way; new
  `step_aside` (a blocker steps back off the path: a walk in depth to 0.3, feet 0.3 tiles higher,
  drawn behind; or walks `to` a place); `walk_to` / `run_to` / `jump` gained `react: {when:
  pickup | land | arrive, expression, effect}`; `walk_to` / `run_to` take a tile `{column, row}`
  (`MapTile`, renamed from `JumpTile`).
- **Validation**: `level_move_problems(..., props=LevelProps)` follows the key (pick_up, hold,
  give, put_down, throw, let_go, blow_away), doors (open with `by`, close), blockers
  (step_aside) and the moves with obstacles and pickups; refusals at `.to`, `.by`, `.target`,
  `.react` naming the beat.
- **Renderer**: `cartoon/level_items.py` `Collectible` (bobbing, a coin turning; `collect()` pops
  it: grows, rises, fades in 0.35 s), added after the shadows (not graded by the light).
  `level_motion.py`: `Reaction` and a `_Cues` mixin on `RouteWalk` / `ArcJump` (`pickups`,
  `reaction`): pickups pop on the frame the feet get there; a reaction eases the face to its
  expression from its moment by changing the base state the walk / jump draws from (lip sync and
  motion go on) and starts its effect symbol (added hidden by `Stage.level_moved`).
- **Stage**: `level_state` (`_level_now` reads key holders from the props), `level_pickups`,
  `level_walk` / `level_jump` (`react`, obstacles, pickups, `.picked`), `level_enter` /
  `level_exit` (obstacles), `level_moved` (pickups collected, effect symbol), `level_open`,
  `level_close`, `level_step_aside`. Directing: `StageFrame.columns` (a tile's x).
- Docs: CONFIG "Story props on a level (keys, doors, coins, stars, blockers)", the Moving table
  (`step_aside`, `react`, tiles), `open` `by`, the level row and symbols, the action lists; DESIGN
  §86.8; the guide's `jump`, `step_aside`, `open` rows (+ `AGENTS.md`).

YAML
```yaml
params:
  props: [{prop: door, name: gate, at: gate_spot}, {prop: key, name: gold_key, at: key_spot}]
  level:
    map: |
      ...............*..........
      ..a...k..$$$.d.......t..h.
      ##############....########
    spots: {a: start, k: key_spot, d: gate_spot, t: path, h: home}
    locks: {gate: gold_key}
    blockers: [tobble]
beats:
  - actions: [{walk_to: lumo, to: key_spot}, {pick_up: lumo, to: gold_key, at: 0.6}]
  - actions: [{walk_to: lumo, to: {column: 13, row: 3}, react: {when: pickup, expression: happy, effect: sparkle}}]
  - actions: [{open: gate, by: lumo}]
  - actions: [{jump: lumo, to: {column: 19, row: 3}, react: {when: land, expression: laughing}}]
  - actions: [{step_aside: tobble, at: 0.6}]
```

Decisions
- Coins and stars are map symbols (many, never named in a beat); key, door and blocker are the
  stage's props and characters standing at spots, given their parts by `level.locks` /
  `level.blockers` (DESIGN §86.8 says why). Letters stay spots only.
- An obstacle shuts its column up to the tile above it, so a jump cannot hop a closed door or a
  small blocker ("blocks walks and jumps"), while a path over its head stays open.
- `react` lives on the move (not a separate timed action): the runner plays an action changing
  the same character after the one playing, and a pickup's time is known only once the move is
  planned. Key `when`, not `on` (YAML 1.1 reads `on:` as `true`).
- No snail species was added: a blocker is any cast member (the scratch story used a turtle);
  a new species is a much larger job.
- Reused: `door` prop shapes and `open` / `close`, `pick_up` / `give` / holdings for the key,
  `_reach_low` for the opener, `Walk` in depth and the depth draw order for stepping aside,
  `EffectSymbol` / `show_symbol` / `effect_color` for the reaction's symbol, `blend_poses` /
  `kind_parts` for the face. Nothing for pickups or obstacles existed (searched).

Known gaps for Step 153 and later
- **Sounds (Step 153)**: no sound yet for a pickup (the `Collectible.collect` frame), a door
  opening on a level (`level_open`; the room door creak exists as foley), a key turning, a
  blocker stepping aside, a landing (`ArcJump` settle start) or a reaction's effect symbol (an
  `effect` action plays one with foley; the move's symbol does not). The pickup shares are in
  `walk.pickups` / `jump.pickups` (path shares, not times: map them through the walk's phases or
  record the frame in `collect`).
- `enter` / `exit` on a level pick up nothing (the replay does not follow their ways); a blocker
  that stepped back off the path is not followed any more (a later walk of it fails at render:
  "not standing on a tile"); `close` on a door with someone standing in it is not refused.
- A move's reaction expression is kept (like `emote`), not undone at the next beat; a jump's
  `when: arrive` starts on its last frame.
- `vidgen lint` `off_frame` reports the level's tile chunks (`level_3`...) cut at the frame edge
  when a following camera happens to rest at the stage's centre (seen on the scratch story at
  `meadow_b5`; not from this step's code, the chunks are Step 150's): Step 154 (camera) should
  exempt them.
- A `set:` with props cannot be used with a story prop list (its props stand at depths: Step 150).

## Step 153 — Sound effects on a level

What was built
- **Level sounds as stage foley** (`cartoon/foley.py`, no manim): `PlayedAction.pickups`
  (`(share, kind)` of the coins / stars a move picks up) and `.unlocks`; `lands` also marks a level
  jump's touch-down. `pickup_cues` (a `coin` / `twinkle` per pickup, the share mapped through the
  walk's easing and wind-up or the jump's crouch; each further one of a kind +1 semitone, at most
  +5), `landing_cues` (a soft short `thud` + a `footstep`, louder after a longer drop),
  `door_cues` (`unlock` then the creak 0.3 s later for a locked door opened with its key),
  `step_aside` (a soft low `swoosh` and heavier, softer footsteps). Constants
  `LEVEL_LANDING_THUD`, `LEVEL_LANDING_STEP`, `LANDING_INTENSITY*`, `PICKUP_SOUNDS`,
  `PICKUP_PITCH_STEP` / `_MAX`, `UNLOCK_GAIN`, `UNLOCK_SECONDS`, `ASIDE_STEP`, `ASIDE_SWOOSH`.
- **Hooks**: `Stage._played` reads an `ArcJump`'s landing (`1 − phases.after`) and the `pickups` of
  `RouteWalk` / `ArcJump` (`_picked_kinds`); `Stage.level_open` returns whether a key unlocked the
  door, `_Reshape._on_level` passes it on and `Open.apply` marks the `PropReshape` `unlocks`.
- **New built-in sounds** (`sfx.py`, numpy): `unlock`, `coin`, `twinkle` (descriptions in
  `vidgen list-sfx`; levels set by the library: −27 LUFS, peaks ≤ −9 dBFS).
- Docs: CONFIG sfx table (3 rows), the foley paragraph, the level's **Sounds** bullet (replacing
  the Step 153 placeholder), the walking section; the stage's `foley` param docstring; DESIGN §86.9
  and the §6 API note; the guide's sound list and cartoon **Sound** bullet (+ `AGENTS.md`), where
  the `jump` row's `react: {on: land}` (a Step 152 slip) now reads `when`.

## Step 154 — Camera follow and `character_size`

What was built
- **`character_size: small | medium | large`** (`config.CharacterSize`): a top-level key and a
  `stage` param; the default `size` × 0.7 / 1 / 1.4 (`level_stage.CHARACTER_SIZE_FACTORS`,
  `character_size_default`; the stage's `_default_size` before-validator, which replaced
  `_level_size`): plain stage 0.315 / 0.45 / 0.63, level 0.175 / 0.25 / 0.35. Scene wins, then
  video, then medium; a written `size` wins over the video's; both in one scene is refused.
  The video's value reaches the stage scenes as data (`includes.expand_character_size`, called by
  `Project._load` after `expand_sets`, also after a variant's merge). Medium = the old sizes.
- **Plain stage (decided, DESIGN §86.10)**: applied as the named `size`: characters and props
  scale; stage width, marks, ground line, background, layers and walking times stay.
- **Level**: tiles, props, coins, stars scale with `size`; default speeds scale too
  (`level_pace`), so moves and their foley take the same seconds at every size (render test
  compares the SFX schedule medium vs large). Sky, background picture and layers keep their
  framing (the distance; deliberate, DESIGN says why).
- **Camera** (`vidgen/camera.py`, no manim): `smooth_damp`, `SmoothFollow` (dead zone 0.08 of
  the width, ease 0.45 s, hard limit 0.3, bounds; vertical: head room 0.08, feet room 0.2, head
  never within 0.02 of the top). `NarratedScene.follow_with_camera` / `_camera_step` use a
  follower's `view_center(center, dt, w, h, bounds)` and `restart()` when it has them (plain
  `x_of` unchanged). `Stage.camera_follower(mob)` gives a `SmoothFollow` on a level; the `follow`
  action uses it. **`level.follow: <character>`**: `Stage._follow_hero` starts the camera on the
  hero (settled view) and follows from the first frame; refused with `camera_at`; must name a
  stage character. `StageFrame.follows`, `_start_state` (camera_x `None`), `reframe_path(following=)`.
- **Vertical**: `LevelFrame.top` (map bottom + used rows + 2 + `LEVEL_HEAD_ROOM` 2 tiles, at least
  the frame's top) → `Stage.camera_bounds`; tall levels no longer refused (`level_fit_problems`
  only checks the width; its hint names `character_size: large`). With a raised top the colour /
  gradient sky moves with the camera (factor 0), `layer_half_extent(stage_top=)` covers the views
  up there; tiles are drawn to their used rows.
- **Portrait raise**: `level_raise` (sky over the tiles + a character ≤ 0.4 of the frame, raise ≤
  0.3 of it; whole rows; portrait frames only) → `LevelFrame.below` / `bottom`; `level_shapes(below=)`
  and `draw_columns(below=)` draw ground under the map (gaps stay open); `Stage._level_lift` raises
  the background picture and the layers with it.
- **Lint**: new rule `small_speaker` (`SmallSpeakerRule.min_face` 0.075, warning): a speaking
  character in view whose head box is smaller; suggests a closeup / medium shot or
  `character_size: large`. `off_frame` skips layout objects with `scenery: true` (introspect sets
  it for an `ImageMobject` with `scenery = True`: the level's tile chunks).
- Docs: CONFIG (top-level row, stage rows, new "Character size (`character_size`)", "The camera
  on a level (`follow`)", the level Size bullet, Shots note, `follow` action row, lint rows and
  settings example); Shorts cookbook §3 (recommend `large`); the guide (+ `AGENTS.md`): 9:16
  cartoons bullet, `follow` row, cartoon lint list, troubleshooting row; DESIGN §86.10 (+ §86.4
  edits); stage docstrings.

YAML
```yaml
character_size: medium            # video (default); a 9:16 variant: character_size: large
scenes:
  - id: meadow
    type: stage
    set: park
    params:
      props: []
      character_size: large       # this scene (wins over the video's); or size: 0.3, not both
      level:
        follow: lumo              # the hero: the camera starts on it and follows it gently
        map: |
          ...
lint:
  rules:
    small_speaker: {min_face: 0.075}
```

Decisions
- `character_size` applies to plain stages too (above); the video's value is expanded into the
  scene params at load (like sets) so every consumer of `params.size` agrees.
- Background picture, sky and layers do not scale with `character_size` (distance; set layers
  are frame fractions). The brief listed "backgrounds/parallax scale together": what scales
  together is the near world; parallax keeps working because the camera moves more units per
  tile at larger sizes.
- Smooth following only on levels (plain stages keep the hard follow: unchanged renders).
- The hero follow is opt-in (`level.follow`), not guessed.
- The portrait raise is portrait-only, so landscape levels (and all existing tests) are unchanged.
- Searched first: `Spring.follow` (time-function targets, not frame-by-frame), `view_center_within`,
  `layer_half_extent`, `layer_transform`, `_move_by_parallax` (reused, factor 0 for the sky),
  `shot_home` (gives the follow back after a shot), the lint `hidden_speaker` pattern.

  top of Clover Hill; she skips along collecting sun pennies, climbs a ladder to a plank for the

## Step 156 — Actions timed to a spoken word (and the Phase P plan)

What was built
- **Phase P planned**: tasklist.md "Phase P — Presentation toolkit" (Steps 156–164, the brief's
  titles and scope as checkboxes) and DESIGN §87 (goal, rules, §87.1 a table of the nine steps'
  design intent, §87.2 this step).
- **Word anchors** (`src/vidgen/word_anchors.py`, no manim): a beat action's `at` may be
  `"@gradient"` (the first time the beat says it), `"@gradient#2"` (a later time),
  `"@gradient+0.3s"` / `"@gradient -0.25s"` (an offset; the `s` is required so `@K-Phi-3` stays
  one word), `"@learning rate"` (a phrase). Matching ignores case, accents (`textnorm.fold`) and
  surrounding punctuation, against `beat.text.split()` (the words the timings are of).
- **Resolution** (DESIGN §87.2): `ActionConfig.at` is `float | "@..."`; the written anchor is kept
  in `ActionConfig.anchor`, `at` becomes its fraction. `BeatConfig` checks the word and estimates
  (default rate), `VideoConfig` re-estimates in its `language` and `narration.words_per_second`,
  `Project.__init__` re-times beats with an MP3 from `beat_word_times` (TTS alignment, else the
  estimate within the MP3's speech; the spoken form via `Project.spoken`), the captions' timings.
  So every consumer of `at` (runner, stage move order, musicfit reveals, directing, host) reads a
  float unchanged, and validate / direct / storyboard / lint / drafts work before `vidgen tts`.
  `shorthand()` and `model_dump` write the anchor back; `resolved()` keeps the fraction.
- **Errors**: `scenes[0].beats[1]: actions: callout item2 at '@downn': beat 'steps_b2' does not say
  "downn" (words like it: down)`; `... says "gradient" 2 times, so there is no #3`; syntax errors
  with examples; a beat id before `@` on an action; `at 1.5` says the range and the word form; an
  anchor in a scene's `sfx:` list points to the beat's `sfx` action.
- **Every action that takes `at`**: all go through `ActionConfig` (scene actions, `callout`,
  `sfx`, `particles`, stage moves / acting / handling, host actions), so all take a word; the test
  validates a bullets scene (reveal, callout) and a stage scene (walk_to, gesture, emote, sfx).
  **`lower_third`**'s `at` takes `"@Ada"` (the scene's first beat that says it; `#N` over the
  scene) or `"intro_b2@Ada"`, checked in `validate_project`, timed in `window()`.
- **Translations**: `_translated` pins anchors of translated beats to the source config's fraction
  (`pin_translated_anchors`) before validating the translated config.
- **Example and docs**: `examples/minimal` trend callout `at: "@sparse"` (0.33; was 0.4); CONFIG
  "Actions on a spoken word" (new subsection of Beat actions; the `at` rows of actions, sfx and
  lower_third; the Checks paragraph moved above it), guide `at` bullet and its example
  (`at: "@iterate"`) + `AGENTS.md`, EXTENDING "A word of the narration".

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/word_anchors.py`, `tests/test_word_anchors.py`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/config.py` (`ActionConfig.at`, `anchor`, `fraction`, `set_fraction`, the
  serializer, `resolved`, `shorthand`; `BeatConfig._time_word_anchors`; `VideoConfig` calls
  `time_config_anchors`; `DEFAULT_WORDS_PER_SECOND`; `SfxCue` refuses an anchor),
  `src/vidgen/project.py`, `src/vidgen/api.py`, `src/vidgen/scenes/overlays.py`,
  `examples/minimal/video.yaml`, `docs/CONFIG.md`, `docs/EXTENDING.md`,
  `src/vidgen/data/guide/AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `tasklist.md`, `HANDOFF.md`,
  `tests/test_actions.py` (the range message changed: "0 <= at < 1").

Public interfaces
- YAML: action `at: "@WORDS[#N][±S s]"`; `lower_third` `at: "[BEAT]@WORDS[#N][±S s]"`.
- `vidgen.api` adds `WordAnchor`, `is_word_anchor`, `parse_word_anchor`, `locate_word_anchor`
  (DESIGN §87.2; built-ins import only `vidgen.api`). `ActionConfig.anchor`, `.fraction`,

Decisions
- Resolve to a fraction at load rather than teach every consumer a new type: one place, and the
  render worker loads the project after `vidgen tts`, so renders get the audio's times.
- A translated beat keeps the source word's moment (its words differ); an untranslated beat of a
  translated variant keeps its anchor and its own audio timing.
- No new lint rule: a word that is not said is a validate error, and a word late in the beat is
  already caught by `rushed_animation` (run times shortened below 0.5 s).
- `cartoon/directing._beat_words` was left as it is (it passes the spoken form only for voice
  sounds); `word_anchors.beat_words` always passes `Project.spoken` like the captions. Moving
  directing onto it would change gesture timing with `pronunciation:`: not done unasked.

  the thumbnail's `at`, `sting` start / end.
- With `overlap` / `interrupt` the runner scales `at` by the beat's shorter body, so a word-timed
  action lands slightly early (Backlog).
- `@mid-20s` parses as `mid` with -20 s; write `"@mid-20s+0s"` (Backlog).
- Pre-existing, not from this step: `test_builtins_use_only_the_public_api` fails on

## Step 158 — Code that morphs between versions

What was built
- **`code_morph`**, a new scene type (`src/vidgen/scenes/code_morph.py`, DESIGN §87.4):
  `versions` (at least two; each the code as a string, or `{code | path, highlight}`), plus
  `code`'s `language`, `title`, `line_numbers`, `style`, `font`, `size`, `highlight_color`,
  `wrap`. Version 1 shows with beat 1; at beat *i* the listing morphs into version *i*: kept
  glyphs and line numbers glide, the window resizes, removed lines / tokens fade out, new tokens
  of an edited line fade in, new lines grow from their left end. A version's `highlight` (a line
  spec, or `changed`: new, edited, re-indented or moved lines) dims the others and lays `code`'s
  band. Chosen over a mode of `code` because `code`'s beats follow its `highlight` entries and its
  targets are one listing's lines.
- **The diff** (`diff_code`, `difflib`, pure): lines by text without indentation; within a
  replaced block, lines paired in order by token similarity (>= 0.5, a small DP) so an edited line
  stays one line; a line moved unchanged is found; shared tokens keep their characters. A glyph
  is (line, n-th non-space character), which is how Manim's `Code` draws them, wrapped or not.
- **On a word** (Step 156): targets `version<N>` / `version<N>.line<K>` have the morph as their
  entrance, so `{reveal: version2, at: "@cache", run_time: 1.5}` morphs on the word; a version a
  `reveal` action shows is left out of the scene's own steps (else its beat would morph at its
  start). Morphs only go forward; skipped versions are diffed away directly.
- **Phone readability**: `CodeListing._fit_listing` became `_fit_listings` (one font size, scale
  and wrap width for several listings; `code` passes one), so `code`'s rules (wrap to >= 32
  columns at >= the readable size) hold for every version. Versions are centred across the body
  and share the top of the tallest. `code`'s band drawing moved to a shared `listing_bands`.
- **After a morph** the scene holds the new version as one `Code` (`_Morph.clean_up_from_scene`
  removes whole families: playing the group had lifted unanimated parts, e.g. a wrapped line's
  empty number label, into the scene), so the layout dump, lint and `is_shown` see one listing.
- **Checks** (`vidgen validate`): fewer than two versions; a version equal to the one before;
  a `highlight` past its version's last line (or an invalid spec); code and path both / neither;
  a missing `path` file.
- **Docs and examples**: CONFIG `code_morph` section, targets-table row, the header-band and
  per-beat lists, a sentence in "Actions on a spoken word"; the guide's chooser row, per-beat
  note and a snippet (+ `AGENTS.md`); `examples/gallery` scene `morph` (a loop becoming a
  comprehension, morphing on "comprehension"); `docs/gallery/code_morph.md` + stills / GIFs
  (`vidgen gallery --types code_morph`); README's scene list.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/scenes/code_morph.py`, `tests/test_code_morph.py`, `docs/gallery/code_morph.md`,
  `docs/gallery/media/code_morph-{16x9,9x16}.{png,gif}`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/scenes/code.py` (`_fit_listings`, `listing_bands`), `scenes/__init__.py`,
  `examples/gallery/video.yaml`, `docs/CONFIG.md`, `docs/gallery/README.md`, `README.md`,
  `src/vidgen/data/guide/AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `tasklist.md`, `HANDOFF.md`,
  `tests/test_builtin_scenes.py`, `tests/test_actions_coverage.py`, `tests/test_translation.py`
  (samples for the new type).

Public interfaces
- YAML: scene type `code_morph` (params above); targets `title`, `listing`, `version<N>`,
  `version<N>.line<K>`; `highlight: changed`.
- No `vidgen.api` change (the diff lives in the scene module; built-ins import only the API).

Decisions
- Opacity animations, not `FadeOut`, for what leaves: a remover would dissolve the old listing's
  group in the scene's mobject list.
- No lint rule: the code scenes' layout rules read the beat-end stills (one `Code` there), and a
  no-op version is a validate error.

  `reveal` action's morph runs for the action's `run_time` (default 0.8 s; docs write 1.5).

## Step 159 — Terminal scene

What was built
- **`terminal`**, a new scene type (`src/vidgen/scenes/terminal.py`, DESIGN §87.5): a terminal
  window in which step *i*'s command is typed at beat *i* (a block cursor moving along,
  `typing_speed` 18 characters/s, faster when the beat is short), then its output appears row by
  row and the prompt comes back. The output is the author's: vidgen runs nothing. `steps`: a
  command (a string) or `{command, output, clear, output_color}`; an output-only step is a
  program still printing (no prompt before it); `clear` starts a new page in the same window.
  `prompt` (`$`, `""`, `>>>`), `language` (`bash`; `pycon`...), `prompt_color` (`accent`), and
  the code scenes' `style`, `font`, `size`, `wrap`.
- **On a word** (Step 156): targets `command<N>`, `output<N>`, `output<N>.line<K>`; `{reveal:
  output2, at: "@fails"}` shows the output on the word, `command2` types the command then (with
  its output unless an action shows that). The scene leaves what an action reveals to it;
  what comes before it on the page appears at once. A first command left to an action still
  shows its prompt with the window.
- **`NarratedScene.entrance_time(target)`** (new public hook, default `None`): seconds a target's
  own entrance wants; `Reveal.run_time_for` uses it, so a `reveal` of a command types for its
  typing time instead of 0.8 s (an explicit `run_time` wins). EXTENDING mentions it.
- **Beside code / after code**: `code: {code | path, language, highlight}` puts a listing
  beside the terminal, left or above (whichever gives larger text in 16:9; above in 9:16), one
  font size for both; targets `code`, `code.line<K>`. After a `code` / `code_morph` scene,
  `carry: ["listing -> code"]` glides the listing into place (the carry machinery; checked by
  eye, see below).
- **Look and readability**: `code`'s window, Pygments colouring and fitting (`_fit_listings`
  gained `lexed=` and `numbered=`, and records `fit_scale` / `shown_lines` on each listing), so
  `code`'s phone rules hold. One window for the session, sized for the largest page.
- **Layout dump**: every prompt / command row / output row is its own one-line `Paragraph`
  placed on the page listing's glyphs, added to the window (a `Code`) once shown, so the dump
  and lint read exactly the text on screen, as `code`.
- **Docs and examples**: CONFIG `terminal` section, targets-table row, header-band and per-beat
  lists, "Actions on a spoken word"; guide chooser row, per-beat note and a snippet (+
  `AGENTS.md`); `examples/gallery` scene `shell` (after the morph, carrying its listing, the
  output on "pass"); `docs/gallery/terminal.md` + stills / GIFs; README's scene list; DESIGN
  §87.5. The Shorts cookbook is Step 164's.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/scenes/terminal.py`, `tests/test_terminal.py`, `docs/gallery/terminal.md`,
  `docs/gallery/media/terminal-{16x9,9x16}.{png,gif}`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/scenes/code.py` (`_fit_listings` / `_listing` / `_code` keywords),
  `src/vidgen/scene.py` (`entrance_time`), `src/vidgen/scenes/actions.py` (`Reveal.run_time_for`),
  `src/vidgen/scenes/__init__.py`, `examples/gallery/video.yaml`, `docs/CONFIG.md`,
  `docs/EXTENDING.md`, `docs/gallery/README.md`, `README.md`, `src/vidgen/data/guide/AGENTS.md`,
  `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `tasklist.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `tests/test_builtin_scenes.py`,
  `tests/test_actions_coverage.py`, `tests/test_translation.py` (samples for the new type).

Public interfaces
- YAML: scene type `terminal` (params above); targets `title`, `terminal`, `code`,
  `code.line<K>`, `command<N>`, `output<N>`, `output<N>.line<K>`.
- `NarratedScene.entrance_time(target) -> float | None` (through `vidgen.api`'s
  `NarratedScene`; DESIGN §87.5).

Decisions
- A scene type with an optional code pane rather than a general split of two scene types:
  there is no split mechanism, and the coding case (code + terminal) is what Shorts need.
- Segments as separate texts (not one listing with hidden glyphs), so targets are in the scene
  only once shown and the dump never reports text not on screen yet.
- Glyphs appear (printing), they do not fade; the cursor does not blink (a blink would make
  Manim redraw every frame of every wait).
- No lint rule: the code scenes' layout rules read the beat-end stills (`min_font` etc.).

Known gaps (Backlog, Quality)
- No split with other scene types; a long session does not scroll (`clear`); one colour per
  output; `code_morph`'s `reveal` could now use `entrance_time` for its 1.5 s morph.
