## Step 160 — Maths toolkit, part 1: function plots

What was built
- **`function_plot`**, a new scene type (`src/vidgen/scenes/function_plot.py`, DESIGN §87.6):
  maths axes (crossing at the origin when it is in view, arrow tips, round ticks, one `0`,
  faint grid, plain-text labels) with `functions` written as maths (`x^2`, `2x + 1`,
  `f(x) = sin(x)`, `{expr, name, label, color, domain, dashed}`; a later one may call an
  earlier one: `g(x) = f(x) + 1`), `x_range`, `y_range` (default from the values, an asymptote's
  far ends left out), `dots` (`{on, x, label, tangent, guides, color, tangent_color, decimals}`:
  a live label `'{name}({x}) = {y}'` / `'slope {slope}'`, a tangent that turns with the dot,
  dashed guides to the axes), `areas` (`{under, over, between, label, color, opacity,
  decimals}`: `'A = {area}'` is the signed integral), `x_label`, `y_label`, `grid`, `aspect`
  (`auto` / `equal`), `reveal` (`per_beat`: functions, then dots, then areas, one per beat; `all`).
  Undefined values and asymptotes break a curve into pieces (`curve_runs`).
- **Safe expressions** (`src/vidgen/mathexpr.py`, no manim): sympy is not a dependency
  (checked), so a small tokenizer + recursive-descent parser compiles to numpy closures;
  implicit products, `^` / `**`, unary minus, `pi` / `e` / `tau`, a whitelist of numpy functions,
  Unicode maths; anything else is a `ValueError` naming it, its column and close names.
  Nothing is ever `eval`ed.
- **The `trace` action** (`to`): a dot travels along its curve (its label, guides and tangent
  follow), or an area's right end moves (its value follows); 2 s, `until:` moves it back; on a
  word with `at: "@word"` (Step 156). `reveal` of `dot<N>`, `tangent<N>`, `area<N>`,
  `function<N>` on a word works; such an item's own beat holds.
- **Labels placed by vidgen**: curve labels where they cover no curve, axis, tick label or other
  label (else the nearest free spot); dot labels on the side above the curve, clear of the
  others; area labels inside the area where they fit, else above it. Curve, dot and area labels
  sit on a plate in the background colour (readable on the grid and on area fills).
- **Concept colours** (Step 157): a function named after a term (or whose label is one) takes the
  term's colour; an area takes the colour of the first term its label says; every label goes
  through `self.text`, so terms in labels are coloured. `terms.term_conflicts` (lint
  `concept_colors`) reports a function's or area's own `color` on a term.
- **Lint fix**: `cap_height` counts U+2212 (the minus of the tick labels) as a small glyph, like
  `-`; before, `−3` measured 3 % under `min_font`.
- **Docs and examples**: CONFIG `function_plot` section, targets-table row, `trace` in the
  actions table, "Actions on a spoken word", the terms "Where" list, `concept_colors` row, the
  header-band list; guide chooser row, a snippet and the `trace` action row (+ `AGENTS.md`);
  EXTENDING (maths expressions); README's scene list; `examples/gallery` scene `slope` (a dot
  tracing on "travels", the area revealed on "area" and growing on "grows");
  `docs/gallery/function_plot.md` + stills / GIFs (`vidgen gallery --types function_plot`).
- **Step 161 plan** in DESIGN §87.7: points, vectors (sums, `trace` generalised to move / scale
  them) and marks (braces, angle arcs, dimension lines; builders in a shared module exported by
  `vidgen.api`) as additions to `function_plot` (`functions` becomes optional; `axes: false` for
  pure geometry); a separate `number_line` scene type sharing the tick code.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/mathexpr.py`, `src/vidgen/scenes/function_plot.py`,
  `tests/test_function_plot.py`, `docs/gallery/function_plot.md`,
  `docs/gallery/media/function_plot-{16x9,9x16}.{png,gif}`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/api.py`, `src/vidgen/scenes/__init__.py`, `src/vidgen/terms.py`,
  `src/vidgen/lint/layout_rules.py`, `examples/gallery/video.yaml`, `docs/CONFIG.md`,
  `docs/EXTENDING.md`, `docs/gallery/README.md`, `README.md`, `src/vidgen/data/guide/AGENTS.md`,
  `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `tasklist.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `tests/test_builtin_scenes.py`,
  `tests/test_actions_coverage.py`, `tests/test_translation.py` (samples for the new type).

Public interfaces
- YAML: scene type `function_plot` (params above); targets `title`, `axes`, `function<N>`,
  `function:<name>`, `dot<N>`, `tangent<N>`, `area<N>`; action `trace` (`to`).
- `vidgen.api`: `MathExpression`, `parse_expression`, `pretty_expression`, `split_definition`,
  `MATH_FUNCTIONS`, `MATH_CONSTANTS`, `MATH_NAMES` (DESIGN §87.6, EXTENDING).

Decisions
- A scene type, not a `line_chart` mode: chart axes sit at the plot's edges and plot the
  author's data; maths axes cross at the origin and plot expressions.
- Own parser rather than `ast` + whitelist: maths syntax (`2x`, `x^2`, `π`) is what authors write.
- `trace` plays an animation on the dot (or the area's shape) plus a no-op animation on each
  other shown part: Manim then redraws them every frame instead of freezing them in the static
  background, and no wrapper group is added to the scene.
- An item a `reveal` action shows keeps its slot in the scene's steps (empty), as in the other
  scenes, so the other items keep their beats.

## Step 161 — Maths toolkit, part 2: geometry basics

What was built
- **Geometry on `function_plot`'s plane** (as planned in DESIGN §87.7; details §87.8):
  `functions` became optional (at least one of `functions`, `points`, `vectors`, `marks`),
  `axes: false` hides axes, ticks and grid, and the ranges default to the figure. New lists:
  `points` (`[x, y]` or `{at, name, label, color, decimals}`), `vectors` (`[x, y]` from the
  origin or `{from, to | components, name, label, color}`, positions as `[x, y]`, a point's or
  vector's name; `{sum: [a, b]}` draws copies of b... sliding tip to tail, then the resultant)
  and `marks`: `{segment: [A, B, C], closed, dashed}`, `{brace: [A, B]}`, `{angle: [A, V, B]}`
  (a square at 90°), `{dimension: [A, B]}`; braces and dimensions go outside the figure
  (`side:` to choose). Labels are live templates: `{x}`, `{y}`, `{name}`, `{length}`, `{angle}`.
  `aspect` defaults to `equal` with vectors or angle marks or without functions.
- **`trace` generalised**: `{trace: "point:C", to: [4, 4]}` moves a point,
  `{trace: "vector:a", to: [x, y]}` / `{trace: "vector:a", scale: 2}` moves / scales a vector
  (tail fixed); vectors, sums, marks and labels drawn from them follow on every frame. A sum or
  a vector ending at a point's name cannot be traced (the message says what to trace instead).
- **`number_line`**, a new scene type: `range`, `step`, `points` (a number or `{at, name, label}`;
  `trace` slides them), `intervals` in interval notation (`"[-1, 3)"`, `"(2, inf)"`, or
  `{from, to, ends, label}`; dots, rings, an arrow at infinity, stacked lanes when overlapping),
  `jumps` (`[2, 5]`: an arc above the line labelled `+3`; higher over an earlier one), one item
  per beat (`reveal: all` / `reveal` actions on words). Horizontal in 9:16 too, numbers thinned.
- **Mark builders for everyone**: `vidgen/geometry_marks.py` (`brace_mark`, `angle_mark`,
  `dimension_mark`, `segment_normal`, `angle_between`, `GeometryMark`), exported by `vidgen.api`.
- **Shared maths parts** moved out of `function_plot.py` into `scenes/math_axes.py` (axes, tick
  labels, live labels, label placement, `ChainedTargets` (entrances that bring what an item
  stands on), the `trace` action and `TraceMove`); `function_plot.py` shrank accordingly.
- **Concept colours**: points, vectors, marks, number-line items take the colour of a term their
  label says; `terms.term_conflicts` (lint `concept_colors`) reports their explicit `color` on one.
- **Lint fix**: `cap_height` counts `= + < > ≤ ≥ × ÷ ~` as x-height glyphs (`x = −3` was 0.4 %
  under `min_font` at the readable size).
- **Docs and examples**: CONFIG (`function_plot` geometry bullets, params rows and two examples;
  a `number_line` section; targets table, `trace` row, terms "Where", `concept_colors`, word

## Step 162 — Charts that change between beats

What was built
- **Which charts** (DESIGN §87.9): all chart types were checked. `bar_chart` and `line_chart`
  take values per state; `pie`, `histogram`, `scatter`, `heatmap` and `stat` do not (reasons in
  §87.9). Charts without `changes` are unchanged: `vidgen gallery --types bar_chart,line_chart`
  re-rendered their stills and GIFs byte for byte (only the params tables changed).
- **`changes`** on both: the later states (the first is `values` / `series`). `bar_chart`:
  `changes: [[58, 66, 30], ...]` (one value per label) and `sort: true` (largest first,
  re-sorted at each change; labels fade by up to 75 % while passing another bar). One value
  scale over every state, so heights compare (the chart has no value axis to rescale).
  `line_chart`: `changes: [{loss: [...]}, ...]` (series left out keep theirs; one series: a plain
  list), `rescale: true` (the y axis rescales when the values leave it or span less than half of
  it; `y_min` / `y_max` pin an end; `false`: one axis over every state). Old ticks and gridlines
  slide to their values on the new axis while fading, new ones slide in.
- **Steps and words**: change N is a step after the chart's own reveal steps (the highlight step
  stays last), or plays on a word with `{reveal: change<N>, at: "@word"}` (the scene then leaves
  that step empty, as `code_morph` does). `change<N>` targets (the whole chart) are "shown" once
  the chart reached state N (`ChangingChart.is_shown`); a reveal plays a change for 1.2 s.
  `reveal_steps` adds a rise / fall step per change (host reactions, music cues).
- **Cursor**: `{trace: series1, to: 4, at: "@word"}` (or `series:<name>`) sweeps a dot with the
  line's value (linear between points) along the line; on category `x`, `to` is the position
  from 1. It stays, rides along through changes; `until:` takes it back.
- **Concept colours**: unchanged paths (`self.text` / `fit_text`; a series named after a term
  keeps its colour); tested through a change.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/scenes/chart_changes.py` (`ChangingChart` mixin, `needs_rescale`,
  `state_axes`, `swap_parts` / `_SwapAtEnd`, `keep_opacity`, `lerp`), `tests/test_chart_changes.py`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/scenes/bar_chart.py` (layouts as functions of a fractional slot and a
  value; `set_bar`; `play_change`; `_order`), `src/vidgen/scenes/line_chart.py` (states computed
  up front; `_set_series`, `play_change`, `_rescale`, `_Cursor`, `trace_problem`,

## Step 163 — Narration–picture check in lint

What was built
- **`said_before_shown`** (warning; `src/vidgen/lint/narration_rule.py`, DESIGN §87.10): the
  narration names an on-screen *label* (a scene text of at most `max_words` 4 words with a
  content word: a diagram node, a callout, a stage, an axis title) more than `min_lead` 1.5 s
  before it is on screen, and does not name it again in the beat that shows it. Message:
  `beat 'cache_b1' says "database" at 4.9 s, but 'Database' appears only in beat 'cache_b3': show
  it on the word ({reveal: <target>, at: "@database"}) or say it when it shows`; within a beat
  `... appears 5.9 s later`.
- **When a label arrives**: from every frame of the layout dump (beat-end stills; a storyboard's
  mid-beat stills make it finer): it was not there at the frame before its first one. A
  `reveal` / `callout` / `transform` of that beat pins it to the action's time (Step 156 word
  anchors included): a callout whose `label` has the label's words, or an action on a word the
  label says. When it is named: the beats' word times (`word_anchors.beat_words`: the TTS
  alignment, else the estimate, so it works before `vidgen tts`) over the activity file's beat
  starts.
- **Matching**: case and accents folded (NFKC first, so `x²` is not a word), English stems
  (plural, `-ing`, `-ed`, final `e`, doubled consonant; other languages a plural `s`), English
  and Portuguese stop words, numbers and single letters dropped; a multi-word label counts as
  named when all its words are said within `len + 1` content words of one beat.
- **What the dump knows per beat** (Step 162's note): a chart's category labels and series names
  are in the dump from the beat the chart shows, and `changes` only change numbers; numbers are
  never content words and labels with the same words are one label (`slope 0.50` -> `slope
  1.20`, a value counting), so chart changes, rescaled ticks, live values and cursors never
  count as reveals. Checked by a real render (bar race with `sort` and a change on a word, a
  line chart with a change and a cursor): no finding.
- **Not counted**: overlays (captions repeat the narration; chapter indicator), speech bubbles,
  maths, code, texts longer than `max_words`, a label whose words another text on screen
  already says (a heading), a label named again as it shows (the early word was in passing).
- **`unsaid_reveal`** (default severity `off`; `info` once given a severity): a beat other than
  the scene's first brings new labels and the scene's narration names none of them. Kept off:
  on the examples it mostly finds labels that need no words (below).
- **Runner**: `SceneContext.narration` (a `NarrationPicture`), filled by `narration_picture`
  only when one of the two rules runs; `_timing_findings` gets the layout dump and now passes a
  scene rule's `objects` to its finding, so `lint_ignore: [{rule: said_before_shown, object:
  Database}]` works and the JSON `object` is the label.
- **Docs**: CONFIG lint table rows, config block, JSON `object` note, a bullet in "Actions on a
  spoken word"; guide troubleshooting rows and a sentence at the `at` bullet (+ `AGENTS.md`);
  DESIGN §87.10. CHANGELOG is left to Step 164 (the phase's entry).

False positives, measured (`vidgen lint` with fresh renders of `examples/gallery` (23 scenes),
`plan` (19), `minimal` (11), `kphi3` (8, real audio); plus the rules run directly on every
existing dump of the examples, 14 builds incl. vertical and `pt`: 118 scenes, 365 beats, 338
labels)
- `said_before_shown`: 2 findings. `plan` `how_cache_works_b1` names the database two beats
  before its node appears and beat 3 never names it: a real, useful finding. `kphi3` `title`
  says "large language model" in beat 1, and the subtitle "in Large Language Models" shows in
  beat 2: correct, minor (a title card). gallery, minimal, custom_scene, the cartoons and the
  platform story: 0 (the cartoon examples have no scene labels).
- Tuning: a first version reported 4; "named again in the beat that shows it" removed gallery
  `render` ("A render starts by validating..." before the `Render` stage, whose beat says
  "rendered") and kphi3 `equivalence` (a dense layer discussed a beat before the `Dense layer`
  label, named again with it).
- `unsaid_reveal` (if turned on): 20 beat findings in 365 beats, mostly fine unsaid (a map's
  cities, quote authors, a chapter's subtitle, a terminal's command, a scatter's "diagram"
  cluster, an equation step's "Simplify"); hence off by default.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/lint/narration_rule.py`, `tests/test_narration_rule.py`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/config.py` (`LINT_RULES`, `RuleName`, `SaidBeforeShownRule`,
  `UnsaidRevealRule`, `LintRules`), `src/vidgen/lint/__init__.py`, `src/vidgen/lint/rules.py`
  (`SceneContext.narration`), `src/vidgen/lint/run.py`, `docs/CONFIG.md`,
  `src/vidgen/data/guide/AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `tasklist.md`, `HANDOFF.md`.

Public interfaces
- YAML: `lint.rules.said_before_shown: {min_lead, max_words, severity}`,
  `lint.rules.unsaid_reveal: {max_words, severity}` (default `off`); `lint_ignore` entries
  with these rule names and `object: <label text>`.
- No `vidgen.api` change (lint rules are built in).

Decisions
- Rules on the rendered dump, not on the config/plan: only the dump knows what text is on
  screen for every scene type (project scenes too). The cost is a render, which lint does anyway.
- Nothing within a beat unless an action pins the label's arrival: a beat-end still cannot say
  when in the beat a label came, and guessing would flag the common "named at the start of the
  beat that shows it".
- A label named again when it shows is not reported, trading the "named a beat early but also
  when shown" case for no false positive on words used in passing.

Known gaps (Backlog)
- Stems and stop words for English (and Portuguese stop words) only; a label inside a picture,
  maths or code is not seen; a mention in an earlier scene is not compared; the message cannot
  name the target to reveal (the dump does not know targets).
- Observed, not changed: in `diagram`, a node revealed by an action on a word comes without its
  incoming edge until the scene's next step (scratch project, `{reveal: "node:cache", at:
  "@cache"}`).

How to test
- One file at a time under `capped`: `tests/test_narration_rule.py` (12, 7 s); with
  `test_lint`, `test_timing_lint`, `test_docs`, `test_guide`, `test_config`, `test_terms` (199,
  not render, 10 s); `test_lint`, `test_timing_lint`, `test_json_output`, `test_word_anchors`,
  `test_api` (97, 37 s); `test_schema` (62, capped3g, 122 s): all pass.
- Manual: a scratchpad project (a diagram naming its database early with a node revealed on
  "@cache", a bar race with `sort` and a change on a word, a line chart with a change and a
  cursor, bullets with a callout late in the beat): `vidgen lint` in 16:9 and 9:16 reported
  exactly the database and the callout ("learning rate" 5.9 s before it shows); stills looked at.

## Step 165 — Built-in pronunciation dictionary

What was built
- **Built-in lists** shipped with vidgen (DESIGN §88): `src/vidgen/data/pronunciation/kokoro-en.yaml`
  (every English Kokoro voice, 21 entries) and `kokoro-en-us.yaml` (American voices, +3), in the
  `pronunciation_file` format, each entry commented with misaki's phonemes before and after.
  The list a beat uses follows its effective voice: Kokoro by the language its G2P reads with
  (`kokoro-en-us` for `a` voices, `kokoro-en-gb` for `b`, `kokoro-pt-br` for a dubbed `pf_dora`,
  which has no file), other providers by the video's language (`elevenlabs-en`: no file).
- **Order**: built-in list, then `pronunciation_file`(s), then `pronunciation:`; same term replaces,
  `term: null` removes, the project's rule wins a tie on the same span; a project entry for
  another `language` does not replace the built-in one. Opt-out `pronunciation_defaults: false`.
- **Visible**: `vidgen list-pronunciation [PROJECT] [--json]`; `vidgen validate` line `pronounce:
  built-in kokoro-en-us changes N beat(s): epoch (2), JSON (1) (vidgen list-pronunciation)` and
  JSON `pronunciation_defaults`; no validate warning for built-in entries; `tts --dry-run` adds
  `  (built-in: epoch)` to `says:`, a run `, built-in pronunciation: epoch` to the `generated`
  line, `tts --json` `builtin_pronunciation`; readback / word-flag hints for a built-in entry say
  to write the project's own entry or `term: null`; a term misheard in 2+ beats without an entry
  adds "(other videos with it can share a pronunciation_file)".
- **Audio**: the hash formula is unchanged (spoken text), so only beats whose spoken text a list
  changes go stale; `vidgen tts` regenerates only those (tested). CHANGELOG "Behaviour changes"
  and CONFIG say so, with the way to keep old audio.
- **Entries** (misaki in the Kokoro venv, `fallback=espeak.EspeakFallback`, as `KPipeline` runs
  it; American and British, alone and in sentences): README(s) → readme(s), JSON(s) → Jason(s),
  YAML(s) → yammel(s), ReLU(s) → ray loo(s), RMSProp → R M S prop, neural-api → neural A.P.I. (any
  case), Jupyter → Jupiter, ResNet → Rez net, C# → C sharp, F# → F sharp, BERT → Burt, NaN → nan,
  TeX → tek, tanh → tanch, enum(s) → E num(s) (any case), Cauchy → Koh shee; American only:
  epoch(s) → E pock(s) (any case), VS Code → V S Code. Deviations from the request: README is
  `readme`, not `read me` (misaki reads "read" as ɹˈɛd after "each" and in "read me.md"; `readme`
  is ɹˈidmi everywhere); SGD dropped (misaki already says ˌɛsʤˌidˈi, the same letters as "S G D").
  Full phoneme table in DESIGN §88 and the files' comments.

## Step 167 — Characters moving on an iso place: routes, draw order while moving, facing

What was built
- **Rules** (`vidgen/world/iso_moves.py`, no manim, DESIGN §89.9): `find_route` on the grid
  (8 neighbours; a diagonal only past two free level cells; up or down one step at a time;
  round water, walls, objects (but a bridge or a rug) and, when it can, other characters;
  fewest turns; deterministic), `goal_cell` (a spot or `{column, row}`), `meet_routes` (side by
  side on the picture's level line, the one from the left on the left), `follow_route`
  (`after:` a leader, `gap` cells behind), `wander_route` (seeded), `edge_ways` /
  `entry_route` / `exit_route` (over the place's edge on the picture's `left` / `right`, or from
  / to a spot), `IsoRoute` (feet points; `at()` eases the feet up before a higher cell and down
  after it), `plan_move` (one plan for the render and for validation, from the logical cells) and
  `iso_move_problems` (the replay `vidgen validate` runs). Errors name the beat, the character,
  the goal and where the way stops: `'pip' cannot walk from row 2, column 1 to 'well': the way
  stops at row 4, column 3: water (a bridge crosses it) at row 4, column 4`.
- **The walk** (`cartoon/iso_motion.py`): `IsoWalk(Walk)`, the side walk cycle along the projected
  route, facing left / right by the picture's direction, the front view straight towards the
  camera (when the character has one), no back view; feet on blocks, steps and a bridge's deck
  (`IsoPlace.stand_z`, `ObjectKind.deck`); the shadow follows on the cell top.
- **Draw order while moving** (`Stage._iso_keep_order`, every frame once a walk was applied):
  the pieces over the character's box (`standing_box`: kept inside its cell; on a bridge or rug
  on top of it), its front picture swapped when they change, the characters re-sorted by their
  boxes; Manim redraws characters, fronts and shadows while an `IsoWalk` plays.
  `IsoScenery` (replaces `IsoPictures` / `iso_pictures`) draws the base once and each front
  picture once per set of pieces, cropped to the pieces in whole canvas pixels.
- **Actions**: `walk_to` / `run_to` on an iso place (`to:` a spot or a cell; new `after:` +
  `gap`), new `wander` and `meet`, `enter` / `exit` (`side` / `to` over the edge, `door:` a spot),
  checks (an x, another mark or `depth` on an iso place; `after` / `meet` / `wander` off one;
  bad spots); timing as any action (`at`, `"@word"`), default speeds scaled by `level_pace`
  (iso branch); lint `rushed_animation` covers `IsoWalk`; foley footsteps for `wander` / `meet`.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/world/iso_moves.py`, `src/vidgen/cartoon/iso_motion.py`, `tests/test_iso_moves.py`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/scenes/stage.py` (iso cells and plans, `iso_walks`, `iso_moved`,
  `on_iso`, `_iso_scenery` with `IsoScenery`, `_iso_front`, `_iso_body`, `_iso_keep_order`,
  `_iso_redrawn`, `level_pace`, `_iso_move_problems`), `src/vidgen/scenes/moving.py`,
  `src/vidgen/cartoon/iso_stage.py` (`IsoScenery`, `standing_box`, `body_box` kept in its
  cell, `iso_stand` on the deck), `src/vidgen/world/iso.py` (`deck`, `stand_z`),
  `src/vidgen/api.py`, `src/vidgen/cartoon/foley.py` (`WALKING_ACTIONS`),
  `src/vidgen/lint/timing_rules.py`, `src/vidgen/config.py` (a docstring), `docs/CONFIG.md`
  (iso "Moving"), guide + `AGENTS.md` (action rows), `DESIGN.md` §89.9, `tests/test_actions.py`
  (action lists), `tests/test_iso_place.py` (the pictures test → `IsoScenery`), `tasklist.md`.

Public interfaces
- Config: actions `wander` (`around`, `radius`, `stops`, `seed`, `speed`) and `meet` (`with`,
  `speed`); `walk_to` / `run_to` `after`, `gap`; on an iso place `to` is a spot or `{column,
  row}`, `enter` / `exit` `door` is a spot.

  `IsoWalk`; − `IsoPictures`, `iso_pictures` (Step 166, replaced).

Decisions
- Follow is `walk_to` / `run_to` `after:` because `follow` is the camera's action.
- 8 neighbours, diagonals without corner cutting or climbing; other characters cost more but
  never block (a crowd would jam lanes); a goal someone stands on becomes the cell beside it on
  the picture's level line (not in front of / behind it, where they would overlap).
- `enter` / `exit` on an iso place: over the edge nearest the goal (`left`: the map's west and
  south edges, `right`: north and east), fading over the step beyond; or `door:` a spot (a
  house's door) to fade in / out at. Indoors only an edge door is a way out.
- Planning from logical cells (where everyone stands once planned moves are over), so the render
  and `vidgen validate` agree.

## Step 168 — Staging on an iso place: camera and shots, small things, changes to the place

What was built (DESIGN §89.10)
- **Pictures in tiles at levels of detail** (`cartoon/iso_stage.py`, `cartoon/iso_pictures.py`):
  `IsoScenery` now gives *pictures* (`Picture`: ground or not, pieces with their states): `base()`,
  `front(box)`, `layer(name)`, drawn in 512 px tiles (`tiles`, `tile_image`, LRU cache) on the canvas
  of a level of detail (level k = 2^k × level 0, up to 3; `detail_for(zoom, density)`). On the stage
  each picture is an `IsoTiles` group showing the tiles in the camera's view at the zoom's level,
  swapped by a camera listener and before Manim splits moving/static (`get_moving_and_static_mobjects`:
  after a cut the static image showed the previous view's tiles). `draw_tile` (installed on the
  camera before the light wraps it) resizes only the visible part of a tile into just that part of
  the frame: the test village (50 s with a long follow) went from 239 s to 59 s. `draw_shapes` skips
  shapes off its canvas (`shape_bounds`).
- **Camera**: shots work unchanged on the place (close-ups are sharp: the head at 8× zoom); `wide`
  is the establishing view; `follow` zooms in to a plain stage's character size (`follow_start`,
  `follow_width`, `ISO_FOLLOW_SIZE` 0.45) and tracks up/down (`_MoveThenFollow(y_of=...)`, then the
  stage's `SmoothFollow` as on a level); `pan` to a spot centres on the object there / a character's
  middle, or on its targets, across and up (`pan_point`); `zoom` on a group as anywhere. 16:9 and 9:16
  checked by eye.
- **Small things**: the stage's `props` on an iso place, small ones only (`ISO_ITEMS`; refused: big
  props, depth/lift/against, non-spot `at`, a name clash), standing at a spot on the ground or on a
  table/bench/chair/bed/sofa/rock/well rim (`ObjectKind.top`, `iso_item_point`, `TOP_SPOTS`),
  bodies in the draw order like characters (`item_box`, own front pictures). `pick_up`, `give`,
  `put_down` (no `to`: dropped beside the feet, `iso_put_point`; `to: <spot>`: placed on the object
  there) work; `throw` / `blow_away` refused. New prop `flower`. Reach is checked in cells by the iso
  replay (`iso_move_problems` with `items`, `ISO_ITEM_ACTIONS`, `ISO_REACH` 1), the flat holding
  replay gets no positions on an iso place.
- **Changes to the place**: `ObjectState` (`shown`, `open`, `on`), `object_shapes(..., state)`
  (house door open + windows lit, lamp lit with a pool of light, flowers in bud), room doors in
  standing back walls named `door_1`... (`IsoPlace.doors`) opening into the room; `iso.objects`
  `open` / `on` / `shown`. Actions: `open` / `close` (house, door_n, flowers), `switch_on` /
  `switch_off` (lamp, house), `reveal` (generic, via the object's target entrance), new `hide`
  (`scenes/hide_action.py`, cued). Changed objects are *layered*: out of the base, an `IsoObject`
  group after the base (object + pieces over it); `Stage.iso_change` fades a new layer in by a scene
  updater, sets the state at the start, refreshes fronts/other layers; `_iso_redrawn` redraws the
  layers while a change overlaps an animation. Objects not there are left out of route planning
  (`IsoPlace.without`; render and validate replay with `reveal` / `hide`, `ISO_PLACE_CHANGES`).
- **Fix from Step 167**: a follower ending one cell straight behind (or in front of) its leader on
  the picture takes a step aside (`follow_route`).
- Code move: Step 167's iso methods of `Stage` moved to `scenes/stage_iso.py` (`IsoStaging` mixin,
  `_moving_block`), with this step's.

- Changed: `src/vidgen/world/iso.py` (`ObjectState`, `default_state`, `OPENING_KINDS`,

## Step 169 — Mood, sound and who speaks on an iso place; the iso lint

What was built (DESIGN §89.11)
- **Time of day / weather reuse the stage's keys** (decided: no new mood key or preset): `light`
  (`morning`, `day`, `sunset` = evening, `night`; a tint for a rainy day, documented) and
  `particles` (rain, snow). **Lit things glow**: `Poly` / `Disc` `glow` (lit window glass and core,
  lit lantern faces, the lamp's pool of light); `draw_shapes(glow=True)` draws a picture of the
  lights only (other shapes clear what they cover, so hidden lights stay hidden);
  `IsoScenery.glows`, `tile_image(glow=)`; `IsoTiles` adds `GlowTile`s after its tiles, never
  graded (`light_graded` is a read-only false property). By day no visible change; at
  sunset/night lamps and windows stay bright.
- **Rain on the place**: `IsoRainGround` (`RainGround.landing(shares, x)`; the flat stage's band is
  unchanged), `place_outline` (front/back edge of the place's picture per x), drops land anywhere
  on the ground in view, not beside the place, not on characters (no splashes on faces).
  `puddles` / `settle` / indoor rain refused with alternatives (`iso_particle_problem`). Fixed on
  the way (Step 168 bug): a place change in the first beat before the set's entrance crashed
  (`_iso_insert` now inserts into the backdrop still to come).
- **Sound**: new built-in sounds `step_grass`, `step_gravel`, `step_wood`, `step_stone`;
  `surface_at` / `route_surfaces` (grass, path, boards, tiles, stone, bridge, rug) →
  `PlayedAction.surfaces` → the step per footfall (`SURFACE_STEPS`, `footfall_distances`);
  `handling_cues` (pick_up pop, give swoosh, put_down thud), `place_change_cues` (door creak/thud
  for houses and room doors, a twinkle for a bloom or a `reveal`); lamp click was already there.
  Ambience: new bed `crickets` (auto on an iso place outdoors at `sunset` / `night`; nameable on
  any stage); an indoor iso place gets `room_tone`. All iso-only branches.
- **Name tags** (automatic; `iso.name_tags: false` to turn off): `NameTag` from
  `IsoStaging.speak`, the voice's label in its speaker colour, same size on screen, inside the
  view (16:9 and 9:16 checked), shown while the line's lip sync lasts and the head is under 7.5 %
  of the view's short side; a `say` bubble replaces it (`iso_untag`); removed at the beat's end.
- **Lint**: `hidden_speaker` on iso measures the speaker's eyes-and-mouth box (`features`) against
  the real alpha of the place's tiles in front (`covers` masks written by the layout dump,
  `face_grid`), threshold `min_hidden_features` 0.25, naming the pieces (`the place's lamp`): the
  tree-crown false report is gone, the lamp post across Dot's face (33 %) is reported.
  `small_speaker` skips a tagged speaker with a line of ≤ `max_tagged_words` (12). New rule
  `offscreen_action` (`min_seen` 0.5): each walk, handing action and place change is watched over
  its own frames (`iso_watch`, a self-removing scene updater); the dump's `iso_actions` via a new
  scene hook `layout_keys(beat_id)`.

## Step 170 — The iso example story and the docs of Phase Q

What was built
- **The example** `examples/iso-story/video.yaml` ("Hazel and the Lamp by the Bridge", original
  story and cast): Hazel (a rabbit), Grandpa Rowan (an old bear with a cold) and Juno (a
  bluebird). Morning: the establishing view of Brookfield Green, a `zoom` on Rowan and the lamp
  he lights every evening, Hazel walks to her flower bed (buds), Juno `meet`s her, close-ups for
  their lines, Juno walks over the bridge and `exit`s, Rowan coughs (close-up), opens his door and
  goes in (`open` / `exit door:` / `close`). Evening: the light fades to a rainy tint as the rain
  starts, a `zoom` on the dark lamp, Hazel's worried close-up, a `follow`ed `run_to` to Rowan's
  house and in at its door. Rowan's room (`place: indoor`, sofa, table, rug, shelf, a lit floor lamp):
  Hazel enters over the edge, close-ups and a two-shot, she picks up the lamp key from the table
  and leaves. Night in the rain: she comes out of Rowan's door holding the key, runs to the lamp,
  `switch_on` on "@Click" (zoom on her and the lamp; the lamp and its pool glow), Juno appears on
  the far bank (name tag in the wide view), walks over the bridge to her, two-shots, they walk
  home (`after: hazel`). Next morning: Rowan comes out, Hazel `give`s the key back, three buds
  `open` one by one (zoom), close-ups, a wide ending. The village is a project set
  (`sets: {village: ...}`) for four scenes. Kokoro voices: narrator `bf_emma`, Hazel `af_bella`,
  Juno `af_heart` (speed 0.8), Rowan `bm_george` (0.75); `music: cartoon` at -4; a `short` 9:16
  variant. No audio committed (as platform-story).
- **Voiced and rendered outside the repo** (`<scratchpad>/s170/voiced`, a copy of the example):
  Kokoro `vidgen tts` (38 beats), `vidgen lint` with the audio and the final render (below).
- **Fixes found while making it** (DESIGN §89.12):
  - a thing held by a character that `exit`s (or `enter`s) the place stayed drawn at the doorway
    while its holder faded: `IsoStaging.iso_walks` passes the held props as the walk's `carried`;
  - a walk `to` a spot where someone stands, when no cell beside them could be reached (across a
    stream), ended at the nearest cell the walker could reach, on the wrong bank, and `vidgen
    validate` said nothing: `find_route` keeps the goal within `BESIDE_REACH` (2) cells of the
    character there, else "no way there" (found writing the guide snippet);
  - rain on an iso place looked like a sunny day (the review's note): a scene with `rain` in its
    `particles` and no `light` (its own or its set's) gets `ISO_RAIN_LIGHT` (`#6B7890` at 0.45),
    the tint the docs recommend. Iso only; rain started by the `particles` action keeps the
    light (paired with a `light` action, as the example does);
  - lint `said_before_shown` took a name tag ("Juno", shown while she speaks) for a label and
    reported the narration naming her a beat before she spoke, although she was on screen: name
    tags (the dump's `name_tag` key) are no labels (`narration_rule._label_texts`).
- **Docs**: guide topic `iso` (when to make one, the map, telling a story clearly: shots, voices
  and name tags, moves and their timing, cause and effect, mood; a validated snippet) + topic
  list + `AGENTS.md`; CONFIG iso section (one place in several scenes through a set, the example,
  the rain light, held things, the beside rule) and the stage table's `light` and `iso` rows;
  README feature and example entries; CHANGELOG "Isometric story places (Phase Q)" (0.3.0 now
  Steps 61–170); the Shorts cookbook (an iso place has no `character_size`);
  `docs/gallery/stage.md` params table regenerated with `vidgen gallery --types stage` (it had
  no `iso` rows; its stills and clips left as committed); DESIGN §89.12; tasklist.

## Step 171 — Review of Phase Q

Review of Phase Q (Steps 166–170: the iso world model, projection and drawing, routes, staging,
mood, sound and lint, the example and its docs)
- Fixed, known gaps:
  1. **Wide views left the frame half empty** (the village used about half of a 16:9 frame; in
     9:16 it sat small in the middle): the camera now starts on a *wide view*
     (`iso_stage.wide_view`, DESIGN §89.13) magnified from the whole-place fit until the place
     fills the frame both ways (its diamond tips cut), at most `ISO_WIDE_MAX` 2, but keeping in
     view the characters and small things at their spots (those entering later too) and, in a
     landscape frame, every spot and every `iso.objects` object whole (a roof is never cut; the
     map's trees and bushes may be cut at the edges; a room keeps all of itself). `shot: wide` is
     that view (`IsoStaging.iso_wide_shot`), `camera_at` moves it across. The world's scale is
     unchanged, so close shots, `follow`, the tiles and every measure are as before. The
     village: 1.21x in 16:9 (it spans the frame's width), 2x in 9:16.
  2. **`pan` did nothing on the whole-village view**: on an iso place a pan to a spot or a
     character moves in to at least `ISO_PAN_ZOOM` (2) times the whole place
     (`IsoStaging.pan_width`).
  3. **Characters stayed dark in a lamp's light at night**: `LampLit` on each character and
     small thing of a place with a lamp; `StageLight` grades them with `lamp_lit` (warm, up to
     `LAMP_LIFT` 0.6 of the way to the lamp's grade, scaled by how dark the light is: nothing by
     day), by the feet's distance from each lamp (`ISO_LAMP_REACH` full within 1 tile, none
     beyond 2.2) and the lamp's level, which fades with its switches; asked when drawn (no scene
     updater, so waits stay cheap).
  4. **A larger flower bed drew one clump**: `flowers` and `bush` (`BED_KINDS`) draw a clump with
     its shadow in each cell of their footprint (a bed's clumps alternate its colours); 1 x 1 as
     before.
  5. **A bare `on: true` failed the JSON Schema check**: `schema._yaml_on_key` adds a `"true"`
     property beside every boolean `on` (props and iso objects), as JSON writes YAML 1.1's key.
- Decided and documented (CONFIG "Moving", the guide, DESIGN §89.13): **closed doors do not
  block walks** (a room's doors are drawn closed and every way in goes through one; `open` a
  house's door before going in); **two walkers at the same time do not avoid each other**
  (routes go round standing characters; walkers are drawn in the order of their boxes; time
  crossing walks apart, or `meet`).
- Found by this review: a 9:16 room scene's `enter` was off screen once the wide view kept only
  the characters already there (lint `offscreen_action`): the view keeps the entering
  characters' spots too.
- Error messages for AI authors (read through `vidgen validate` with 14 typical mistakes): a
  `jump` to a place on an iso place now says `walk_to or run_to it` (it named a platform level);
  `size` / `character_size` names the shots; `on` / `open` on flowers reads "not flowers"; two
  objects on one cell say to move one. The others (unknown spot, an x as a goal, `depth`, `level`
  with `iso`, an unknown symbol or object, a big prop, `switch_on` a well, a pan to an unknown
  spot) name the problem and the alternative already.

## Step 173 — The `iso_diagram` core

What was built (DESIGN §90.6–90.7, CONFIG `iso_diagram`)
- A presentation scene type `iso_diagram`: blocks in the isometric view of the iso places —
  `box`, `slab`, `cylinder`, `database` (a cylinder with two bands), `tile` (a flat platform) —
  on a grid (`at: [column, row]`, `size`, `height`) or arranged in the order written
  (`arrange: auto | row | column | grid | zigzag`, `spacing`); a block with `layers` (bottom up)
  is a stack (`gap`, `label_side`); `groups` put a plate under their members; `edges` are
  connectors along the grid (`"a -> b: label"`, `-->` dashed, `style: pipe`, the scene's
  `edge_style`), straight, with one turn, or round the front of what is in the way, their tips
  stopping where they meet the target's outline as seen (`hidden_run`). Floor (`grid`, `plain`,
  `none`) under everything, following a zigzag's steps.
- Labels flat and readable: on a block's top when they fit (ink chosen by contrast), else on a
  plate above / below / right / left, placed greedily against other labels, block faces and
  connectors; stack layers in a column at the side with leader lines; connector labels beside
  the connector; sizes from `size` down to the readable minimum, never below. The diagram is
  fitted to the body by bisection on the tile width; a warning when blocks come out small or it
  does not fit.
- Colours: a block's `color` (a layer's, else its stack's), else the colour of a `terms:` term
  its label says, else `block_color` (`palette` by default); faces shaded as on the iso place,
  outlines a darker shade of each block (`outline_ink`), plates tinted by the group colour.
- `arrange: auto` is a row in 16:9 and a `zigzag` (two picture columns, spacing 2) in 9:16: the
  only direction of the 2:1 view that runs down a tall frame.
- Steps: the whole diagram in the first beat (floor and plates, blocks back to front, then the
  connectors); targets `heading`, `block<N>`, `block:<id>`, `stack:<id>`, `group:<id>`,
  `edge:<from>-><to>`, so `reveal` / `dim` / `highlight` / `zoom` already work on it.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/iso_blocks.py` (model, routing, shapes; no manim), `src/vidgen/iso_vector.py`
  (iso shapes as Manim mobjects), `src/vidgen/scenes/iso_diagram.py`, `tests/test_iso_diagram.py`,
  `docs/gallery/iso_diagram.md` and its four media files.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/api.py`, `src/vidgen/scenes/__init__.py`, `docs/CONFIG.md` (section and
  targets row), `src/vidgen/data/guide/AGENTS.md` + `AGENTS.md` (chooser row, a snippet under
  "flows": the gallery sample), `docs/gallery/README.md`, `examples/gallery/video.yaml` (scene
  `arch`), `tests/test_actions_coverage.py`, `tests/test_builtin_scenes.py`,
  `tests/test_translation.py` (samples of the new type), `CHANGELOG.md` (0.3.0 now Steps 61–173),
  `DESIGN.md`, `tasklist.md`, `HANDOFF.md`. Nothing in `cartoon/` or `world/` changed.

  `layout_iso_diagram`, `DiagramShapes`, `diagram_shapes`, `outline_ink`, `readable_ink`,

## Step 174 — `iso_diagram` actions, label placement, lint

What was built (DESIGN §90.8–90.11, CONFIG `iso_diagram` / "Iso diagram actions", lint table)
- Eight actions on `iso_diagram` scenes, timed like any action (`at: 0.5`, `at: "@word"`):
  `build` (`style` grow / drop / fade: blocks grow up from the floor, a stack layer by layer, or
  drop or fade in; the scene's own steps leave what it names to it; a connector comes in once
  both its ends are there), `raise` (`by`) / `lower` (with a shadow on the ground; a raised layer
  lifts the layers above, a group its plate and caption), `explode` (`gap`) / `collapse` (a
  stack's layers apart and back, side labels going along), `flow` (`count`, `style` dots /
  packets, `color`, `back`, `chain`: dots or small cubes along connectors, on top of pipes),
  `focus` (`padding`, `scale`: the camera onto a part and staying; `focus: diagram` back) and
  `relabel` (`text`: a label or value morphs into a new one in place; the scene keeps room for
  it). Each refuses another scene type and targets of the wrong kind, naming them.
- `dim` and `highlight` keep a block's shading (a generic hook `Target.recolor`; a dimmed block
  stays opaque, mixed towards the background); a highlighted label is coloured text on its plate.
- Params `build: together | each` (one block or stack per step over the beats), `entrance: drop |
  grow | fade` (the scene's steps and `reveal`), `portrait_grid: auto | keep`; a stack's
  `label_side: below`; a target `diagram`.
- The three problems in Step 173's stills, fixed: (1) labels are now placed by the blocks'
  outlines, not boxes — right by their block, clear of other blocks (with a little room), labels,
  pipes and connectors, else pushed clear with a leader line; group captions go first, by the
  plate's front edges, with the plate's blocks as obstacles; connector labels beside the
  connector along its longest run (leader when pushed off); (2) one label per block: a stack of
  one layer is labelled once (its layer's label, else the stack's), a caption that repeats a
  layer's label is not drawn; (3) in 9:16 a stack lists its layers under it with colour swatches
  (`label_side: auto`) and may be drawn 1.35× larger (Step 173: 0.93 units a tile, now 2.5); an
  `at` grid is slanted down a 9:16 frame when that draws it larger (`slant`).
- Lint `iso_labels`: from geometry the scene adds to each still of the layout dump (labels,
  block and plate outlines, connector paths in pixels): a label over another block, over another
  label, hiding another connector, or far from what it names without a leader. Size and contrast
  stay `min_font`'s / `contrast`'s.

## Step 178 — Bug fix: a block shown at full before it grows in

The bug (owner, `<scratchpad>/s177/open_a_web_page.mp4`): "When a block is meant to grow in, it
appears at its final full size for a split second, then jumps back to tiny and grows." Seen frame
by frame: the Browser at full size with its label from 10.833 s to 11.200 s (12 frames), then an
empty floor at 11.233 s, then the growth; the same for the load balancer, the app servers, the
cache, the "HTML response" slab during the crossfade into `render` and the Rendering stack.

Root cause (DESIGN §90.15)
- `IsoDiagram._arrivals` plays what comes with a block first (the floor piece under it, a
  group's plate, at a scene's start the heading) and then the blocks, in a `Succession`. Manim adds
  the mobjects of every non-introducer sub-animation to the scene when the `Succession` starts, but
  begins (first interpolates) each sub-animation only when its turn comes. `GrowBlock` was not an
  introducer, so the block stood in the scene at its final look until the fade before it ended,
  then its `begin()` hid it and it grew. `drop` / `fade` and connectors use `FadeIn` (an
  introducer) and were not affected.

Fix
- `GrowBlock` is an introducer (`scenes/iso_motion.py`): the block joins the scene when its growth
  starts, unseen and flat on that frame. Covers every timing and target (beat start, `at:`,
  `@word`, `build: each`, the first beat's steps, `reveal`, block / stack layers / group / diagram).
- The same class on an iso place (Step 168's changes, `scenes/stage_iso.py`), found with a scratch
  render (`s178/stage_reveal.py`): when a change started, the other pictures showing the object
  (the layer of an object behind it, a character's front picture) were swapped at once, so a
  revealed pine showed at full on its first frame over the lamp behind it; also a picture made
  mid-play was not drawn until the next animation, and one removed mid-play stayed in Manim's
  moving list and was drawn on (a hidden pine came back at full; a closed door's open leaf stayed
  until the beat's end). Now: `_iso_follow_change` puts each new picture right under the old one
  (`_IsoFollow`; new fades in during the first half, old fades out over it in the second; a lone
  picture fades with the change), `_iso_follow_on` continues a fade a second simultaneous change
  starts from, `_iso_refresh_layers` redraws an object fading in by its own change at its current
  opacity, new pictures join the moving list and `_iso_undraw` takes removed ones out of it.
  `_iso_swap_front` is the front swap `_iso_keep_order` used inline (`keep=` for the follow).

Files touched
- `src/vidgen/scenes/iso_motion.py`, `src/vidgen/scenes/stage_iso.py`; new
  `tests/test_step178.py`; `DESIGN.md` §90.15, `CHANGELOG.md` (0.3.0 now Steps 61–178),
  `tasklist.md`, `HANDOFF.md`. No public interface change (`vidgen.api` unchanged).

Tests (`tests/test_step178.py`, 7, all render at tiny sizes)

## Step 185 — Instrument library and effects

What the owner agreed (Phase S plan): the beds' building blocks as named, adjustable instruments,
track effects and movement, `vidgen music patches`; the format must be able to express what
`momentum`, `ascent`, `horizon`, `beacon` and `neon` do (Step 186 re-creates the 14 beds).

What was built (DESIGN §93.4, §93.7)
- `studio/instruments.py`: 26 instruments in six families (drums, noises, basses, plucks and
  keys, leads, pads), each wrapping a `vidgen.music` function (no code moved, `music.py`
  untouched). New: `gated_snare`, `tick` (`_clock`), `pulsar` (`_pulsar_pulse`), `static`
  (`_static` for its held steps; sine fade-in / cosine fade-out so back-to-back holds join at
  constant power; stereo), `analog_bass`, `square_pluck`, `pizzicato`, `music_box`, `woodblock`,
  `soft_lead` (new synthesis: 1/h^1.5 harmonics, 5 Hz vibrato fading in, cosine release; Step
  181 had left `_soft_lead` out of `music.py`), `saw_pad` (`_SOFT_SAW`), `glass` (beacon's
  shimmer); `sub` gains `second` / `third`; pads gain `detune` (was a fixed width) and `fade`
  (was the fixed 1.6 s chord cross-fade). Drums may return stereo. `Instrument.width_cents` is
  gone (now the `detune` setting); `Instrument.group` is new.
- `studio/effects.py`: `Curve` (number, `{from, to}` ramp over the section, `[[bar, value], ...]`
  points; frequencies interpolated in octaves), `Duck`, `Gate`, `Echo`, `Reverb`, their
  YAML parsing (shorthands `duck: kick`, `gate: "x.x."`, `echo: true` / a delay, `reverb: true`
  / a mix), the `EFFECTS` catalogue, and the processing (`smooth`, `swept_filter`, `echo`,
  `reverb`, `widen`, `duck_dip`, `gate_window`).
- `score_file.py`: track / section keys `spread width lowpass highpass duck gate echo reverb`,
  `volume` may be a curve; `none` / `off` / `false` / `null` switches an effect off in a section;
  `duck.to` checked against the tracks (did-you-mean, not itself, or `beat`); `score_outline`'s
  tracks list their `effects`.
- `render.py`: a track with a bus effect renders onto its own buffer(s) — one per (echo, reverb)
  setting, so each section's notes get their own and the tails carry over — then filters, gate,
  ducking, volume curve and width along the piece; a track without is summed straight into the
  mix exactly as in Step 184. `spread` alternates the pan by step. Notes outside 20 Hz–12 kHz
  (also `play: chords` tones, which were not filtered before) are left out and described in

  (no sub) is byte-identical (loop and one-shot); `skyline_lift` changes slightly (true peak

  a chord every 7.5 s).

## Step 187 — Analysis: vidgen music check

What the owner agreed (Phase S plan): `vidgen music check <score|wav>` — a report in words and
JSON (loudness and steadiness, true peak, clipping, tempo vs the score, loop-seam click,
voice-range share, bass weight, harsh highs, section energy), a spectrogram with section marks,
a demo under a narration sample with default ducking, plain-language advice naming score keys
(tracks rendered separately), `--compare`; limits calibrated so the 14 beds pass and bad scores
are flagged.

What was built (DESIGN §93.9)
- `studio/check.py`: `check_music_score` (plays the score track by track), `check_music_audio`
  (any audio, measured at −28 LUFS, 2 s blocks for bars), `MusicCheck` (verdict, facts, findings
  `{topic, level ok/note/fix, text, fixes}`, sections, tracks), `music_check_text`, `check_dict`,
  `compare_rows` / `compare_text`, `LIMITS` (each with the beds' range in a comment), the
  narration demo (`load_narration`, `speech_spans`, `duck_gain_db` = `mix.duck_curve` with
  `DuckConfig()`'s numbers, `narration_demo`, `add_demo`) and the picture
  (`spectrogram_image`: one row per piece, section marks, voice-band lines, a per-bar voice-range
  lane against the limit). Advice computes, from the tracks' shares, the fewest tracks to lower
  and by how many whole dB, written as the score change (`` `kick.volume: -5` (now 6) ``,
  `` `piano: sections: {main: {volume: -1}}` (−5 dB) ``), plus another way (octave, tone,
  lowpass, decay, master lowpass); lifts / builds / unsteady pieces name tracks quieter where they
  should not be.
- `render.render_music_stems(score, on_stem)`: each track on its own canvas handed to a callback
  (before the master filter and level), the mix as `render_music_score` (within 1e-5), and the
  final gain. `render_music_score` is unchanged.
- `src/vidgen/studio/data/narration_sample.mp3` (package data, `pyproject.toml` `studio/data/*`):
  20 s, two original lines by Kokoro `af_heart` (Apache-2.0), −21.5 LUFS as stereo
  (`<scratchpad>/s187/make_narration.py`). Decision: a real voice (Kokoro's licence allows
  shipping) rather than speech-like noise — the voice-range clearance is only meaningful with
  speech.
- `vidgen music check SCORE|AUDIO [--narration FILE] [--compare OTHER] [--out DIR] [--json]`
  (`cli._music_check`, `jsonout.music_check_document`, action `check`): writes
  `<name>-check.png` (or `<name>-vs-<other>.png`) and `<name>-demo.mp3` (each piece's) to `--out`
  (default `.`), prints the report, the comparison table and the time taken.
- `vidgen.api`: `MusicCheck`, `check_music_score`, `check_music_audio`, `music_check_text` (§6.4).
- Docs: DESIGN §93.1, §93.2, §6.4, new §93.9; CONFIG "Checking a piece" (+ JSON table); README
  commands row; CHANGELOG (0.3.0 now Steps 61–187); tasklist. Guide and `AGENTS.md` unchanged
  (the recipe comes with Step 188's MCP tools).

Calibration (`<scratchpad>/s187/calibrate.py`, `out/calib-*.json`): the 14 beds as audio and
their 14 templates as scores, plus `tidewater` and `skyline_lift`: no finding above `ok` for any
of the 30. Ranges → limits in DESIGN §93.9 (e.g. loudest voice-range bar −35.0 … −27.2 dB
(`lullaby`) → −26; highs up to −34.8 dB (`bright`) → −30; build / lift by loudness or
brightness, since `ascent`'s lift is only +0.3 dB louder but +1.9 dB brighter). Dropped: the 50 ms
level step across the seam (a downbeat makes it jump 5–12 dB in clean beds). Bad scores
(`<scratchpad>/s187/bad/*.yaml`, `run_bad.py`): each is flagged for its own fault only — voice

Known gaps / for later steps
- 188: MCP tool for the check; the author-guide recipe (template → change one thing → check →
  compare → a human listens).
- The key check is per section (not per chord); a lift is compared with the section just before
  it; audio files have no sections; no psychoacoustic masking model (the per-bar voice-range level
  and the demo's clearance stand in).

  lint rule row and config, MCP tools; README (music bullet, MCP list, list-music row); DESIGN

Decisions
- Names: a suffix-less source that is not a bed is a piece name (`assets/music/<name>.yaml` /
  `.yml`, sub-folders with `/`), unless it is an existing file under the project (stays a file,
  as before); `.yaml` / `.yml` sources are the path form.
- A bed's name that is also a project piece is a problem (validate and render), not a silent
  precedence: rename the piece or use the path form.
- A `loop: false` piece always plays once (the cue's `loop` cannot repeat an ending); a loop piece
  with the cue's `loop: false` plays one pass.
- Cache key = the file's bytes + `PIECE_RENDER_VERSION` + `vidgen.__version__` + rate (the
  version alone does not move between steps, so bump `PIECE_RENDER_VERSION` when the studio's
  sound changes); cached as `.npy` (exact float32, so a cached join equals a fresh one).
- The lint rule reports only what matters under a voice by default (voice range, highs, bass,
  steadiness, peaks, loop seam); key / sections / tempo are opt-in topics (musical choices).

Compatibility
- Mixes byte-identical before / after (`<scratchpad>/s188/mixcompare.py`, run with HEAD's `src`
  from `git archive` and with this step's): `gradient-descent` and `iso-web-page` (`bright`),
  `host-explainer` (composed `curious`), and a project with a music file then `momentum`.

  skyline 9 s); no disk cache (the beds have none; `ascent` takes 17 s). The shipped YAML data

## Step 191 — Review of Phase S

What was reviewed and fixed (DESIGN §93.13)
- **Module boundary**: `studio` imports no video code, but the test only imported the package's
  `__init__` (not `check`, `templates`, `measure`, `patches`). It now imports every module and is
  an allow-list: `music`, `sfx`, `loudness`, `errors` and what they pull in (`config`, `languages`,
  `textnorm`, `voicesounds`, `word_anchors` — through `music`'s cue settings; noted in §93.2).
- **Holds across sections** (Step 184's gap): a track's steps may start with `-`, holding on the
  note sounding as the section starts (or round a loop's end); it keeps its section's sound. Was
  a parse error, so no score changes. Checked: a hold into a section changes nothing against the
  same note in one section; "- - C5 -" is "C5 - - -" shifted. A leading `-` where the track rested
  before, or at a one-pass piece's start, is a problem naming the section.
- **Ducking by level** (Step 185's gap): `duck: {follow: true}` (default false, as before).
- **Filter sweeps** (Step 185's gap): the copies run in up to four threads and add only where
  their weight is not 0 — bit-identical to the old loop (tested); skyline 9.1 → 7.9 s on two
  cores (`swept_filter` 3.9 → 2.3 s). Not done: anything inexact (block-wise filtering) — the
  owner approved `skyline` sample for sample.
- **`vidgen music check`** (Step 187/189 gaps; `CHECK_VERSION` 2, cache `piece-<key>-check2.json`):
  per chord, each audible pitched track's share on the key's or the chord's notes (a `key` fix
  under 25 %: track, chord, bar, the notes off it); the first section of a loop compared with the
  last; a note when a lift stays 1 dB under an earlier section; lift advice no longer suggests a
  riser, a boom or a part that only plays in builds (Step 189's bad advice); build advice measures
  a riser that is there (dB under the rest, how far to raise it). Calibration
  (`<scratchpad>/s191/calibrate.py`, `calib3.json`): the 16 templates, the piece, both test
  demos, the five cookbook sketches and Step 189's v1–v9: no new finding; worst part per chord
  0.39 (`skyline`'s bass) – 0.99; the bad scores (`s187/bad`, new `s191/bad/bad_chord`,
  `bad_break`, `bad_riser`) flagged as meant (bad_chord's bell 0.006; bad_break's note and advice
  without the riser; the riser "39 dB under"). A riser still measures little at its normal level;
  `bad_riser`'s build passes on +1.08 dB of brightness from the chord cycle (the build limit is
  near the beds' own swing; not changed).
- **A cue's `section`** (Step 188's gap "pieces cannot follow the video"; decision: a section
  start, not re-timing a written piece): `music: [{source: theme, to: setup}, {source: theme,
  from: results, section: lift}]` lands the lift on `results`. Pieces and the two score beds;
  other sources and unknown sections are problems with did-you-mean.
- **Lint `music_check` on the part played** (Step 188's gap): `played_bars` from the video plan,
  `start` / `section`, loop; findings about a seam never crossed, sections never reached or loud
  voice-range bars never played are dropped; messages name the bars played.
- **Names** (Step 188's gap): `vidgen music render` / `check` / `--compare` and MCP
  `music_render` / `music_check` take a project piece's or a bed's name (a code bed rendered or
  checked as its audio).
- **Step 189's caption offset — a real bug** (not music, not `stat`): `narrate` rounded the time
  left in a beat, the plan rounds the beat's window; on a window of x.5 frames they differ by a
  frame when the beat's animations took an odd number of frames (banker's rounding). Kokoro lines
  of whole frames + 0.35 s pad at 30 fps hit it; `gps-time-of-flight`'s intro, orbit and timing
  ran a frame short (captions 0.1 s early after them, the overlay warning). Fixed in

  Step 100 item (ticked). `<scratchpad>/s191/plan_vs_render.py` on a copy of the example
  (`s191/gps`, those three scenes re-rendered at 1080p): every beat and scene now equals the plan,
  no warning, 88.80 s (the README's 88.7 s is Step 189's render). Behaviour change (CHANGELOG):

## Step 193 — vidgen studio: architecture and skeleton (Phase T starts)

What was built (DESIGN §94)
- **The plan for the whole phase**: tasklist Phase T (Steps 193–201) and DESIGN §94 — modules,
  server and guards, sessions and versions on disk, the JSON API including the calls Steps
  194–199 will add (§94.5), the render cache and Step 196's stem plan (§94.6), versions / undo /
  A/B (§94.4: the score text is the source of truth; controls change one value in place via
  `yaml.compose` marks so comments survive), how MCP reaches an open session (§94.8: through the
  disk — `open.json` and a session `inbox/`, not HTTP), variations (§94.9).
- **`vidgen studio [PROJECT] [--port N] [--no-browser]`** (`cli.cmd_studio`,
  `studio_app.run_studio`): a standard-library `ThreadingHTTPServer` on 127.0.0.1 (a free port by
  default; `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` on Windows; a port in use is a clear `VidgenError`), opens the
  browser with `webbrowser`, Ctrl+C stops it and removes `open.json`. Checked as a real process
  (`<scratchpad>/s193/cli_run.py`): address printed, `/api/info` answered, SIGINT → "studio
  stopped", exit 0, `open.json` gone.
- **`StudioApp`** (`studio_app/app.py`, no HTTP): presets (the 17 beds with a one-line
  description ≤ 110 characters, their use, and the templates' facts), patches, `load` (preset or
  text → a new session, version 1), `validate` (problems as `{where, message, line}`: the
  score's did-you-mean messages, the line found from `where` with `yaml.compose`; YAML syntax
  errors with their line), `score`, `render` (whole or one section; cached by
  `render_key` = SHA-256 of the YAML data + `STUDIO_RENDER_VERSION` + vidgen version, so comments
  do not re-render; a 16-bit WAV at +12 dB = the Listen page's −16 LUFS for every version; a
  section is cut bit-exact from the whole render), `audio_file` (names checked by pattern).
- **`StudioServer`** (`studio_app/server.py`): routes, JSON envelope `{ok, result|error}`, static
  files and three bundled fonts from allow-lists, audio with single `Range` requests (206 / 416),
  guards (Host must be 127.0.0.1 / localhost with the port; POST must be JSON and same-origin; 2
  MB bodies; CSP `'self'`, nosniff, no-referrer), dropped connections ignored.
- **Sessions** (`studio_app/session.py`): `<project>/build/studio/` or `studio/` in vidgen's
  cache folder; `sessions/<id>/session.json`, `versions/v0001.yaml` (text as written),
  `renders/`; `open.json` (url, session, pid) while running.
- **The page** (`studio_app/static/`, package data; vanilla ES modules, no build, no CDN):
  top bar (preset picker as a listbox with key / tempo / length and the one-line description;
  A/B, versions, undo / redo, Export disabled with their step in the title; YAML toggle; theme
  toggle), song strip (key, tempo, time, seed, bars and length, the progression as written, the
  chord names of the section under the playhead), transport (play / pause, stop, loop (whole),
  "under narration" disabled, seek slider, time), timeline (coloured sections sized by bars,
  playhead, click to seek), tracks (name, instrument, volume bar, pan knob, steps text; M / S
  disabled), inspector (instrument words, plays, sections, effect chips, settings as disabled
  sliders at the written / default values), the score file highlighted with line numbers
  (problem lines marked), check panel placeholder and status line. The page auto-loads
  `momentum` when no session is open; a reload keeps the open piece.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/studio_app/__init__.py`, `app.py`, `server.py`, `session.py`,
  `static/index.html`, `studio.css`, `app.js`, `api.js`, `player.js`, `yaml_view.js`,
  `favicon.svg`; `tests/test_studio_app.py` (20), `tests/test_studio_ui.py` (3, marker `ui`).
- Changed: `src/vidgen/cli.py` (the `studio` command), `src/vidgen/sfx.py` (`wav_bytes`;
  `write_wav` writes its bytes — the same file), `src/vidgen/render/fingerprint.py`
  (`studio_app` in `NOT_RENDER_INPUTS`, so scene caches stay valid), `pyproject.toml` (package

## Step 194 — vidgen studio: song strip, timeline and track list

What was built (DESIGN §94.12)
- **Edits in place** (`studio_app/edits.py`): `set` / `delete` / `insert` / `rename` on the
  score's text by path (`tracks.bass.volume`, `sections[2].bars`), found with `yaml.compose`
  marks, so one value changes and comments and layout stay (a missing key is added by its
  siblings; a quoted string keeps its quotes). Built here rather than in 195 because every
  control of this step edits.
- **Song edits** (`studio_app/song.py`): add a track (default pattern per instrument and time
  signature, `volume: -6`), delete a track, add / remove / rename a section (references in
  `only`, `rest` and per-section changes follow; a track that plays only in a removed section
  goes with it, named in the label; a new section takes the chords before it when there is no
  score progression, and is a rest for tracks with per-section steps only).
- **Chords as Roman numerals with names for every template** (`song.roman_numeral`,
  `analyse_progression`): the 14 Python beds' `{chord, notes}` voicings now show numerals too;
  each section's own progression is in the outline and shown when the loop or playhead is in it.
- **`POST /api/edit`** (`StudioApp.edit`): every committed edit is a version (`origin: edit`,
  parent the version edited, a label); problems write nothing (`{ok: false, problems}`);
  `dry_run` for live checks. `POST /api/render` takes `mute` (a listening mix: the other
  tracks' stems at the whole mix's gain, `<key>.m<tag>.wav`). Renders carry `energy` (LUFS per
  bar; `STUDIO_RENDER_VERSION` 2).
- **The page** (new `strip.js`, `timeline.js`, `tracks.js`; `app.js`, `player.js`,
  `yaml_view.js`, `index.html`, `studio.css` changed): key (tonic + mode), tempo and seed
  edited in place; chord chips (numeral, name, the one playing lit), click to type, names live,
  problems inline; transport loop select (whole or a section); timeline with section names (click
  = loop it, again = whole), drag a right edge for bars (or arrow keys), energy curve, playhead,
  a sweep while rendering; a section bar (rename, bars, own chords / the score's, loop, add
  after, remove); track rows with a meter, M / S, a volume bar, pan knob, steps edited in place
  with the problem under the row, delete; `[+ track]` instrument menu (two columns, by kind). The
  YAML view flashes the lines an edit changed. Player keeps the piece's time across sources
  (`offset`), so a re-render, a loop switch or a mute continue at the same moment.

Decisions
- Mute / solo are a listening aid only (the page's state sent with renders), never written to
  the score; exports (197) render the score as written. Making it permanent = delete the track
  or lower its volume.
- Section loops play the section file cut from the render with `<audio loop>` (no Web Audio).
- Meters are rough, computed from the score's steps (gain, accents, holds, volume) under the
  playhead; Step 196 replaces them with stem RMS.
- Removing a section removes tracks that play only there (labelled; the earlier version keeps
  them) instead of refusing — refusing blocked every template with lift-only parts.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/studio_app/edits.py`, `song.py`, `static/strip.js`, `static/timeline.js`,
  `static/tracks.js`; `tests/test_studio_song.py` (15).
- Changed: `studio_app/app.py` (edit, mute mixes, energy; `describe_score` moved to `song.py`),
  `server.py` (`/api/edit`, `mute`), the static files above, `tests/test_studio_app.py` (the
  progression is now `{text, written, chords}`), `tests/test_studio_ui.py` (+3 flows),
  `DESIGN.md` (§94.12, §94.5 table, §94.2 / §94.7 module lists), `tasklist.md`.

Public interfaces
- None in `vidgen.api`. The page's HTTP API grows (`/api/edit`, `mute`, `energy`); still internal.

## Step 195 — vidgen studio: inspector, step grid, the score file typed

What was built (DESIGN §94.13)
- **Inspector** (`static/inspector.js`): instrument picker (a dry run explains what the change
  keeps, drops or moves into range, then [Change to …]); "Edit for" the whole track or one
  section (writes `sections: {s: {...}}`; the section's own values in its colour, the track's
  otherwise, ↺ back); **Sound** sliders generated from the catalogue (units, log scale for
  frequencies, default tick, typed values, reset, help line on hover / focus) plus volume and
  pan; **Notes** (octave, transpose, accent; a pad's play mode chords / steps); **Steps** (the
  grid); **Effects** chips (echo, reverb, duck to a track or beat with follow, gate with its own
  step pattern, lowpass / highpass / width / volume curves as fixed / ramp / points with a
  drawing, spread; off in one section and back); **Per section** table (plays switch via
  `rest` / `only`, the changes there, clear, edit).
- **Step grid** (`static/stepgrid.js`): the steps text read with the patterns' tokens into bars
  of cells (bars of different step counts line up in time), beat groups, accent dots, holds
  drawn; a cell edit replaces only its characters in the text; brushes, drag-paint (one
  version), keys (a burst = one version), + / − bar, steps per bar (resampled), a text field
  live both ways, the step under the playhead lit.
- **The score file typed** (`static/yaml_edit.js`): transparent textarea over the highlighted
  text; checked 0.3 s after typing (bad lines marked, problems listed with line links and the
  CLI's did-you-mean), valid for 0.8 s → a version (`POST /api/text`), the controls follow; a
  draft with problems is never a version, dims the editing controls, [Revert to vN].
- **Server**: `edits.unset` (removes a key and the mappings it empties, `keep` parts kept);
  `studio_app/inspector.py`: `studio_catalog` (units, scale, integer), `change_instrument`,
  `set_play_mode`, `set_section_plays` as ops `change_instrument`, `play_mode`,
  `section_plays` of `/api/edit` (its answers carry `notes`); `StudioApp.text`; the outline's
  tracks carry `spec` (the track as written).

Decisions
- Units come from the settings' words (the catalogue has none); `music patches --json` stays as
  it was (the studio decorates a copy). Instrument settings are never "integer" (the catalogue
  writes 2600.0 as 2600).
- A grid edit rewrites only the cell's characters (the text's spacing and `|` stay); resizing a
  bar rewrites that bar only.
- A typed text with problems blocks the other controls (instead of being overwritten by them).
- A field edit on an inherited effect in a section copies the track's effect into the section
  (an effect in a section replaces the track's whole, as the score reads it).

## Step 196 — vidgen studio: fast re-render, playing on, under narration, meters

What was built (DESIGN §94.14)
- **Stems in the renderer** (`vidgen.studio.render`): `render_track_stem` (one track alone, as
  the piece plays it), `mix_track_stems` (sum in order, master filter, level measured on the
  mix — or a listening mix at the whole's gain and length, a one-shot's tails kept; `threads=2`
  runs the filter's channels and the loudness's blocks in threads, bit for bit the same),
  `TrackStem`, `MixFacts`; `render_music_stems` built on them. `render_music_score` unchanged.
  Small additive helpers: `music._level_gain` (`_finish` takes a gain), `loudness.measure` /
  `integrated_loudness` take `threads`.
- **Stem cache** (`studio_app/stems.py`): keys of exactly what a track hears (shared song data,
  its spec, a duck's trigger's hit inputs, renderer and vidgen version); in memory, LRU past
  768 MB, room made before rendering; a plain-volume change scales a kept stem; each stem's
  power per 50 ms for the meters. `StudioApp.render` mixes from it and reports `timing`;
  mute / solo remix kept stems (one-shot tails kept, Step 194's gap closed).
- **Late facts**: loudness, true peak and the energy curve after the answer, one worker that
  gives way to renders (`GET /api/facts`); the page dims the last curve meanwhile.
- **Under narration** (`studio_app/narration.py`, `render {narration: true}` → `….n.wav`): the
  shipped narration sample repeated over the piece, the music ducked with the check's
  `duck_gain_db`, at a video's balance, one gain for every version (voice true peak −1.5 dBTP).
- **The page**: `player.js` brings a new source in on a second `<audio>` seeked ahead and
  cross-faded at the same moment (no gap; measured offset within ±10 ms); the "under narration"
  checkbox works; meters from each stem's audio (`meters` per 50 ms); the status line says what
  was rendered ("pad rendered + remixed in 1.6 s", "bass at the new volume", "listening mix").

Decisions
- Exactness: the remix differs from `render_music_score` only in float addition order (plain
  tracks' notes go straight into the piece there): ≤ 4.7e-10 measured on the 17 templates and
  edited scores, test tolerance 1e-9, the 16-bit audio identical. Keeping the exact order would
  need every overlapping note in memory (280 MB for tidewater's arp); changing
  `render_music_score` instead would have moved 1–2 samples of three templates by a float32
  step (a hard-rule break). Checked byte for byte against the code before the step: every
  template render, the stems mix, the warnings (`<scratchpad>/s196/compare_old.py`).
- Stems in memory, not on disk (float64 needed; ~370 MB a version). Tracks render one at a
  time (two heavy tracks at once reached 2.8 GB). Section-only render not built (§94.14).

  `slow`).
- Changed: `studio/render.py`, `music.py` (`_level_gain`), `loudness.py` (`threads`),

## Step 198 — vidgen studio: listening notes and "Ask an agent"

What was built (DESIGN §94.16)
- **Listening notes** (`studio_app/notes.py`, session `notes.json`): pinned while playing or
  paused by the N key, **+ note**, or a click on the new notes lane under the timeline; each
  records seconds, bar, beat, section (and bar within it) and the version heard. Pins on the
  lane (section colour; hollow when resolved; a dot when an agent answered), an editor popover
  (Enter keeps, Esc closes; ▶ from here, resolve, delete) and a **Notes** tab next to the score
  file (in the piece's order; ▶ plays from 1.5 s before; ✓ ✎ ×; the agents' lines under each).
  Notes carry over to every version: placed at the same bar of their section, so a longer or
  shorter section before them moves them with the music; a shorter or removed section moves
  them to the nearest bar; `moved` says so in words.
- **Ask an agent** (`studio_app/agent.py`): `POST /api/ask` writes the hand-off
  (`request.json`: score, open notes placed in the base version, its kept check as text and
  findings, the parent → base diff, the instruction, the reply format) and returns it as a
  prompt. Answers: (a) MCP tools `studio_sessions`, `studio_read`, `studio_check`,
  `studio_propose` in `vidgen mcp` (through the disk: validated proposals go to the session's
  `inbox/`; the page polls `GET /api/session?since=R` every 1.5 s and they appear);
  (b) **Copy prompt** / **Paste reply** (any chat assistant; `parse_reply` reads the ```yaml
  block, `n1: …` lines and `summary:`); (c) optional **OpenRouter** (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from
  the environment as vidgen's other OpenRouter providers, model on the page or
  `VIDGEN_STUDIO_MODEL`; disabled with how to set the key when missing; Send asks to confirm the
  cost).
- **Proposals** (`proposals.json`): a valid, changed score becomes a version `agent: <summary>`
  that is not made current; the banner above the tracks shows it with one line per note,
  **▶ A/B vN vs vCurrent**, **Keep** (current + resolves the notes it answered) and **Discard**
  (renamed `discarded · …`; never deleted). Invalid answers (problems, unchanged, no score) are
  shown with their problems and can only be dismissed. Nothing ever overwrites a version.

  `tests/test_studio_agent.py` (11).

  paste, send, decide; `info.provider`), `server.py` (routes), `session.py`
  (`add_version(current=)`, `revision`, `touch`), `checks.py` (`kept_check`), `mcp_server.py`

  `studio_propose`; environment variable `VIDGEN_STUDIO_MODEL`; the page's API rows of §94.5.

Decisions
- Notes belong to the session and are placed per version by section + bar-in-section (the
  musically stable anchor), not by seconds or absolute bar.

## Step 199 — vidgen studio: variations

What was built (DESIGN §94.17)
- **Variation operators** (`studio_app/variations.py`): pure, deterministic functions of the parsed
  score giving `edits.py` value edits (comments and layout kept) and a label in words, in four
  kinds — harmony (re-voice the written voicings, substitute one numeral by a relative in the
  key, first inversion, another seed), pattern (the figure — busiest pitched non-bass track —
  turned 1–3 steps, re-accented 3+3+2 ↔ 4+4+2+3+3..., degrees swapped, hat ghost notes / soft
  hits out), mix (darker / brighter: master low-pass, pads' tone, hat level; lead forward /
  back), energy (sparser first section, stronger lift, drums building in / pad breathing in
  one-section pieces). Never tempo or key. `make_variations(text, shuffle, first)` picks one of
  each kind that changes something (others' next ones when a kind has none); shuffle is a
  counter turning each kind's candidate list.
- **Batches** (`VariationBatches`, `variations/b0001/{a..d}.yaml, batch.json`): one worker renders
  the four (kept stems reused; no late facts), then checks them on a second `Checker`; progress
  in the document. **Keep** → next version (`origin: variation`, parent the version varied,
  label `variation: …`); "more like this" varies a candidate (its kind first, the chain of labels
  kept); un-kept candidates never become versions. `/api/render {variation: "b0001/c"}` plays a
  candidate like a version.
- **Page** (`static/variations.js`): Variations button; a panel of four cards (kind colour,
  label, verdict + headline numbers, mini spectrogram, what was rendered), ▶ Play / ■ back at the
  same moment (badge "▶ variation b · …"), Keep, More like this, Shuffle, progress and timings.
- **MCP** `studio_variations` (`agent_variations`): the four as whole scores with labels, nothing
  written.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/studio_app/variations.py`, `static/variations.js`, `tests/test_studio_variations.py` (22).
- Changed: `studio_app/app.py` (second checker, batches, `make_variations` / `variation_batch` /
  `keep_variation`, `render(variation=)`, `_render_whole(late_facts=)`), `server.py` (routes),
  `static/app.js`, `api.js`, `versions.js` (badge for a candidate, `variation` origin shown),
  `index.html`, `studio.css`; `mcp_server.py` (tool, instructions); `tests/test_mcp.py` (tool list,
  a call), `tests/test_studio_ui.py` (+1); guide + `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` (MCP tool list),
  `docs/CONFIG.md`, `DESIGN.md` (§94.17, §94.1/.5/.7/.9), `tasklist.md`.

Public interfaces
- None in `vidgen.api`. MCP tool `studio_variations`; the page's API rows of §94.5 for Step 199.

Decisions
- Variations are value edits of the text (not a re-generated score), so they keep comments and
  read as a small diff; tempo / key are never touched (slow FFT lengths, every track re-rendered).
- Un-kept candidates are not versions (not even "discarded" ones): the version list stays the
  person's history; the candidates remain on disk in the batch folder.
- Keep's parent is the batch's root version, also for "more like this" chains (the label carries
  the chain).
- A second `Checker` for batches so the current version's check and a batch's never cancel each
  other; renders all four before checking so all are playable after ~7 s.

Timings (two cores; `<scratchpad>/s199/shots.py`, `smoke.py`)
- momentum, from the click: first card playable 3.5 s, all four 6.5–7 s, all checked 19–20 s
  (renders: re-voiced 1.7 s — every track —, ostinato 0.5 s, darker 1.5 s, stronger turn 0.6 s;
  checks 2.7–3.8 s each). More like this / shuffle ~20 s. tidewater: renders 4.9 s, checks 20 s.
  Making the four (operators + validation) 0.1–1.7 s per template.
