## Step 225 — Units and the `calculation` scene

What was built
- **Quantities engine `vidgen/quantities/`** (no manim, stdlib only; DESIGN §97.9). Decision: an
  own engine, not pint (pint lacks exact fractions through a chain, school significant-figure
  rules and TeX of each step, and would be a dependency to keep in step on Windows).
  `units.py`: dimensions as seven `Fraction` exponents, a unit table (SI base / derived with
  prefixes, min h d yr, L M (mol/L) t Da u, eV cal Wh, Å au AU ly pc, atm bar mmHg Torr, deg ° % ppm
  sr, `c` for GeV/c², °C / °F with offsets), exact factors where defined exactly, `parse_unit`
  (`m/s^2`, `km h^-1`, `kg·m²·s⁻²`, `J/(mol·K)`, `m^(1/2)`; offset units must stand alone;
  did-you-mean), `Unit.text` / `.tex`, `si_unit` (named derived units: J, N, Pa...; J·s; base
  units otherwise), `describe_dim` ("energy (kg·m²·s⁻², J)"). `constants.py`: SI 2019 exact (c, h,
  ħ, e, k_B, N_A, R, σ), CODATA 2022 (G, m_e, m_p, m_u, ε₀, μ₀), g_n, au (IAU 2012), IAU 2015 nominal
  GM☉, GM⊕, R⊕, and M☉ / M⊕ from them; TeX, meaning, source, aliases. `quantity.py`: `Quantity`
  (SI value, Fraction while exact, `sig` or exact), `written` (values as authors write them;
  exactness rules), `count_sig`, arithmetic with dimension checks and significant figures (products
  fewest, sums by resolution, functions keep), exact roots, `decimal_text` (half away from zero,
  plain vs scientific like the plot core, no ambiguous trailing zeros), `fraction_text`,
  `in_unit` (offsets keep their resolution). `expr.py`: the mathexpr grammar as a tree (plus
  `2 [m]` unit literals), `evaluate` on quantities, `to_tex` (brackets by precedence, products of
  symbols side by side, × for values, `stack` on two lines). `calc.py`: `work(symbols, calcs,
  wrap, lenient)` → `Worked` / `CalcResult` (value, steps formula / substitute (4 variants) /
  intermediate / result / convert, used names, conversions, warnings), `name_tex`.
- **Scene `calculation`** (`scenes/calculation.py`, DESIGN §97.10): symbol table beside the work
  (16:9) or above it (9:16; two columns when short), one calculation at a time aligned at `=`,
  per-line sizing with the substitution variant chosen for readability, result box, conversions,
  results joining the table when the next calculation starts, concept colours on symbols,
  `from_scene` results of other scenes (`resolve_imports`), validation of everything at params
  time (imports at `vidgen validate`). Actions `substitute`, `compute`, `convert`
  (`scenes/calculation_actions.py`); `reveal` of a line; `highlight: "symbol:G"`.
- Docs: CONFIG section `calculation`, targets row, actions row; guide chooser row, snippet
  (gallery sample), action rows, copied to `AGENTS.md`; gallery entry `calculation` (16:9 GIF 86 KB,
  9:16 104 KB; gallery 12.6 MB); `examples/gallery` scene `half_life`; DESIGN §2, §6.4, §97.9,
  §97.10; CHANGELOG; tasklist.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/quantities/{__init__,units,constants,quantity,expr,calc}.py`,
  `src/vidgen/scenes/{calculation,calculation_actions}.py`, `tests/test_quantities.py`,
  `tests/test_calculation.py`, `docs/gallery/calculation.md`, `docs/gallery/media/calculation-*`.
- Changed: `src/vidgen/api.py` (module `quantities`), `src/vidgen/scenes/__init__.py`,
  `docs/CONFIG.md`, `docs/gallery/README.md`, guide + `AGENTS.md`, `examples/gallery/video.yaml`,
  `DESIGN.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `tasklist.md`; test lists in `test_builtin_scenes.py`,
  `test_actions_coverage.py`, `test_actions.py`, `test_translation.py`, `test_registry.py`.

Public interfaces: `vidgen.api.quantities`; scene type `calculation`; actions `substitute`,
`compute`, `convert`. No config key, no dependency.

Decisions
- Own engine instead of pint (above). `mathexpr` unchanged: calculations need a tree (one parse
  for evaluation and every TeX line), so `quantities.expr` reuses its grammar.
- Exactness by how a value is written: fractions and unitless whole numbers exact; numbers with
  units or decimals measured (`532 nm` has 3 figures, `1500 m` 2); `exact` / `sig` override.
  Numbers inside formulas are exact. Constants are shown to 4 figures, used in full.
- Symbols must be listed (a constant too) so the table shows every value with its source; an
  unlisted constant's name in a formula gets "add {name: G, constant: G}".
- One calculation on screen at a time; earlier results move into the table (readable on phones,
  no scrolling stacks). Long substitutions: with units if large enough, else on two lines, else
  SI numbers without units (the table has the units).
- Actions are named after the step (`substitute`, `compute`, `convert`); "show" is the built-in
  `reveal` (a new generic action name `show` would clash with everyday words in other scenes).
- Phase U / V worked-number cards (Hardy–Weinberg, pedigree risk) are left as they are
  (compatibility); new worked numbers use `calculation`.

Compatibility
- Phase Q baseline after the shared change (`api.py`): 31 frames, max difference 0
  (`phase-q-baseline/check225`). Existing scenes untouched.

Known gaps: the narration / on-screen number lint is Step 226 (`Params.worked(project)` and
`CalcResult.warnings` are ready for it); no ± uncertainty propagation; adding two absolute
temperatures is not refused; a long formula is shrunk or stacked, never broken at `=`; a short
beat with a calculation change can be "rushed" for lint (the previous calculation leaving and the
next formula share the first step).

## Step 226 — Lint for calculations and plots

What was built (DESIGN §97.11)
- **Ten lint rules** (scene scope, last in `LINT_RULES`, configurable in `lint.rules`):
  `calc_numbers` (`tolerance` 0.05), `calc_units` (`tolerance`), `calc_sigfigs` (info),
  `plot_units`, `plot_log`, `plot_errors`, `plot_series`, `plot_truncated` (info),
  `plot_conserved` (`tolerance` 0.01), `plot_fit_claims` (`sigmas` 2, `tolerance` 0.05). Each
  message quotes the sentence (or names the series / axis / fit / model) and gives the fix.
- **Knowledge** `vidgen/quantities/accuracy.py` (no manim): numbers in digits and words
  (strict whole-number grammar, "point" decimals, "times ten to the minus nineteen", ordinal
  fractions "forty-nine fiftieths", "three halves", shares "one person in twenty-six"), their
  resolution (trailing zeros allow at most a tenth), significant figures, "about" / bounds /
  ranges; units spoken ("kilometres per second", "metres per second squared", "an hour", "per
  hour", "degrees Celsius") or in symbols via `parse_unit`, "in kilograms" as the sentence's
  unit; `agrees` (SI, "about" = rounding to 1–2 figures or tolerance), `mixup_power` (10^(3k));
  `dimension_claims` ("a speed of 30 kilometres"); `fit_quantities` / `fit_claims` (half-life,
  lifetime, rate, doubling time, exponent, slope, intercept, centre / mass, σ, width, capacity,
  midpoint, mean, custom parameters; errors propagated); `error_meaning_claims`.
- **Glue** `lint/calc_rule.py` (candidates: every calculation scene's symbols and results,
  `worked(project)`; which value a number refers to — DESIGN §97.11; screen texts of any scene:
  title, caption, text, lines, bullets…, plot notes, callout labels) and `lint/plot_rule.py`
  (the plot resolved with its CSVs and models; `bar_chart` baselines). Both add to
  `SceneContext.science` like the science / genetics rules.
- **Narration–picture rules**: `fit`, `annotate`, `grow`, `substitute`, `compute`, `convert`
  are showing actions; `Plot.target_text` (series, named fits, annotation texts, title) and
  `Calculation.target_text` (`row:` / `symbol:` → "meaning · source", title).

YAML (nothing new to write; what the rules read)
```yaml
- id: orbit
  type: calculation
  params:
    symbols: [{name: G, constant: G}, {name: M_sun, constant: M_sun}, {name: r, constant: AU}]
    calculations: [{name: v, expr: "sqrt(G*M_sun/r)", sig: 3, convert: km/s, meaning: orbital speed}]
  beats:
    - text: "The Earth moves at about thirty kilometres per second."   # fine; "thirty-five": calc_numbers
lint: {rules: {plot_conserved: {tolerance: 0.005}, calc_sigfigs: {severity: off}}}
```

## Step 228 — Review of Phase W

What was done (DESIGN §97.13): a critical review of Steps 222–227 against numpy / scipy, with
fixes, and the known gaps decided.

Findings and fixes
- **Histograms dropped values** (bug): with `bins: N` (and a rule with `nice_bins: false`) the
  12-digit cleaning of the edges could move an outer edge past the smallest or largest value, which
  then fell `outside` (most samples of 50 random values with 7 bins; a 20-bin density differed from
  numpy by 16 %). `plotcore/hist._cover` keeps the outer edges at the data's ends.
- **Counts fitted with √N weights were biased** (accuracy): weights from the observed counts
  (Neyman's χ²) pull a decay towards low counts — λ 0.47 σ high on average for the example's data
  (300 simulated sets). New `fit_curve(..., poisson=scale)`: least squares re-weighted with the
  fitted curve's variance until it settles = Poisson maximum likelihood (the score equations hold;
  errors from the Fisher information; χ² is Pearson's). The `plot` scene uses it for a series with
  `y_err: sqrt` (counts ≥ 0) and for curve fits to histograms (density: the per-bin scale); a 0
  count no longer raises "a y error of 0". Normalized residuals of such fits use σ = √fit.
- **RK45** stepped onto every output time (2401 calls for 400 samples; scipy 716): now steps follow
  the error control and samples come from the dense output (scipy's interpolant `_P`): 709 calls,
  the same error as `solve_ivp`. `simulate_ode` scales the absolute tolerance by the largest initial
  value (a 10⁻⁷ mol/L model was integrated to an absolute 10⁻⁹).
- **Temperatures** (gap of 225): `Quantity.temperature` marks readings in °C / °F (`"point"`) and
  their differences; adding two readings is refused, a difference cannot be shown in °C / °F
  (result `unit` or `convert`). Values are unchanged (kelvin arithmetic was right).
- **Equal aspect**: both axes tick with the larger step inside the equal-aspect loop
  (`figure._common_step`; the scale stays equal — test_plot's render check).
- **Residual panels** (the example's was hard to read): normalized panels symmetric about 0,
  ticked at ±2 (new `AxisSpec.ticks`), points without bars (each is ±1 by definition).
- **Lint**: intermediate calculation lines keep their evaluated parts (`Step.values`); the lint
  takes them as unnamed candidates (a number said for one agrees; never blamed).
- **Calculation hand-over**: the leaving calculation takes `LEAVE_SHARE` = 0.5 of a step (its slow
  fade read as a ghost behind the next formula).
- Checked and fine: lines / polynomials / Gaussian / logistic / power fits and their errors vs
  `curve_fit` (≤ 1e-5), bands vs the textbook formulas (1e-15), binning rules vs numpy, ML
  distributions vs `scipy.stats`, quantiles and χ² tail (1e-9), x errors vs `scipy.odr` (0.06 σ:
  the effective-variance approximation, documented), SplitMix64 reference sequence, every constant
  vs `scipy.constants` (CODATA 2022), unit factors.
- Module boundaries: `plotcore` and `quantities` import only `errors` / `mathexpr` (no manim,
  scipy or scenes); `quantities.accuracy` (lint knowledge) pulls the pure-Python cellworld /
  genetics packages for three sentence helpers — noted, not moved.

The example: λ = 0.274 ± 0.004 min⁻¹ (χ²/ν 0.77) by Poisson likelihood; the `half` scene now 0.274
min⁻¹ → t½ 2.53 min, σ 0.041 min, z = 0.5 ("about half a standard error away"); three beats
re-voiced with Kokoro (counts_b4, half_b1, half_b3); README, cookbook and the guide's science snippet
updated to the same numbers.

Files touched
- New: `tests/test_science_review.py` (15).
- Changed: `src/vidgen/plotcore/{fit,hist,integrate,models,axis,figure}.py`,
  `src/vidgen/quantities/{quantity,expr,calc}.py`, `src/vidgen/lint/calc_rule.py`,
  `src/vidgen/scenes/{plot,plot_parts,plot_figure,calculation}.py`,
  `examples/radioactive-decay/{video.yaml,README.md}`, `tests/test_radioactive_decay.py`,
  `docs/CONFIG.md`, `docs/COOKBOOK-SCIENCE-CHARTS.md`, guide + `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md` §97.13,
  `CHANGELOG.md`, `tasklist.md`.

Public interfaces (additive): `plotcore.fit_curve(poisson=)`, `AxisSpec.ticks`,
`quantities.Quantity.temperature`, `quantities.Step.values`. No config key, no dependency.

Decisions
- Poisson likelihood by default for counts rather than an option: it is the correct fit for
  Poisson data, and √N weights are a known bias; `weighted: false` still gives an unweighted fit.
- Temperature marks only on values written in °C / °F: a value in K may be a temperature or a
  change, so averages in K work and nothing written in K is refused.
- Normalized residuals without error bars (pulls), ticks at ±2 only (0 has its dashed line).
- Kept as gaps (§97.13 table): SI fallback for a single factor wider than the frame,
  `label_size: caption` for crowded 16:9 fit figures, one progress per rescaling panel, no zoom on
  broken axes, the 9:16 fit-box room, `bar_chart` / `line_chart` value labels unchecked, the
  domain plots of §97.12.

## Step 232 — Many bodies

What was built (DESIGN §98.6):

- **Model** `vidgen.orbits.threebody` (no manim): the circular restricted three-body problem in
  normalised rotating units — L1–L3 from Szebehely's quintics (`numpy.roots` + Newton), L4 / L5,
  `ROUTH_MU` = 0.0385209 / `routh_stable`, the effective potential, the Jacobi constant (from the
  rotating frame or from inertial positions about the barycentre), zero-velocity curves
  (vectorised marching squares), the rotating-frame equations on Phase W's RK45, co-orbital
  angles and kinds (tadpole L4 / L5, horseshoe, passing), `Restricted` with presets `earth_moon`,
  `sun_earth` (Sun + Earth–Moon barycentre, 1 AU), `sun_jupiter`. `vidgen.orbits.manybody`: the
  figure-eight (scaled to a mass and length), barycentres and binary shares, nearest period
  ratios, the Laplace angle, conjunctions by root finding, `bends_toward`, tidal acceleration and
  the equilibrium tide. The Galilean moons as body / orbit presets; masses as `'2 Msun'`; n-body
  runs record the angular momentum and give velocities; `simulate(initial=)`.
- **Scene** `orbit`: `system` (a pair integrated as n-body about the barycentre, RK45 by default;
  or `figure_eight`), `view: inertial | rotating` and the actions `corotate` / `inertial`
  (smooth turn over `run_time`), `lagrange`, `zero_velocity`, bodies `near: L1…L5` with `shift` /
  `drift` (rotating frame), `origin: barycentre` (binary stars draw both ellipses), `resonance`
  (ratios, Laplace angle, conjunction lines and counts), bodies' `curvature`, `center` + `extent`
  close-ups with a pointer to the off-plot central body, `tides` (its own schematic layout: pull,
  centre pull, tidal arrows with the enlargement factor, bulges, the near side; "schematic: not to
  scale"). Panel rows: μ, Routh, the frame shown, L1 / L2 distances, Jacobi constant and ΔC/C,
  the angle ahead of the secondary and the co-orbital kind, the figure-eight's return, a binary's
  mass ratio, ΔL/L.
- Performance of the panel (orbit scenes, output unchanged): the cached row texts are drawn in
  place and their points restored (copying every row each frame dominated long renders: a Trojan
  scene went from 100 s to 55 s, the tides 56 → 24 s); trails wholly inside the plot skip the
  per-segment clipping.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/orbits/{threebody,manybody}.py`, `src/vidgen/scenes/{orbit_systems,orbit_many}.py`,
  `tests/test_orbit_many.py` (31 incl. 2 renders).
- Changed: `src/vidgen/orbits/{__init__,bodies,nbody,values}.py`, `src/vidgen/scenes/{orbit,
  orbit_parts,orbit_overlays,orbit_actions}.py`, `docs/CONFIG.md` (orbit section, param table,
  targets row, actions row), the guide + `AGENTS.md` (chooser row, two snippets, a paragraph, two
  action rows), `DESIGN.md` §98.6, `tasklist.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Public interfaces (additive): in `vidgen.api.orbits` the names of `threebody` (`integrate` as
`integrate_restricted`, `potential` as `restricted_potential`) and `manybody`,
`GALILEAN_PERIODS`, `GALILEAN_PHASES`; `NBodyRun.angular / angular_scale / angular_drift /
angular_error / velocity`; `simulate(initial=)`; the `orbit` params, targets and actions above.
No dependency, no config key.

Decisions
- The restricted problem is drawn from an inertial n-body run (massless bodies), not from the
  rotating-frame equations: one integrator path for every view, the switch between frames is a
  view transform (`OrbitModel.turned`, angle from the run's own secondary), and leapfrog stays
  available (symplectic only in the inertial frame). RK45 is the default with a pair: leapfrog's
  fixed step blows the Jacobi constant up at a close pass (seen: ΔC ≈ 12 above Routh's limit);
  the rotating-frame RK45 integrator in the model serves the tests and authors' own scripts.
- `sun_earth` uses the Earth–Moon barycentre's GM (the usual pair for L1 / L2): L1 / L2 at
  1.4976 / 1.5077 million km — the brief's "≈ 1.5 million km" verified.
- The Galilean moons are defined by their published sidereal periods (a from Kepler III with the
  `jupiter` preset's system GM; within 0.03 % of the published distances), circular and at phases
  giving the Laplace angle 180°: the conjunction geometry (Ganymede 90° away at each Io–Europa
  conjunction) is exact in this model. **For the owner to check**: the satellites' GM values
  (quoted as JPL JUP310: 5 959.916, 3 202.739, 9 887.834, 7 179.289 km³/s²) and the sidereal
  periods' last digits; the figure-eight digits are Simó's as commonly quoted, and verified here
  by integration (back within 10⁻⁶ AU after T).
- `tides` is an `orbit` param, not a new scene type (a new type needs a gallery entry; the gallery
  is at its budget until Step 235).
- `center` is the body's position halfway through the span (a symmetric close-up of a path).
- The rotating frame's words are in the panel; the plot carries only a small turning arrow.

Compatibility: no shared code changed (only the orbit scene and the `orbits` package), so the
Phase Q baseline was not re-run; the 229–231 orbit tests pass unchanged (the panel's in-place
texts draw the same points).

Known gaps: n-body with burns (refused); forbidden regions drawn as their boundary; the tidal
bulges do not lead (no spin, no friction) and the Sun's tide is not shown; the Moon's
concave-path close-up is honest but subtle at true scale (the panel row carries the claim); a
9:16 panel with a pair is long (two columns, smaller text); LEO scenes still hide a low orbit under
the true-scale Earth (231's note; not addressed here); a lint warning mid-turn (a trail over the
L2 label while the frame turns); gallery media (Step 235).

## Step 233 — The Solar System on a date

What was built (DESIGN §98.7):

- **The compact side panel first** (reviewer: 232's panels had 10–15 rows of tiny text). Every
  panel row (`Slot`) has a `name` and a `rank`; `choose_rows` keeps rank 0, then ranks 1 / 2 in the
  scene's order up to 6 rows (16:9) / 5 (9:16) besides the "not to scale" notes, never a
  diagnostic, every row at least the label size, one column. `panel: compact` (default) | `full`
  (the old panel) | `none` | a list of row names (`PANEL_ROWS`, did-you-mean). ΔE/E, ΔL/L, the
  Jacobi drift and the figure-eight's return error are diagnostics (`energy: true` brings ΔE/E and
  ΔL/L back); `Orbit.diagnostics(params)` gives them to the lint (Step 234) whatever the panel shows.
  The 229–232 scratch projects were re-rendered (s232 16:9 dark and 9:16 light, s231, s230 16:9)
  and lint clean (s232's old mid-turn warning is gone too); the tides note is shorter in compact.
- **Model** `vidgen.orbits.ephemeris` (no manim): Standish's Table 1 (J2000 values and rates per
  century for Mercury … Neptune and Pluto; source and validity in the docstring), Julian dates,
  validity checks (1800-01-01 to the end of 2050, start and end), mean elements on a date,
  heliocentric ecliptic positions (the document's method), longitudes, distances, elongations,
  sidereal and synodic periods, `next_event` (opposition, conjunction, inferior / superior
  conjunction, aligned: root finding on the wrapped longitude difference) and `events_between`.
  The planet presets now read their J2000 values from `TABLE1` (one copy); `preset_on`; Pluto as a
  body and orbit preset (`kepler_planets` stays the eight planets).
- **Scene** `orbit` (`scenes/orbit_sky.py`): `date`, `event`, `radial: log`, `inset`, `sizes`
  (its own picture); targets `event`, `inset`, `rings`; the panel's `date`, `event`, `distance`,
  `synodic` rows.

Files touched
- New: `src/vidgen/orbits/ephemeris.py`, `src/vidgen/scenes/orbit_sky.py`, `tests/test_orbit_sky.py` (35).
- Changed: `src/vidgen/orbits/{__init__,bodies,laws}.py`, `src/vidgen/scenes/{orbit,orbit_parts,
  orbit_overlays,orbit_manoeuvres,orbit_many}.py`, `tests/test_orbit.py` (3 assertions on panel rows:
  `energy: true`, `panel: full`, a row list), `tests/test_orbit_many.py` (the Jacobi row is now a
  diagnostic), `docs/CONFIG.md` (panel paragraph, Step 233 section, params, targets row), the guide +
  `AGENTS.md` (chooser row, two snippets, two paragraphs), `DESIGN.md` §98.7, `tasklist.md`,
  `CHANGELOG.md`.

Public interfaces (additive, one visible default): `vidgen.api.orbits` gains the `ephemeris`
names (`longitude` as `ecliptic_longitude`, `distance` as `planet_distance`, `SOURCE` as
`TABLE1_SOURCE`), `planet_preset`, `preset_on`, the `pluto` presets; `Orbit.diagnostics`; `orbit`
params `panel`, `date`, `event`, `radial`, `inset`, `sizes`. Visible change: orbit panels are
compact by default (ΔE/E hidden unless `energy: true` / `panel: full`).

Decisions
- Ranks are chosen per scene by what it is about (a transfer's Δv rows always; Routh's test only
  when L4 / L5 matter; the legend last); the budget leaves out lower ranks rather than shrinking text.
- Events by heliocentric longitudes (equal or 180° apart): the same instant as the geocentric
  opposition in longitude and monotone at the synodic rate, so bracketing is robust. Published
  dates come out within hours (Mars 2020-10-13 23:24 TT vs 23:20 UT published; 2022-12-08 05:32 vs
  05:36).
- The Earth's longitude at an equinox is 180° of date; Table 1's frame is J2000, so the tests
  subtract the precession since 2000 (50.29″/yr) — that is why 2020's raw value is 179.72°.
- From the date the planets move on two-body Kepler orbits from the date's elements (consistent
  with every other orbit scene); over a year they stay within 2 × 10⁻⁴ AU of Table 1's positions
  (tested). Non-Table-1 presets with a date must be placed with `nu` / `mean_anomaly` (the Moon's
  position on a date is not modelled).
- `inset` reuses the flyby's side-box slot; the inner planets and the Sun are named in the inset,
  not at the crowded centre of the main picture. `sizes` is an `orbit` param, not a new scene type
  (the gallery budget, as for `tides`).
- Values **for the owner to check**: Table 1's numbers were entered from memory of the document and
  verified indirectly (the equinoxes, eight published event dates within hours, the sidereal year
  365.2564 d, synodic periods 779.94 / 583.92 / 398.88 d) — Pluto's rates and the slower planets'
  rates are the least exercised by the tests; Pluto's GM 975.5 km³ s⁻² (system) and radius
  1 188.3 km. (Fetching JPL's table file https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/txt/p_elem_t1.txt to compare was
  not permitted in this session.)

Compatibility: shared code untouched (only the orbit scene files and `vidgen.orbits`), so the
Phase Q baseline was not re-run. Existing orbit scenes render the same picture with a shorter
panel (the deliberate change above); `panel: full` gives the previous panel.

Known gaps: the Moon / satellites on a date; Table 2a; light-time, aberration, the equinox of
date; greatest elongations; in 9:16 a true-scale picture with an inset is small (the inset takes
the room under it); gallery media (Step 235).

  `orbit_period`, `orbit_speed`, `orbit_dv`, `orbit_transfer`, `orbit_distance` (tolerance 0.05),

  atmosphere, an undeclared-atmosphere flyby, n-body bodies within their radii' sum.

  `event`, `barycentre`, `face`, `motion` (`orbit_manoeuvres.burn_text`, shared with the drawing).

  the Sun" — s233 — speaks of distances and is right), and only when the bodies are surely enlarged
  without running the layout (7 units per reach is more than any layout's scale).

## Step 236 — Review of Phase X

What was done (DESIGN §98.10): a critical review of Steps 229–235 with fixes — a physics-accuracy
pass against independent calculations, the reviewer's points (picture size, units in substitutions,
render speed, known gaps), compatibility.

Findings and fixes
- **Physics** (scratchpad `s236/physics_check.py`, 133 checks; the lasting ones in
  `tests/test_orbit_review.py`): Kepler's equation (bisection, e 0–0.999999 and 1.000001–10, Barker),
  Vallado's COE2RV and the `from_state` round trip, propagation against DOP853, vis-viva, Hohmann
  LEO → GEO and Earth → Mars, bi-elliptic thresholds and Δv, plane changes, the flyby's turn, v∞ and
  periapsis against an integrated hyperbola, the Sun-frame gain and energy change, L1–L3 by root
  finding for four μ, L4/L5, Jacobi constants, Routh's μ, Sun–Earth L1/L2, the figure-eight returning
  after T, the Galilean ratios and Laplace relation, Table 1 positions against Standish's method
  written here, 14 published opposition / conjunction dates 2018–2027 (all within 0.48 d), every
  constant and preset against its cited value. **No physics error found.** Noted: Kepler III from
  Table 1's a gives 365.2578 d for the EMB, the table's mean motion 365.2564 d (independent fits).
- **Render speed / memory** (the reason Step 235 rendered at 720p): every new readout string built a
  manim `Text` (~20 ms) and the panel's caches kept it plus a deep copy with its SVG path objects
  (~0.3 MB each): memory passed 3 GB and the worker was killed (exit −9). New
  `scenes/orbit_text.LiveText`: a string laid out once per shape (digits as 0), the real digits from
  glyphs rendered once, following glyphs shifted by advances and pair kerning — equal to `Text` to
  10⁻⁷ units (tested); plain `VMobject` glyphs; the panel text cache bounded (`TEMPLATE_CACHE` 256,
  points kept on the mobject); the plate built once; the panel measured with the same glyphs. The
  title, caption and axes lie below the clock's mobject (`STILL_Z` −2 < `CLOCK_Z` −1), so manim draws
  them once per play into its static image. `hohmann` 1920×1080 in-process: 179.9 s, 129 ms/frame,
  ≥ 1.5 GB → 99.3 s, 71 ms/frame, 0.81 GB; via `vidgen render`: `straight` 90.5 → 59 s, `hohmann`
  killed → 105 s; the whole example at 1080p in ~6½ min.
- **16:9 picture size**: the caption stands in the side column under the panel (left-aligned, ≥ 4.4
  units wide; under the picture when the column has no room); the picture takes the height under the
  title (61 % → 69 % of the frame height in the example). **9:16**: a transfer's Δv₁ / Δv₂ rows are
  rank 1 in portrait (the burns' labels carry them): two rows fewer, the picture ~25 % taller.
- **Units in substitutions** (`quantities.calc`): `Step.common` / `common_stacked` — every value in
  the result's unit, the unit once at the end, `(√(2.945² + 10.93²) − 7.726) km/s` — when all values
  with units share the result's dimension (or the result is a pure number: `common_bare`, then it
  ranks with the SI numbers so readable full-unit lines are not replaced). Order: full units (one
  line, two, per factor), common unit, SI numbers.
- **Gaps fixed**: the orbit lint reads digit groups with spaces ("384 400 km", thin / no-break too);
  the phase angle's label keeps off its own lines and the central label, its lines start at the
  central body's edge, in the highlight colour at 0.6 (they were "dim" like the gridlines, which the

  vertex; a G-parity violation only moves a hadronic decay from strong to electromagnetic with a
  note ("slow"). Not checked: parity, orbital angular momentum, CKM suppression, FCNC, colour.

  Higgs `secondary` — `highlight` stays free for the actions.

  minus); every symbol carries an (invisible) bar so the flip morphs like into like.

## Step 238 — Feynman diagrams

What was built (DESIGN §99.5–§99.6): Feynman diagrams in proper notation, with every vertex checked
against the Standard Model, as a model (`vidgen.particle_physics.feynman`, `.feynman_layout`, no
manim) and the scene type `feynman` with the actions `travel`, `vertex_rule`, `swap_channel`.

First, two fixes from the review of Step 237:
- τ(Λ) corrected to the PDG 2024 average (2.617 ± 0.010) × 10⁻¹⁰ s (2.632 before; Λ̄ follows, it
  is built by conjugation); m_W 80.3692, m_Z 91.1880, Γ_Z 2.4955, m_H 125.20 GeV are confirmed and
  no longer marked `# check` (DESIGN §99.2 updated; a test pins the values).
- `test_builtin_scenes.py::test_builtins_use_only_the_public_api` passes again: `orbit_text.py`
  imports through `vidgen.api` (which exports `plot_draw`), and `calculation.py` — which also
  broke the rule (`from vidgen import registry`, since Step 231) — uses the new
  `vidgen.api.find_scene_type` (= `registry.find`).

The step:
- **Model** `feynman`: `Diagram` / `DiagramLine` (a particle running forward in time `from` →
  `to`: vertex ids, `in`, `out`; spectator quarks `in` → `out`), `HadronGroup` (quark lines
  bracketed as n, p, π⁺…, content checked), `build_diagram` (structure errors), `vertex_rule`
  (the Standard Model's tree-level vertices; no H γ γ / H g g / H Z γ vertex — "draw the loop
  (preset h_to_gammagamma)"; flavour change only at a W, leptons within their family, quarks with
  the CKM element; four fermions → "draw the W"), `check_vertex` (Q, B, L_e/μ/τ with Step 237's
  `check`, the vertex as a process with all lines off-shell), `colour_problem`, `fermion_chains`,
  `check_diagram` (+ the whole reaction and the hadron reaction), computed couplings (α, α_s, v, g,
  Yukawa), 12 presets (`PRESETS`, `preset_diagrams`).
- **Layout** `feynman_layout.layout`: time order from the legs (timelike / spacelike internal
  lines, loop vertices early / late), columns, barycentric y, every order of the ends tried for the
  fewest crossings (u-channel uncrossed), groups beside their spectators, bowed multi-edges.
- **Scene** `feynman` (`scenes/feynman.py`, `feynman_draw.py`, `feynman_actions.py`): notation
  (arrows, waves, coils, dashes, dots, labels with drawn bars, brackets), reaction line, time arrow
  (`time: right | up`), reveal in time order, targets `line:<id>`, `vertex:<id>`,
  `hadron:<particle>`, `process`, `diagram`, `time_axis`; `travel` (dots along lines on one clock),
  `vertex_rule` (ring + rule, coupling, checks beside / under the diagram), `swap_channel`
  (morph between a scene's diagrams; targets follow).

  `src/vidgen/scenes/{feynman,feynman_draw,feynman_actions}.py`, `tests/test_feynman.py` (79
  incl. 3 renders), `docs/gallery/feynman.md` + `media/feynman-{16x9,9x16}.{png,gif}`.

`diagram_layout`. No dependency, no config key.

Decisions
- A line names the particle that travels forward in time (an incoming positron is `e+ in -> v1`);
  the arrow is derived from the fermion number, so the author never draws arrows by hand and an
  antifermion's arrow always points against time.
- Vertex rules are written on the lines read as all outgoing (crossing symmetry), so one table
  serves absorption, emission, annihilation and pair creation; conservation reuses `check` with
  every line off-shell (no energy check at a vertex).
- The u-channel is drawn uncrossed with the outgoing legs swapped (the same diagram); the brief's
  "no crossings for tree diagrams" holds for every preset (tested) and a custom diagram that still
  crosses gets a warning.
- Internal lines are labelled as written (`γ`, not `γ*`, unless the author writes `gamma*`);
  presets use `γ*` in Drell–Yan and `Z*` in H → ZZ*.
- The vertex-rule text takes a column on the right in 16:9 (only when the scene uses
  `vertex_rule`), a band at the bottom in 9:16; the diagram keeps the rest of the frame.
- In 9:16 with time left → right the diagram may grow to 1.15 × its width tall (the frame is
  narrow); `time: up` is the alternative for tall frames.
- The gallery sample is the guide's first `feynman` snippet (Bhabha with `vertex_rule`,
  `swap_channel`, `travel`).

Compatibility: Phase Q baseline 31 frames, max difference 0 (`phase-q-baseline/check238`).
Existing scenes untouched (the two import changes are refactors). Gallery 14.1 MB of 15 (the entry
about 0.16 MB: GIFs 76 KB and 70 KB).

Values: couplings computed from constants (α), PDG 2024 (α_s(m_Z) = 0.1180, G_F = 1.1663788 ×
10⁻⁵ GeV⁻², the masses of Step 237). **For the owner to check**: sin²θ_W ≈ 0.231 (shown with three
figures; the stored 0.2313 is my memory of the PDG 2024 MS-bar value) and the CKM magnitudes
(two figures: |V_ud| 0.97, |V_us| 0.22, |V_ub| 0.004, |V_cd| 0.22, |V_cs| 0.97, |V_cb| 0.04,
|V_td| 0.009, |V_ts| 0.04, |V_tb| 1.0); both marked `# check` in `feynman.py`.

Known gaps: two-loop and box diagrams are not laid out (one loop: triangles and bubbles); colour
flow is checked, not drawn; the vertex-rule text is English only; with `reveal: time` and few
beats, a diagram's last lines may be drawn in the beat after (steps spread over the beats) — a
`swap_channel` early in that beat then morphs a diagram not yet complete (use `reveal: all` or

## Step 241 — Collisions, decays and data

What was built (DESIGN §99.10 review note, §99.11–§99.12): simulated collision data and what is
read from it as two model modules (`particle_physics.spectrum`, `particle_physics.branching`, no
manim), four scene types (`mass_spectrum`, `decay_chain`, `branching`, `branching_pie`), three
plot models and a few additive `plot` features.

First, the review of Step 240's stills:
- Display presets draw the boson mass from a Breit–Wigner truncated to M ± Γ
  (`detector.DISPLAY_WIDTHS` = 1, was ±3Γ), still one seeded uniform: `z_to_mumu` seed 3 now gives
  m(μμ) = 89.0 GeV (was 85.9); a test checks 20 seeds within Γ_Z.
- 16:9 detector about 15 % larger (circle 60 → 69 % of the frame height): the label column writes
  the field on two lines, the side columns stand 0.6 × GAP from the drawing. Gallery entry

  times and the Z line shape are plot models; `decay_chain` is its own picture.
- Readout significance = Asimov with the *expected* window shares (the sample's own shares were 0
  for few events); the fit note = likelihood ratio; both "local", the p-value explained as the
  chance that background alone fluctuates this high.
- Fits start from the expected mass / width and the background-only polynomial (the generic peak
  guess latched on the curvature of an exponential background; 14 of 20 γγ fits failed before).
- Z fitted with a Breit–Wigner: its Γ includes the resolution (caption and docs say so); no Voigt.
- 9:16: when all boxes went above the plot it kept a fifth of the frame; a fixed headroom (2× the
  highest bin), no legend and one combined box inside the plot keep it large.
- With a `fit` action and no `annotate` of the note, the note follows the fit (the plot's own step
  would grow the data to the end before the fit).
- Gallery budget 15 → 16.5 MB (recorded in `tests/test_gallery.py` and DESIGN §99.12): the four
  entries take 0.74 MB (gallery 15.4 MB); room left for Step 243's showcase.

(`story-qeh/`); nothing of them is in the repo.

What was done
- **Adaptation and gap analysis** (private): the script with a shot list (narration and dialogue
  per speaker, camera, staging, light, sounds, music) and the gap list per shot; a test render of
  an iso lab. Generic summary and the phase plan: DESIGN §100.1, tasklist Phase Z (Steps
  245–248).
- **Voice effects** (DESIGN §100.2): `effect:` on `voice:` / `voices:` — `deep`, `high`, `robot`,
  `radio`, `chorus`, `echo`, `hall`, `otherworldly`, a list, or `{use, pitch, amount}`; any
  provider, applied after synthesis with ffmpeg (`EffectProvider` wraps the provider); in the
  hash only when set; not inherited by named voices; each preset about as loud as the dry voice
  (measured); `echo` / `hall` / `chorus` add a 0.35 / 0.9 / 0.1 s tail.
- **Hologram characters** (§100.3): `hologram: true | {color, opacity}` on a character —
  colours mapped through the hologram colour by lightness, translucent fills, bright edges, never
  graded by the stage's light or soft shading; character PNGs and sheets show it.
- **Portals** (§100.4): the `portal` prop (new `SCIFI_PROPS`), switched like a lamp: opens from a
  crack into a crackling, swirling, pulsing oval with sparks and an unlit glow; seals back to a
  seam; whoosh + rumble / swoosh + thud; no shadow (`FLOATING_IN_PLACE`); stands at a spot of an
  iso place (`ISO_ITEMS`), and `enter` / `exit` with `door:` its spot step through it.

## Step 246 — Story-cartoon features: framing, alarms, labs, holograms, visitors, memories

The rest of Phase Z's gap list, plus a reviewer's notes on the 245 test stills (the room filled
~60 % of the frame; close-ups cropped badly; the visitor did not read tall or iridescent; the
alarm was a salmon tint; the lab looked like a living room). All generic, opt-in, neutral
samples; the private story project stays in the scratchpad.

What was built (DESIGN §100.6–§100.14)
- **Framing**: `iso: {wide: fill}` (or 1–2.5) — a room's wide view fills the frame (~80 % instead
  of ~60 %); `closeup` / `medium` of 2–3 characters (`shot: closeup ana ben`: all faces, headroom
  over the highest head, centred); `shot: {..., clear: true}` hides the characters the shot does
  not frame for its beat (no legs poking in). Tall visitors: `scale: 1.4–1.5` (works already).
- **Alarm and shutters**: `- alarm: start | stop` (`color`, `period`): a dark room under a red
  light pulsing like a beacon (a new `StageLight.alarms` grade over the light), a two-tone siren
  bed while it runs; unlit things (portal, holograms, screens) keep shining. `- shutters: close
  | open` on an indoor iso place's windows (`iso.shutters: true` starts them down), with a slam.
- **Holograms**: `materialise` / `dematerialise` actions (a flickering wireframe, then solid; the
  character waits unseen until its first materialise); holograms flicker now and then
  (`hologram.flicker`, default on). One `FigureAlpha` per character holds every opacity factor.
- **Visitors**: `iridescent: true | {seconds, strength}` (oil-on-water hue bands drifting up the
  figure) and `afterimages: true | {spacing, life, opacity}` (fading copies while it moves).
- **Hand in hand**: `- {hold_hands: ana, with: ben}` / `- let_go_hands: ana`; the hands meet
  every frame, standing or walking side by side; lint lets the pair stand close.
- **Lab and memory objects**: iso `console` (glowing screens), `server_rack` (blinking lights),
  `projector_pad`, `whiteboard`, `flower_arch`, `chess_table`; the `hologram_display` prop
  (`pattern: fractal | data | text`, grows out of its beam, a hum and a chime); a portal's
  `view: coast | stars | meadow`; portals and displays cannot be picked up.
- **Flashback**: `flashback: true | {...}` on a stage: faded warm colours (`LightGrade.saturation`,
  new) and a soft vignette over the camera's view.
- **Sounds**: `alarm`, `crackle`, `hum`, `drone`, `slam` (procedural, numpy); beds `hum` (named:
  `ambience: hum`) and `alarm`. The Listen page (`docs/music`) regenerated: a `sfx-story` row, the
  two beds in the ambience clip (6.6 MB; its budget test 6.5 → 6.8 MB).
- **Gallery**: showcase `iso_lab` ("The night shift": a hologram materialises on a pad, screens,
  blinking racks, shutters, a rift with a starry sky); 16.1 of 16.5 MB. The alarm itself is left
  out of it: its pulsing doubled the GIFs past `CLIP_MAX_BYTES`.

Decisions

## Step 247 — The story video, light on the characters, hands that show

A private story project (an isometric cartoon, narrator + five character voices) was built,
previewed and rendered in the scratchpad (`story-qeh/proj`, never committed). The reviewer's
notes on the 246 test cut (night faces dark, darker skin especially; the visitors not reading
tall and their iridescence muted; held hands not visible, one character in front of the other)
led to three generic fixes, all opt-in or on features new in 246 (DESIGN §100.15).

What was built
- **`fill_light`** (stage param 0–1, default 0): a soft light on the characters alone —
  `lighting.lifted(grade, share)` (a grade moved back towards the colours as drawn), applied by
  `StageLight._grade_of` to members marked with `shading.mark_light_lift` (after a lamp's light;
  cached per grade and share). `StoryStaging._fill_lights` marks each non-hologram character.
- **`iridescent.glow`** (0–1, default 0.5): an iridescent visitor shines partly by its own
  light (the same lift), so its colours stay vivid at night or under an alarm.
- **Hands that show** (`HandHold._keep_close`): two holding hands further apart than their arms
  reach step in across the picture until the hands meet (never closer than 0.42 of the taller
  one's height at the feet); while both walk, the second keeps its place beside the first, so
  they go side by side (walks with the same `run_time`).
- **Tall visitors**: `scale` does apply on an iso place (checked in layout, shots, two-shots);
  1.45 next to a `tall` human read human-sized, so the docs now suggest 1.5–1.8 and a
  `two_shot` with a human (the story uses 1.75 / 1.7).

Files
- New: `tests/test_story_light_hands.py` (5).
- Changed: `cartoon/lighting.py` (`lifted`), `cartoon/shading.py` (`LIGHT_LIFT`,
  `mark_light_lift`, `StageLight._grade_of` / `_lifted`), `cartoon/figure_fx.py` (`HandHold`:
  `_keep_close`, `HAND_REACH`, `HAND_MIN_GAP`, `HAND_MIN_APART`), `config.py`
  (`IridescentConfig.glow`), `scenes/stage.py` (`fill_light`, `_fill_lights` call),
  `scenes/stage_story.py` (`_fill_lights`), `api.py` (`lifted`, `mark_light_lift`); docs CONFIG
  (stage table, Light and shadows, Iridescent skins, Holding hands), guide (copied to
  `AGENTS.md`), CHANGELOG, DESIGN §100.15, tasklist.

Public interfaces: `vidgen.api` adds `lifted`, `mark_light_lift`. Config: stage `fill_light`;
`characters[].iridescent.glow`.

Decisions
- A fill light as a lift of the stage's grade per character (the lamp mechanism), not a light
  source in the scene: it follows every light change, alarm pulse and flash, and costs one
  cached grade per (grade, share).
- Iridescent `glow` defaults to 0.5 (not 0): new in 246, no committed render shows it.
- Holding hands moves the figures across the picture only; the iso cells, draw order and
  `iso_feet` stay the walks' (neighbouring cells side by side are 1.7 tiles apart, far more than
  arms reach).

The story video (private, scratchpad)
- 16 scenes (title, 13 iso stage scenes — the lab at night, four flashback memory vignettes —,
  end card), 54 beats; Kokoro: narrator `bm_fable` 1.0, heroine `af_heart` 0.95, hero
  `am_michael` 0.95, the lab AI `af_nicole` 1.2 + `echo`, the visitor `am_onyx` 0.9 +
  `otherworldly`, the building's voice `am_echo` + `{robot, pitch -5}`; music `enigma`, `lullaby`,
  `calm` at −4/−5 dB; sounds (alarm bed, slams, crackle, drone, riser, chime, whoosh, typing).
- Final 16:9 1080p30: 7:12 (432.1 s), 96.6 MB, −16.4 LUFS integrated, true peak −1.9 dBTP.
  Median pitch of one line each: narrator 126 Hz, heroine 191, hero 129 (another accent), AI
  154 (with echo), visitor 80 (deep, chorus, hall), building 140 (a flat buzz); speech levels
  within 2 dB except the robot (+5 dB, one line).
- Render: scenes at 1080p take 5–18× real time (the alarm scenes the most: every frame regraded);
  peak RSS 1.1–1.4 GB per process (two scenes in parallel under the 3 GB cap). A long scene would
  pass the 10-minute tool limit, so the three longest were split in two (beats keep their ids,
  so their audio is reused) and rendered with `storyboard --final --scene ... --jobs 2`; then
  `vidgen render` joined them (447 s, mostly the music and the mix). Kokoro TTS: 54 beats in
  205 s, peak 2.8 GB.
- Lint: 0 errors, 17 warnings (narration speed of a few short or slow lines, a rushed entrance,
  facing while a character looks at a display, the heroine and her memory self look alike — on
  purpose, and walk overlaps where four characters step into a portal and fade out).
- 9:16 not made: the iso wides keep every character in view and show the room small in a tall
  frame; close-ups read well, but a vertical cut would need its own staging.

Checks
- Tests (one file at a time or two): test_story_light_hands 5, test_story_fx 20 (2 renders),
  test_cartoon_lighting + test_config + test_api 39, test_schema 71, test_docs + test_guide 163,

- Phase Q baseline 31/31 identical (`phase-q-baseline/check247`).

Known gaps / for 248
- A `zoom` with `until` across a beat that has its own `shot` moves the camera back during that
  shot (and a later beat without a shot returns to the zoomed view); the story uses `until` the
  next beat only. Worth a lint warning or a fix.
- `render` of a long project renders every stale scene in one call; scenes over ~60 s of video
  at 1080p with many characters pass a 10-minute run (split scenes, or a resumable render).
- Kokoro reads a few short lines fast (whisper / excited) and the AI slow; the robot voice is
  louder than the others.

## Step 248 — Review of Phase Z: zoom and shots, level-matched effects, renders in steps

A critical review of the private story video (every shot at 1080p, speech levels per voice, the
mix) and of the issues Step 247 left. Generic fixes in vidgen (DESIGN §100.16); the story
project itself (scratchpad, never committed) was fixed and rendered again.

What was built
- **A shot inside a zoom's `until`** (`Zoom.revert` in `scenes/actions.py`): the shot holds for
  its beat, the next beat without a shot returns to the zoomed view, and the zoom ends at its
  `until` beat; before, the camera pulled back during the shot and later returned to the zoom.
  The zoom remembers the shot on screen when it starts; a zoom started inside a shot is undone
  as before.
- **Level-matched voice effects** (`tts/effects.py`: `level_match`, `with_effect`): the effect's
  audio is brought to the dry voice's integrated loudness (within ±`MATCH_LIMIT` 15 dB), then
  limited. The effect spec gains `level: matched` (voices with an effect are voiced again once).
- **`vidgen render --max-scenes N`** (pipeline `render_project(max_scenes=)`, CLI, MCP
  `render.max_scenes`): renders at most N of the scenes to render and stops without joining
  while more are left (a `VidgenError` naming them, `details.rendered` / `remaining`); the next
  run goes on. Docs: README, CONFIG (`--json` error details), the guide (copied to `AGENTS.md`).
- **`tests/test_actions.py`**: one `BUILTIN_ACTIONS` list for the three tests that listed the
  built-in actions by hand (failing since Phase X); the reversible actions come from the registry.

Files
- Changed: `src/vidgen/scenes/actions.py`, `src/vidgen/tts/effects.py`, `src/vidgen/voice_effects.py`
  (`MATCH_LIMIT`, spec), `src/vidgen/render/pipeline.py`, `src/vidgen/cli.py`,
  `src/vidgen/mcp_server.py`, guide + `AGENTS.md`, README, `docs/CONFIG.md` (voice effects,
  shots, render JSON), CHANGELOG, DESIGN §100.16, tasklist; tests `test_cartoon_shots.py` (+1
  render), `test_voice_effects.py` (+1), `test_render.py` (+1 render), `test_actions.py`.

Public interfaces: CLI `render --max-scenes N`; MCP `render(max_scenes=)`;
`render_project(..., max_scenes=None)`; `vidgen.tts.effects.level_match`;
`vidgen.voice_effects.MATCH_LIMIT`. Behaviour: a zoom over a shot (above); effect loudness.

Decisions
- Resuming inside one scene was not built: manim would have to replay the scene's state up to a
  beat, and skipped animations do not reproduce it exactly (updaters get one step). A scene
  longer than a time limit is still split in two (beat ids keep their audio); a project of many
  scenes renders in steps with `--max-scenes`.
- `test_actions.py` keeps an explicit list for the registry check (a guard that new actions are
  meant), and builds the message / enum expectations from it.

The story video (private, scratchpad) — what the review found and changed
- Fidelity: every beat of the story in order, names right (both doctors, the sister, the
  student, the father, the visitors, the coast; the time and date line). No change needed.
- Shots: key beats moved from tiny wides to closer framings (the AI materialising: a zoom on the
  three; the hand found hers: a medium with the hands; the triumph: a two-shot; the visitors
  stepping out: a zoom on the rift; the choice offered: a medium of the visitor and the pair; the
  pair stepping through: a zoom on the rift with the visitors following); a two-face close-up
  for a line said to the other; the student memory restaged (the student no longer cut by the
  frame); the wedding memory's flashback lighter so the blue dress reads; warmer expressions
  on the romantic and compassionate lines; the coast through the rift larger.
- Title card in the story's night colours (it was a bright blue burst); end card line brighter.
- Audio: speech outliers evened with an emotion's `gain` (two whispers were 8.5 dB under the
  narrator, an excited line 3.8 over; a few narrator / hero lines +2–3); the robot voice +5 →
  +0.4 dB by the generic fix; per-voice medians now within 2 dB of the narrator; music alone
  about −27/−28 LUFS against speech about −16; a quieter drone.
- Renders: 1080p scenes at 6–18× real time, rendered with `render --frames --jobs 2
  --max-scenes 2..4` in seven runs under 10 minutes each, then joined (the join under a minute
  this time). Final 16:9 1080p30: 7:12 (432.1 s), 98.9 MB, −16.3 LUFS, true peak −1.9 dBTP.
  Delivery copy: H.264 720p two-pass `-preset slow -tune animation` 365 kb/s + AAC 128 kb/s,
  27.3 MB (1080p at the same size showed blocks in the dark gradients; 720p looked cleaner).

## Step 249 — Shorts from a longer video: cuts, hooks, the Shorts safe area

Phase Z2 (Steps 249–250) cuts vertical Shorts out of a private story video. This step built the
generic support (DESIGN §101) and Shorts 1–3 of the story (scratchpad, never committed).

What existed: variants (lists replace, so a variant had to repeat the whole `scenes`), karaoke
captions (word-synced), shots / zooms, `reframe`, cards, `render --max-scenes`.

What was built
- **`cut:`** (`src/vidgen/cuts.py`, `apply_cut` on the raw config in `Project._load`, before sets
  and validation; base config and variants): `scenes` (an id, or `{scene, beats: [ids] | {from,
  to}, ...changes}`; a scene twice under another `id`), `beats` (changes by beat id: mappings
  merge, lists replace), `hook` (adds the `hook` overlay), `end_card` (a silent `end_card` or
  `card` scene `cut_end`). Beat ids are written out first, so a cut reuses the full video's
  audio. Scene `params` merge like a set's (characters / props / layers by name). The first
  scene's transition is dropped unless the entry gives one. Errors at `cut...`.
- **`hook` overlay** (`scenes/overlays.py`): big bold text on a `primary` plate near the top,
  `at` / `seconds` (default 0 / 3), pops in, fades out.
- **`shorts:`** (`true | {max_seconds, bottom, right, top, left}`; defaults 60 s, 20 %, 15 %):
  `overlays.shorts_area`; captions (no lift), lower thirds, the hook, every scene's safe area and
  the `card`'s words keep out of the app's parts; the layout dump header gets `shorts` (px);
  lint `shorts_safe_area` (text / a face in the covered parts, an overlay over a face) and
  `shorts_length` (error; on the last scene, planned length); validate warns (not vertical, too
  long). Unused voices are not warned about in a cut.
- **`zoom` `hold: true`**: no zoom-out after the beat (avoids a flash of the wide view before a
  cut or at a scene's end).
- **`audio.bitrate`** (128k–320k, default 192k): FFmpeg's AAC at 192k pushed the −14 LUFS
  Short's true peak from −1.9 (mix WAV) to +1.9 dBTP; 256k: −1.6.

Files
- New: `src/vidgen/cuts.py`, `src/vidgen/lint/shorts_rule.py`, `tests/test_cuts_shorts.py` (18, 1 render).
- Changed: `config.py` (`CutConfig`, `CutScene`, `CutBeatRange`, `CutEndCard`, `ShortsConfig`,
  `VideoConfig.cut/shorts/shorts_zones`, `AudioConfig.bitrate`, `ShortsSafeAreaRule`,
  `ShortsLengthRule`, `LINT_RULES`), `project.py`, `overlays.py` (`shorts_area`),
  `scenes/overlays.py` (`Hook`; lower third in a Short), `scenes/captions.py`, `scenes/card.py`,
  `scene.py` (safe area), `scenes/actions.py` (`hold`), `introspect.py`, `lint/{__init__,rules,run}.py`,
  `render/{ffmpeg,pipeline}.py`, `voices.py`, `cli.py` (validate warnings), `api.py`; tests
  `test_overlays.py` (overlay list), `test_particle_lint.py` (rule order); docs CONFIG (top level,
  Variants → "Cuts and Shorts", `hook`, captions / lower third placement, zoom `hold`,
  `audio.bitrate`, lint rules), guide (social topic, actions table, lint table; copied to
  `AGENTS.md`), README, CHANGELOG, DESIGN §101, tasklist (Phase Z2).

Public interfaces: `vidgen.api` adds `apply_cut`, `shorts_area`. Config: `cut`, `shorts`,
`audio.bitrate`, overlay `hook`, zoom `hold`, lint rules `shorts_safe_area`, `shorts_length`.

Decisions
- Cuts rewrite the raw config (no new pipeline stage); left-out beats are not "fast-forwarded"
  (manim cannot replay a scene's state exactly, §100.16): a cut states where characters start.
- `shorts` is a property of the output, separate from `cut` (a Short need not be a cut).
- The bitrate is opt-in (default unchanged): existing projects' audio is identical.

The story's Shorts (private, scratchpad `story-qeh/`)
- Variants `short1`–`short3` in `story-qeh/proj/video.yaml` (1080×1920, `shorts: true`,
  `audio: {target_lufs: -14, bitrate: 256k}`, music `enigma` −5 dB, karaoke captions with
  `speakers: color, max_lines: 1`, hooks, end card "Full story on the channel" under the title in
  the story's card colours). Re-staged in `cut.beats`: zooms ×1.5–2 of the 16:9 ones with
  `hold`, closeups / mediums of one to three characters, a zoom centred on the pair so their
  hands show above the captions, two long scenes split in two cut entries (each renders in one
  run; the second starts with the characters where the first left them).
- Results (`story-qeh/shorts/short1_*.mp4` … `short3_*.mp4`): Short 1 43.6 s, 6.3 MB, −14.5 LUFS,
  −1.6 dBTP; Short 2 39.0 s, 10.5 MB, −14.9 LUFS, −1.7 dBTP; Short 3 47.7 s, 9.5 MB, −14.8 LUFS,
  −1.8 dBTP. Contact sheets `story-qeh/shorts/shortN_contact.png` (the hook at
  1 s, one frame per beat, the end card). Lint (preview): short1 2 narration-speed warnings
  (from the film), short2 clean, short3 one `facing_away` (the visitor speaks to the pair out of
  the frame, on purpose).
- Render times at 1080×1920: 6–18× real time (the alarm scenes 23×: 15 s in 347 s), two scenes in
  parallel with `render --variant shortN --jobs 2 --max-scenes 2`, then the rest and the join.

Checks
- Tests (one or two files at a time): test_cuts_shorts 18 (1 render), test_docs + test_guide 164,
  test_schema + test_config + test_api 102, test_schema 71 (again after `bitrate`), test_project +
  test_voices 41, test_overlays + test_captions 46, test_lint + test_iso_diagram_actions +
  test_particle_lint 170, test_cartoon_lint + test_timing_lint 148, genetics / accuracy / calc /
  orbit / narration lint 146, test_music_pieces + test_actions + test_introspect 44,
  test_cartoon_shots + test_introspect 30, test_json_output + test_mcp 39, test_cli 10,
  test_cartoon_cards + test_scene 52 (with test_cuts_shorts), test_render + test_robustness 48 —
  all passing.
- Phase Q baseline 31/31 identical (`phase-q-baseline/check249`, run twice).

Known gaps / for Step 250
- `off_stage` reports the characters of a beat's `shot` when a `zoom` in the same beat moves
  the camera away from them (avoid: two `hold` zooms instead of a shot plus a zoom).
- A zoom `at: 0` in a scene's first beat still shows the wide view for about the first second
  (the hook frame shows the establishing wide; fine, but check if a Short should open close).
- In portrait a two-character `closeup` frames about like a `medium` (the narrow width needs
  both bodies); use a `zoom` for a tighter face shot.
- Scene renders of a variant are redone after code changes (no reuse across vidgen versions).
- Hook text over 3 lines (short2) reads, but shorter hooks look better.

## Step 250 — Shorts review fixes; Shorts 4–7

Phase Z2's second step: fixes from a review of the first three Shorts (generic, DESIGN §101.4),
then the remaining Shorts of a private story project (scratchpad only, never committed).

What was built (generic)
- Karaoke captions in a Short: a phrase of about 3–5 words on one line (`SHORTS_KARAOKE`:
  `size: body`, `max_lines: 1`, `max_words: 5` when not given), a small margin (`lift` 0.03)
  above the app's area. The "low caption" reported in one beat was in fact at the same place as
  the others (plate bottom on the 80 % line, measured on the video); the margin makes it clear.
- Lint `shorts_safe_area`: faces are checked against an overlay's `reach` (captions: every
  caption of the line being spoken; a still shows only one, which is why a longer caption over a
  face was missed), also on mid-beat stills (`Rule.mid_beat`; lint renders 3 stills per beat in a
  Short), and `min_cover` (0.1) for an overlay over a face (0.25 was too lax for a chin + mouth).
- `zoom` `cut: true`: jump to the view; at `at: 0` of a scene's first beat the scene opens on it
  (`Action.opens_scene`, applied before the set's entrance) — the hook is no longer over the
  establishing wide view for the first second.
- A cut's params entry `{name: x, drop: true}` leaves a character / prop / layer out.
- The hook shrinks (1.25 → 0.8 × title) when that keeps it on two lines.

Files: `scenes/captions.py`, `scenes/overlays.py` (hook), `scenes/actions.py` (zoom `cut`),
`actions.py` (`opens_scene`, `start_beat`), `cuts.py` (`drop`), `introspect.py` (`reach`),
`lint/rules.py` (`mid_beat`), `lint/run.py` (`SHORTS_STILLS`, `_stills_current`),
`lint/shorts_rule.py`, `config.py` (`min_cover`); tests `test_cuts_shorts.py` (+7: reach,
min_cover, karaoke defaults and phrase lengths, `_mark_reach`, drop, cut zoom opens framed
(render, with / without), hook on 2 lines and 3 stills per beat in the render test); CONFIG
(Cuts and Shorts, captions table, hook `size`, zoom row, lint row and settings), guide (+
`AGENTS.md`), CHANGELOG, DESIGN §101.4, tasklist.

Public interfaces: `Action.opens_scene()`; `rule(..., mid_beat=)` / `Rule.mid_beat`; config zoom
`cut`, `lint.rules.shorts_safe_area.min_cover`, cut params `drop`; layout dump `reach` (Shorts).

Decisions
- Shorts-only defaults, so other videos (and the Phase Q baseline) are unchanged.
- A first-beat `shot:` still starts after the stage's entrance (changing it would move existing
  frames); Shorts use `zoom ... cut: true` for the opening view.
- Lint's caption check is per line, not per frame: the reach is the union of the line's captions
  (conservative); the camera between stills is covered by the mid-beat stills.

The private story's Shorts (scratchpad `story-qeh/shorts/`; variants `short1`–`short7` in
`story-qeh/proj/video.yaml`; −14 LUFS target, 256k AAC; contact sheets `shortN_contact.png`
with the first frame, the hook at 1 s, two frames per beat and the end card):
- 1 43.6 s 6.1 MB −14.5 LUFS −1.6 dBTP; 2 39.0 s 11.0 MB −14.9 / −1.7; 3 47.7 s 9.5 MB
  −14.8 / −1.8; 4 35.9 s 5.4 MB −14.5 / −1.8; 5 46.9 s 10.9 MB −14.7 / −1.4; 6 36.4 s 9.8 MB
  −14.7 / −1.8; 7 (teaser) 16.4 s 4.3 MB −15.0 / −1.8.
- Every scene opens framed (zoom `cut`), hooks shortened to 2–3 lines, characters who would
  stand at the frame's edge under the captions dropped from that cut (`drop`).
- Render times at 1080×1920: 6–32× real time (two scenes in parallel); each render command under
  10 minutes with `--max-scenes`.
- Lint (preview, 3 stills per beat): remaining warnings are a sliver of a face at a frame edge
  (one beat each in Shorts 2 and 3, Short 6's visitors walking into the portal),
  narration speed (from the film), `walk_overlap` (all exit through one door, as in the film),
  `look_alike` (a character and its younger self), `facing_away` (as in Step 249).
- Intermediates (build dirs of the Shorts, joined copies in `proj/output/`) deleted.

Checks: test_cuts_shorts 23 (3 render), test_schema 71, test_docs + test_guide + test_config +
test_api 195, test_captions + test_overlays 46, test_actions + test_introspect +
test_cartoon_shots 58, test_lint + test_particle_lint + test_timing_lint 163, test_cartoon_lint

test_callout_action 73 — all passing. Phase Q baseline 31/31 identical (run twice).

Known gaps
- Hook text still wraps at ~12 characters per line at 1.25 × title in a Short (the clear part is

- A first-beat `shot:` shows the wide view during the entrance (use a `zoom ... cut`).
- A caption's reach is per line; a narrow caption never over a face can still be reported when a
